前言 Preface

为什么学习编程语言？ Why Study Programming Languages?

开始学习一门课程时，先问问为什么要学，总是有益的。那么，让我们列出几个理由，说明这门课为何值得学习： It is always healthy to begin a course of study by asking why we should engage in it. So let us list a few reasons to justify this one:

  • 编程语言是人类发明的最美妙、最强大的事物之一。 Programming languages are some of the most beautiful and powerful objects invented by human beings.
  • 它们让我们——确切地说，迫使我们——精确地表达思想，作为回报，我们得以指挥能力强大的机器执行我们的意愿。 They let us—indeed, force us to—capture our thoughts precisely, and in return command machines of immense power to do our bidding.
  • 对程序员来说，它们是终极的人机界面。 To a programmer, they are the ultimate human-computer interface.
  • 它们在产业界十分重要：重要到大公司会创造新语言，或将现有语言纳入自己的阵营，以建立或扩大市场份额。 They are industrially important: so important that major companies create new languages or co-opt existing ones to establish or expand their market share.
  • 它们体现了一种新的知识形式：《计算机程序的构造和解释》将其称为“过程性认识论”。 They embody a new form of knowledge: what Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs  called a “procedural epistemology”.
  • 它们让我们能够证明关于表达手段和表达极限的强有力论断。还有多少种其他语言能让我们做到其中任何一点呢？ They enable us to prove powerful statements about the means and limits of our expression. How many other languages let us do either?

还需要多少理由呢？ How many more reasons does one need?

目标读者 The Target Audience

从第一版开始，本书的目标读者就是“另外的 90%”。也就是说，我猜想，编程语言课上大约有 10% 的学生与教师一样：他们对这门学科满怀热情，有强烈的学习动力，在个人层面认同它，并且可能希望继续深入研究。他们是出色的学生，其中许多人将成为下一代教师。有几本很棒的书正是为这种学生设计的——或者至少最适合他们。 Starting with the first edition, this book’s target has been “the other 90%”. That is, I conjecture that roughly 10% of students in a programming languages class are like the educator: they are deeply excited about and motivated to learn the subject, identify with it personally, and may want to continue to study it further. These are wonderful students, and many of them will go on to become the next generation of educators. There are several terrific books that are designed—or at least, work best—for this kind of student.

但大多数学生——比如说 90%——可能没有这种深切的个人认同。相反，他们希望把这门学科学到足以成为更好的计算机科学家。他们需要学什么，又需要怎样学习呢？他们就是本书的目标读者。一方面，本书努力与许多编程任务建立联系。与此同时，一味迎合这样的读者又太容易了。本书试图在这些联系与对基本原理的关注之间取得平衡，让学习者在很长时间内都能从这些原理中受益。 But most of them—say 90%—may not have this deep personal identification. Instead, they want to learn the subject enough to become better computer scientists. What do they  need to learn, and how do they need to learn it? They are the target audience for this book. On the one hand, the book tries to connect to many programming tasks. At the same time, it’s too easy to pander to such an audience. The book tries to balance these connections with a focus on principles that will stand the learner in good stead for a long time.

当然，我相信那 10% 的学生也会从本书中学到有用的东西。至少，他们或许能学到看待这门学科的另一种视角，也可能对与自己不同的学习者多一些共情。再不济，使用过本书早期版本的学生中，有远不止十几位顺利获得了编程语言方向的博士学位，其中几位如今也已成为教授。所以，至少本书没有害了他们。这样的胜算，我可以接受。 Of course, I believe the 10% will learn something useful from this book, too. If nothing else, they may learn a different perspective  on the subject, and maybe also develop some empathy for learners not like themselves. If nothing else, well over a dozen students who used earlier editions of this book successfully completed PhDs in programming languages, and several are themselves professors now. So, at least, the book has not harmed them. I can live with those odds.

我写这本书时也考虑了在职程序员。他们中许多人可能未受过正规的计算机科学教育，或者至少没在所受教育中得到对编程语言的恰当介绍。在某个时候，他们中的一些人会像那 90% 的学生一样，对自己使用的媒介产生好奇。我希望本书能与他们对话，温和地引导他们离开日常编程的喧嚣，进入一个反省与思考的空间。 I have also written this book with working programmers in mind. Many of them may have not had a formal computer science education, or at least one that included a proper introduction to programming languages. At some point, like that 90% of students, some of them become curious about the media they use. I want this book to speak to them, gently drawing them away from the hustle and bustle of daily programming into a space of reflection and thought.

为什么要有第三版 Why a Third Edition

过去几年里，我的研究有很大一部分是在考察学生如何在许多不同层面理解编程语言。我的发现使我确信，我们需要一种新的方法来教授这些内容。这一版就是朝着这个目标迈出的第一轮尝试。（这也是用我如今的“口吻”重写文字的机会；二十多年来，我的口吻已发生了很大变化。这一版与第一版几乎没有相同的文字，与第二版也只有部分相同。） Over the past several years, a significant part of my research  examines how students understand programming languages at many different levels. What I have learned has convinced me that we need a new approach to teaching this material. This edition is a first iteration to that end. (It was also a chance to rewrite the prose in my current “voice”, which has evolved a lot over two decades. Virtually no text is in common with the first edition, and only some with the second.)

我们所处的世界，其语言的多样性与新颖性也前所未有。似乎每隔几周，我就会听说有人在尝试某种新的语言实验。健壮而有趣的运行时系统随处可得——从 Erlang 的运行时、Java 虚拟机，到浏览器中的 JavaScript、Racket 的运行时，等等，种类繁多——让人们很容易得到一个“配套齐全”的可运行原型，把精力集中在创新上。这既影响着尝试学习新语言的人，也影响着尝试构建语言的人。 We also live in a world of unprecedented linguistic diversity and novelty. It seems like every few weeks I learn about someone trying some new linguistic experiment. The wide availability of robust and interesting run-time systems—as diverse as Erlang’s, the Java Virtual Machine, the browser’s JavaScript, Racket’s, and more—makes it easy to get a working prototype “with batteries” and focus on novelty. This affects both people trying to learn new languages and those trying to build them.

与此相关的是，第一版对编程语言采取了非常“古典”的视角，这受到我自身在该学科所受正规训练的影响。第二版开始脱离这种视角，但尚未完全摆脱。第三版则基本挣脱了这些束缚，更多地反映了当今的语言格局。能讲解“脚本编程”和“渐进类型”等主题而不把它们简化为口号和空话的书并不多；本书尝试用更严谨的方式来讲解它们。 Relatedly, the first edition took a very “classical” look at programming languages, shaped by my own formal training in the subject. The second edition started to migrate from it, but not entirely. The third edition has mostly broken free of those constraints, reflecting more of the current linguistic landscape. There are not many books that cover topics like “scripting” and “gradual typing” without reducing them to slogans and fluff; this book tries to cover them in more rigorous ways.

但这种多样性也提出了一个重要挑战：该如何认识它？在其他学科中，我们通过把新事物分解成已熟悉的组成元素来认识它们。共同之处提供了一个锚点，也是理解其新颖之处的出发点。对于编程语言，这些元素是什么呢？教学传统认为，“范式”是这样一种组织手段，但在我看来，它是某个时代留下的垂死遗产：那时，计算领域希望被视为一门“科学”，并觉得实现这一点的最佳方式，就是把事物放进贴着标签的盒子里。但编程语言是人造的实体，而非自然的实体，没有什么能阻止设计者自由混合不同盒子里的东西——事实上许多人已经这么做了。当几乎一切都是“多范式”的时候，我们该如何理解这个世界呢？ But all this diversity brings up the important challenge of how to approach it. In other disciplines, we approach new objects by decomposing them into familiar constituent elements. Their commonalities provide an anchor, and a point of departure for what makes them novel. What are those elements for programming languages? Pedagogic tradition holds that “paradigms” are one such organizational medium, but I find them a moribund legacy of a period when computing wanted to be viewed as a “science” and felt the best way to do this was to put things in labeled boxes. But programming languages are artificial, not natural, entities, and nothing prevents designers from freely mixing between the boxes—as indeed many have. When virtually everything is “multiparadigm”, how can we make sense out of the world?

组织我们的学习 Structuring Our Study

正如我在别处更详尽地论述过的，把编程语言看作特性的集合更有意义。特性就是构件。当然，一旦组合起来，语言更像化合物而非混合物：各个特性会以不易预测的方式相互作用。因此，理解各个特性及其组合，是认识一种语言的有用方法。 As I have argued in greater length elsewhere , it is more meaningful to think of programming languages as aggregates of features . The features are the building blocks. Of course, once combined, languages are more like compounds than like mixtures: the features interact in ways that may not be easy to predict. Understanding both the features and their compositions is then a valuable way to approach a language.

本书围绕一个核心思想展开：SMoL，即语言的标准模型（Standard Model of Languages）。它体现了许多广泛使用的编程语言的计算核心，从 C# 和 Java，到 JavaScript、Lua、Python 和 Ruby，再到 OCaml 和 Racket。敏锐的读者会发现，这种共性完全不理会“范式”的界线。相反，所有这些语言（以及许多其他语言）在很大程度上拥有共同的计算核心：安全的运行时系统、自动内存管理、急切求值、一等的词法作用域函数、一阶的可修改变量，以及一等的可修改结构。现代编程要求我们深入理解这些内容。例如，我认为，如果不理解 SMoL，你就无法理解带修改的并发、静态成员或所有权。 The book revolves around a central idea, SMoL , the Standard Model of Languages. This is the embodiment of the computational core of many of our widely-used programming languages, from C# and Java to JavaScript, Lua, Python, and Ruby to OCaml and Racket. The astute reader will notice that this commonality pays no respect to “paradigms”. Rather, all these languages (and many others), to a large extent, have a common computational core: safe runtime systems, automated memory management, eager evaluation, first-class lexically-scoped functions, first-order mutable variables, and first-class mutable structures. Contemporary programming demands a deep understanding of these. For instance, I believe you cannot make sense of concurrency with mutation, static members, or ownership, without understanding SMoL.

然而，由于语言是人造的，而编程又是一种几乎可以无限塑造的材料，即使是“标准”特性，在历史上也出现过变体。因此，在逐个学习特性的同时，我们也要研究每个特性内部的变化。为此，我们采用神秘语言方法：使用固定的语法，探索同一特性可能表现出的不同方式。我们希望借助对比案例的认知理论来改善学习效果。 However, because languages are artificial and programming is an almost infinitely malleable material, even “standard” features have historically seen variation. Therefore, while we progress across  features, we also want to study variation within  them. We do this by using the mystery language  approach: with a fixed syntax, we explore the different ways the same feature can behave. This hopes to build on the cognitive theory of contrasting cases  to improve learning .

当然，哪些内容属于 SMoL，需要作出判断：当某个特性没有广泛存在于大量不同语言中（例如静态类型），或者在不同语言之间差异过大（例如对象）时，我就认为它不再属于标准模型。但这不是价值判断：本书会较深入地探索 SMoL，然后把注意力转向几个“非标准”特性，它们不仅重要，而且优美迷人。 What goes in SMoL is, of course, a judgment call: when a feature isn’t present across a large number of diverse languages (like static types), or shows too much variation between languages (like objects), I argue that it’s no longer part of the standard  model. But it is not a value  judgment: in this book we explore SMoL in some depth,  then turn our attention to several non-“standard” features that are not only important but also beautiful and fascinating.

谈到实现，本书提供了另一个支柱：SImPl，即标准实现方案（Standard Implementation Plan）。其思想是，从抽象语法树的角度思考编程语言很有用；这种树适合用代数数据类型表示；而处理这种树的程序则是一个递归函数，其形式主要由类型的结构引导。这一层次的描述涵盖了两种标准的求值媒介：解释器和编译器。它也概括了类型检查器、类型推断、静态分析等的本质。因此，学生应当熟练掌握这种结构，以便在想要实现自己的语言实验时使用。 Turning to implementation, the book provides another pillar: SImPl , the Standard Implementation Plan. This is the idea that programming languages are usefully thought of in terms of an abstract syntax tree; this tree is represented well by an algebraic datatype; and a program that processes this tree is a recursive function that is largely guided by the structure of the type. This level of description encompasses both of the standard media for evaluation: interpreters and compilers. It also captures the essence of type-checkers, type inference, static analysis, and more. Thus, students should gain facility with this structure for when they want to implement their own language experiments.

学习装备 Equipment for Learning

虽然随着时间推移，所有材料可能都会纳入本书，但目前，本书属于一个更广泛的学习生态系统，即布朗大学的 CSCI 1730 课程。所有材料都可在以下网站获得（请找最新年份）： While over time all the material might be incorporated into this book, for now, the book is part of a broader learning ecosystem, which is the course CSCI 1730 at Brown University. All the materials are available from the following site (look for the latest year):

https://cs.brown.edu/courses/csci1730/

课程作业分成几条“线索”： The course’s work is divided into several “threads”:

  • SMoL 使用自动化辅导程序教学生学习 SMoL。 SMoL uses an automated tutor  to teach students SMoL.
  • ML 让学生逐一探究神秘语言。 ML makes students work through mystery languages .
  • Stacker 让学生借助一种新工具 Stacker 来思考程序求值，它提供了一台概念机器。读者会发现，在 Stacker 中运行 SMoL 程序并研究其行为极为有用。 Stacker makes students reflect on program evaluation using a novel tool, the Stacker , which provides a notional machine. Readers will find it extremely useful to run SMoL programs in the Stacker and study how they behave.
  • “实现”线索让学生构建可运行的实现。 The Implementation thread has student build working implementations.
  • “分析”线索要求学生将课堂所学与现实世界的语言情境联系起来。我尤其鼓励教师在自己的课堂中使用“分析”线索的作业。 The Analysis thread asks students to relate material they are learning in the class to real-world language contexts. I especially encourage educators to make use of the Analysis thread assignments in their classes.

本书大量使用 Racket。不过，这种说法太简单了。Racket 的力量来自它定义新语言的能力：这篇文章和这段短视频对此有更详细的讨论。确实，本书中有些程序用 Racket 编程语言（#lang racket）编写，但许多程序用一种专为本书理想化设计的语言（#lang plait）编写。此外，还有些部分定义了自己的语言：其中有多种 SMoL 语言，还有远不止十几种神秘语言。因此，虽然学习者必须对括号语法多一点耐心，但作为回报，他们将获得丰厚的学习体验。 This book makes heavy use of Racket . However, that is too simplistic. Racket’s power comes from its ability to define new languages: this article  and this brief video  discuss that in more detail. Indeed, some programs in this book are written in the Racket programming language ( #lang racket ), but many are in a language ideally designed for this book ( #lang plait ). In addition, other parts define their own languages: there are multiple SMoL languages and well over a dozen mystery languages. Thus, while the learner must demonstrate some forbearance for parenthetical syntax, in return they will be richly rewarded with learning experiences.

从某种意义上说，#lang 的存在推动了本书的重新设计。我曾参与这个特性的设计，这让我格外不自在：面向广泛读者的材料，不应围绕与自己感情过深的工作展开。这也是为什么第一版使用了 Racket 的前身，而第二版没有使用。然而，在这个过程中，我意识到自己剥夺了学生大量的学习机会：毕竟，还有什么能比一种专为设计语言而设计的语言，更适合用来研究语言呢？例如，神秘语言的最初版本既零散又令人困惑；把它们重新实现为一组 Racket #lang 语言之后，它们变得简单清晰得多（也能让它们自身成为直接研究的对象）。因此，这一版加倍（甚至不止加倍）使用 Racket。要把它用好可能有些棘手（例如，要避免模式混淆），也许需要几轮尝试，但这番努力非常值得。 The existence of #lang , in some ways, drove this book’s redesign. I had some hand in that feature’s design , which made me acutely self-conscious: materials intended to be for a broad audience shouldn’t be about work too close to my heart. That was one of the reasons that, while the first edition used a predecessor of Racket, the second edition did not. In the process, however, I realized that I was depriving my students of numerous learning opportunities: after all, what better medium for the study of languages than a language designed for designing languages? For instance, the first version of the mystery languages were ad hoc and confusing; reimplementing them as a collection of Racket #lang s made them far simpler and clearer (and also open them up to be an object of direct study themselves). Thus, this edition doubles down (and then some) on the use of Racket. Getting it right can be tricky (e.g., avoiding mode confusion) and may take a few iterations, but it’s well worth the effort.

••••• 学习 SMoL ••••• ••••• Learning SMoL  •••••

我们先来学习语言的标准模型，它是随后大部分学习内容的基础。 We begin by learning the Standard Model of Languages, which undergirds most of our subsequent study.

自学 SMoL Teach Yourself SMoL

本书的核心是你对 SMoL 的理解。不过，为避免阅读变成一种被动体验，Kuang-Chen Lu 实现了一系列可按自身进度学习的辅导程序，教你学习 SMoL。这些辅导程序既传授概念知识，也教授重要术语。 This work is centered around your understanding of SMoL. However, to avoid a passive reading experience, Kuang-Chen Lu  has implemented a series of self-paced tutors to teach you SMoL. The tutors both give you conceptual knowledge and teach you important terminology.

重要的是，它们还有简短快捷的测试题，确保你走在正确的道路上。这些问题有两个目的。首先，它们迫使你认真学习辅导内容：你不能只是被动地滚动页面。其次，它们针对的是学习这些材料时已知的常见误解。其他学习者犯过这些错误，所以你也可能犯。要留心！ Importantly, they also have short, quick test questions to make sure you’re on the right track. These questions serve two ends. First, they force you to pay attention to the tutor: you can’t just scroll through passively. Second, they are based on known misconceptions  with this material. Other learners made these mistakes, so you might too. Pay attention!

由于这些教程目前不支持中途停止、保存进度后再继续，我们把材料拆成了一组小型（！）辅导程序，每个涵盖一个概念（有时甚至不到一个）。这样，你可以完成一两个或三个辅导程序，休息一下，稍后再接着学。 Because the tutorials currently do not support stopping, saving your work, and resuming, we have broken the material down into a set of small (!) tutors, each covering one concept (and sometimes even less). That way, you can do a tutor or three, take a break, and pick up later.

所有辅导程序都可以在这里找到： The tutors are all available from here:

https://smol-tutor.xyz/tutor/

在继续阅读本书之前，你应该先完成这些辅导程序！ Before you go on in this book, you should do the tutors!

关于 SMoL，一个重要的认识是：它的语义嵌入了我们几乎所有关于编程的思考。最明显的是，我们的算法分析基础——想想空间和时间的大 O 记号——有一个底层的、往往隐含的成本模型。例如，这个成本模型假设，参数在函数调用发生时求值，传递大型数据时不会复制这些数据。这也正是 SMoL 规定应该发生的行为。 The important thing to understand about SMoL is that its semantics is embedded into almost all our thinking about programming. Most notably, our algorithm analysis foundations—think Big-O for space and time—have an underlying, often implicit, cost model. That cost model assumes, for instance, that arguments are evaluated when a function call occurs, and that passing large data does not copy them. This is exactly what SMoL says should happen, too.

••••• 求值 ••••• ••••• Evaluation •••••

我们先来研究构建求值器的过程：求值器就是把程序变成答案的程序。我们将遵循 SImPl，同时探索 SMoL 中的核心概念。 We begin by studying the process of building evaluators: programs that turn programs into answers. We will follow SImPl, while exploring the core concepts in SMoL.

纸上求值 Evaluation on Paper

求值器 Evaluators

我们想要实现一种编程语言：也就是说，编写一个求值器（即某种“将程序归约为值”的东西）。在开始处理计算机带来的复杂性之前，先在纸上理解求值的工作方式会有所帮助。 We’re trying to implement a programming language: that is, to write an evaluator  (i.e., something that “reduces programs to values”). It helps if we can first understand how evaluation  works on paper, before we start dealing with computer complexities.

深入细节之前，值得知道的是，大体上有两类求值器（还有它们的许多组合）。它们采取截然不同的策略： Before we get into the details, it’s worth knowing that there are broadly speaking two kinds of evaluators (as well as many combinations of them). They follow very different strategies:

  • 解释器接收一个程序并模拟其执行。也就是说，解释器所做的，正是我们期望“运行程序”时应该做的事。 An interpreter  consumes a program and simulates  its execution . That is, the interpreter does what we would expect “running the program” should do.
  • 编译器接收一个程序并生成另一个程序。这个输出程序随后还必须进一步求值。 A compiler  consumes a program and produces another program . That output program must then be further evaluated.

也就是说，解释器将某种语言 L 中的程序映射为值： That is, an interpreter maps programs in some language L  to values:

interpreter :: Program L  → Value

目前，我们暂不严格规定值究竟是什么，只把它非正式地理解为用户想看到的答案——换句话说，某种不能或不需要继续求“值”的东西。相比之下， We leave open exactly what a value  is for now, informally understanding it to be an answer the user would want to see—put differently, something that either cannot or does not need to be further e-valu-ated. In contrast,

compiler :: Program L  → Program T

也就是说，从 L 到 T 的编译器（我们用 T 表示“目标”）接收 L 中的程序，生成 T 中的程序。我们并没有规定这个 T 程序必须如何求值。它可以直接解释执行，也可以继续编译。例如，可以把 Scheme 程序编译成 C。这个 C 程序可以直接解释执行，但也很可能会被编译成汇编。然而，我们不能无穷无尽地编译下去：在最底层，必须存在某种解释器（例如，在计算机硬件中）来提供答案。 That is, a compiler from L  to T  (we use T  for “target”) consumes programs in L  and produces programs in T . We aren’t saying about how this T  program must be evaluated. It may be interpreted directly, or it may be further compiled. For instance, one can compile a Scheme program to C. The C program may be interpreted directly, but it may very well be compiled to assembly. However, we can’t keep compiling ad infinitum: at the bottom, there must be some kind of interpreter (e.g., in the computer’s hardware) to provide answers.

注意，解释器和编译器本身也是用某种语言编写的程序，它们自身也必须运行。自然，这会引出一些有趣的想法和问题。 Note that interpreters and compilers are themselves programs written in some language and must themselves run. Naturally, this can lead to interesting ideas and problems.

在学习中，我们将主要关注解释器，但也会看到一种非常轻量的编译器。解释器很有用，因为： In our study, we will focus primarily on interpreters, but also see a very lightweight form of compilers. Interpreters are useful because:

  1. 编写一个简单的解释器通常比编写编译器容易得多。 A simple interpreter is often much easier to write than a compiler.
  2. 调试解释器有时比调试编译器容易得多。 Debugging an interpreter can sometimes be much easier than debugging a compiler.

因此，它们提供了一种人人都能采用的、有用的“基线”实现技术。而编译器通常值得用一整门课程来学习。 Therefore, they provide a useful “baseline” implementation technology that everyone can reach for. Compilers can often take an entire course of study.

术语 Terminology

在网上，经常看到人们说“解释型语言”和“编译型语言”。这些术语毫无意义。这不只是一个评价；而是字面上的陈述：它们在逻辑上说不通。解释和编译是人们用来对程序求值的技术。一种语言（几乎）从来不会规定应当如何对它求值。因此，每个实现者都可以自由选择自己想要的策略。 It is common, on the Web, to read people speak of “interpreted languages” and “compiled languages”. These terms are nonsense . That isn’t just a judgment; that’s a literal statement: they do not make sense. Interpretation and compilation are techniques one uses to evaluate programs. A language  (almost) never specifies how it should be evaluated. As a result, each implementer is free to choose whatever strategy they want.

举个例子，C 经常被选为典型的“编译型语言”，而 Scheme 则经常被当作“解释型语言”介绍。然而，C 的解释器确实存在过（虽说数量不多）；事实上，我最初学习 C 时就用过一个。同样，Scheme 的编译器有很多；我最初学习 Scheme 时就用过一个。Python 也有若干解释器和编译器。 Just as an example, C is often chosen as a canonically “compiled language”, while Scheme is often presented as an “interpreted language”. However, there have been (a handful of) interpreters for C; indeed, I used one when I first learned C. Likewise, there are numerous compilers for Scheme; I used one when I first learned Scheme. Python has several interpreters and compilers.

此外，这种看似明确的区分，在实践中经常被打破。如今，许多语言都有“JIT”，也就是即时编译。也就是说，求值器起初作为解释器工作。如果发现自己反复解释同一段代码，它就把这段代码编译，并改用编译后的代码。何时以及如何这样做，是一个复杂而迷人的主题，但它清楚地表明，两者之间没有泾渭分明的界线。 Furthermore, this seemingly hard distinction is frequently broken down in practice. Many languages now have a “JIT”, which stands for just-in-time  compilation. That is, the evaluator starts out as an interpreter. If it finds itself interpreting the same code over and over, it compiles it and uses the compiled code instead. When and how to do this is a complex and fascinating topic, but it makes clear that the distinction is not a bright line.

有些人会被实现所呈现的界面迷惑。许多语言提供读入—求值—打印循环（REPL），也就是交互式界面。解释器往往更容易做到这一点。不过，许多具有这种界面的系统，会在提示符处接收代码，将其编译、运行，再向用户呈现答案；它们把所有这些步骤都隐藏起来了。因此，界面不能表明你所见的是哪一种实现。把一种实现称为“交互式”或“非交互式”，或许有意义，但这并不反映底层语言的性质。 Some people are confused by the interface  that an implementation presents. Many languages provide a read-eval-print loop  (REPL), i.e., an interactive interface. It is often easier for an interpreter to do this. However, many systems with such an interface accept code at a prompt, compile it, run it, and present the answer back to the user; they mask all these steps. Therefore, the interface is not an indicator of what kind of implementation you are seeing. It is perhaps meaningful to refer to an implementation  as “interactive” or “non-interactive”, but that is not a reflection of the underlying language.

简而言之，请记住： In short, please remember:

  • （大多数）语言并不规定实现方式。使用哪种实现，由不同平台以及其他考量决定。 (Most) Languages do not dictate implementations. Different platforms and other considerations dictate what implementation to use.
  • 实现通常采用两种主要策略之一——解释和编译——但许多实现也是两者的混合。 Implementations usually use one of two major strategies—interpretation and compilation—but many are also hybrids of these.
  • 某个具体实现可能提供交互式或非交互式界面。然而，这并不会自动揭示其底层的实现策略。 A specific implementation may offer an interactive or non-interactive interface. However, this does not  automatically reveal the underlying implementation strategy.
  • 因此，“解释型语言”和“编译型语言”这两个术语毫无意义。 Therefore, the terms “interpreted language” and “compiled language” are nonsensical.

手动模拟解释器 Simulating an Interpreter by Hand

既然已经决定编写解释器，那在研究如何让它做到我们想做的事情之前，先来理解我们究竟想让它做什么。 Since we have decided to write an interpreter, let’s start by understanding what  we are trying to get it to do, before we start to investigate how  we will make it do it.

考虑下面这个程序： Let’s consider the following program:

(define (f x) (+ x 1))

(f 2)

它会得到什么结果？我们都能猜到，它得到 3。现在假设有人问，为什么它得到 3？你会怎么回答？ What does it produce? We can all guess that it produces 3 . Now suppose we’re asked, why  does it produce 3 ? What might you say?

你很可能会说，因为 f 的函数体中的 x 被替换成了 2，然后我们计算函数体，这就是答案： There’s a good chance you’ll say that it’s because x gets replaced with 2 in the body of f, then we compute the body, and that’s the answer:

→   (f 2)

→ (+ x 1)，其中 x 被替换为 2 → (+ x 1)  where x  is replaced by 2

→ (+ 2 1)

→ 3

这些程序用 Racket 编写。你可以把它们放进 DrRacket，选择较初级的学生语言级别（如 Beginning Student），然后使用菜单栏中的 Step 按钮，逐步观看它们运行： These programs are written in Racket. You can put these programs into DrRacket in an early student language level (like Beginning Student) and watch them run, step-by-step, using the Step button in the menu bar:

现在来看这个程序的扩展版本： Now let’s look at an extended version of the program:

;; f is the same as before

(define (g z)

  (f (+ z 4)))

(g 5)

我们可以采用相同的过程： We can use the same process:

→   (g 5)

→ ( f (+ z 4))，其中 z 被替换为 5 → ( f (+ z 4))  where z  is replaced by 5

→ (f (+ 5 4))

→ (f 9)

→ (+ x 1)，其中 x 被替换为 9 → (+ x 1)  where x  is replaced by 9

→ (+ 9 1)

→ 10

术语：我们将函数头中的变量称为形式参数，将函数调用中的表达式称为实际参数。因此，在 f 中，x 是形式参数，而 9 是实际参数。有些人还会用 argument 代替 parameter，但这两个术语之间并没有真正的区别。 Terminology:  We call the variables in the function header the formal parameters  and the expressions in the function call the actual parameters . So in f , x  is the formal parameter, while 9  is an actual parameter. Some people also use argument  in place of parameter , but there’s no real difference between these terms.

注意，我们曾有一个选择：既可以这样做， Observe that we had a choice: we could have gone either

→ (f (+ 5 4))

→ (f 9)

也可以这样做， or

→ (f (+ 5 4))

→ (+ x 1)，其中 x 被替换为 (+ 5 4) → (+ x 1)  where x  is replaced by (+ 5 4)

目前，两种方式会得到相同的答案，但这实际上是个影响深远的决定！事实上，它是编程语言设计中最深刻的选择之一。 For now, both will produce the same answer , but this is actually a very consequential decision! It is in fact one of the most profound choices in programming language design.

术语：前一种选择称为急切求值：可以把它想成，在开始函数调用之前，“急切地”将实际参数归约成一个值。后一种选择称为惰性求值：可以把它想成，不急于执行求值。 Terminology:  The former choice is called eager  evaluation: think of it as “eagerly” reducing the actual parameter to a value before starting the function call. The latter choice is called lazy  evaluation: think of it as not rushing to perform the evaluation.

SMoL 采用急切求值。这有充分的理由，我们稍后会探讨 [ 👉 ]。 SMoL is eager . There are good reasons for this, which we will explore later [ 👉 ].

好了，回到求值。让我们再前进一步： Okay, so back to evaluation. Let’s do one more step:

;; f is the same as before

;; g is the same as before

(define (h z w)

  (+ (g z) (g w)))

(h 6 7)

我们可以再次查看这些步骤： Once again, we can look at the steps:

→   (h 6 7)

→ (+ (g z) (g w))，其中 z 被替换为 6，w 被替换为 7 → (+ (g z) (g w))  where z  is replaced by 6  and w  is replaced by 7

→ (+ (g 6) (g 7))

→ (+ (f (+ y 4)) (g 7))，其中 y 被替换为 6 → (+ (f (+ y 4)) (g 7))  where y  is replaced by 6

→ (+ (f (+ 6 4)) (g 7))

→ (+ (f 10) (g 7))

→ (+ (+ x 1) (g 7))，其中 x 被替换为 10 → (+ (+ x 1) (g 7))  where x  is replaced by 10

→ (+ (+ 10 1) (g 7))

→ (+ 11 (g 7))

→ (+ 11 (f (+ y 4)))，其中 y 被替换为 7 → (+ 11 (f (+ y 4)))  where y  is replaced by 7

→ (+ 11 (f (+ 7 4)))

→ (+ 11 (f 11))

→ (+ 11 (+ x 1))，其中 x 被替换为 11 → (+ 11 (+ x 1))  where x  is replaced by 11

→ (+ 11 (+ 11 1))

→ (+ 11 12)

→ 23

注意，我们又有了一些选择： Observe that we again had some choices:

  • 是一次替换两个调用，还是一次处理一个？ Do we replace both calls at once, or do one at a time?
  • 如果是后者，先处理左边还是右边？ If the latter, do we do the left or the right one first?

语言也必须对这些问题作出决定！上面，我们再次采用了 SMoL 的做法：完成一个调用后才开始另一个，因此 SMoL 是顺序的。如果我们同时替换两个调用，探索的就是一种并行语言。按照惯例，大多数语言选择从左到右的顺序，因此我们在 SMoL 中也这样选择。 Languages have to make decisions about these, too! Above, we’ve again done what SMoL does: it finishes one call before starting the other, which makes SMoL sequential . Had we replaced both calls at once, we’d be exploring a parallel  language. Conventionally, most languages choose a left-to-right order, so that’s what we choose in SMoL.

替换 Substitution

顺便说一句，注意到没有，回答这些问题并不需要懂计算机编程。你在初高中代数课上就做过类似的事。你学到的说法可能是“代入”，而不是“替换”。我们这里遵循的正是同一个过程。事实上，我们可以把编程看作代数的自然延伸，只不过数据类型有趣得多：不只有数字，还有字符串、图像、列表、表格、向量场、视频，等等。 By the way, observe that you didn’t need to know any computer programming to answer these questions. You did something similar in middle- and high-school algebra classes. You probably learned the phrase substitution  for “replaced with”. That’s the same process we’re following here. And indeed, we can think of programming as a natural outgrowth of algebra, except with much more interesting datatypes: not only numbers but also strings, images, lists, tables, vector fields, videos, and more.

好了，这就给了我们一种实现求值器的方法： Okay, so this gives us a way to implement an evaluator:

  • 找到一种表示程序源代码的方式（例如，字符串或树）。 Find a way to represent program source (e.g., a string or a tree).
  • 寻找下一个要求值的表达式。 Look for the next expression to evaluate.
  • 通过（文本）替换得到一个新程序。 Perform substitution (textually) to obtain a new program.
  • 继续求值，直到只剩一个值。 Continue evaluating until there’s nothing left but a value.

然而，正如你可能已经猜到的，大多数编程语言实际并不是这样工作的：一般来说，这会慢得令人难以忍受。所以，我们必须找到更好的方法！ However, as you might have guessed, that’s not how most programming languages actually  work: in general it would be painfully slow. So we’ll have to find a better way!

表示算术 Representing Arithmetic

让我们开始考虑真正编写一个求值器。我们将从一种简单的算术语言入手，再逐步扩展。因此，我们的语言会有 Let’s start thinking about actually writing an evaluator. We’ll start with a simple arithmetic language, and then build our way up from there. So our language will have

  • 数字 numbers
  • 一些算术运算：实际上，只有加法 some arithmetic operations: in fact, just  addition

暂时没有其他内容，以便专注于基础。我们会逐渐扩充它。 and nothing more for now, so we can focus on the basics. Over time we’ll build this up.

不过，在考虑求值器的函数体之前，我们需要弄清楚它的类型：尤其是，它接收什么？ Before we can think about the body of an evaluator, however, we need to figure out its type: in particular, what will it consume?

表示程序 Representing Programs

那么，求值器接收什么呢？它接收程序。因此，我们需要弄清楚如何表示程序。 Well, what does  an evaluator consume? It consumes programs . So we need to figure out how to represent programs .

当然，计算机一直都在表示程序。编写代码时，文本编辑器保存着程序源代码。磁盘和内存中的每个可执行文件，都是程序的一种表示。我们访问网页时，网页会向我们发送一个 JavaScript 程序。这些全都是计算机中表示的程序。但就我们的需求而言，这些表示都有些不便，我们马上就会想出一种更好的表示。 Of course, computers represent programs all the time. When we’re writing code, our text editor holds the program source. Every executable on disk and in memory is a representation of a program. When we visit a Web page, it sends down a JavaScript program. These are all programs represented in the computer. But all these are a bit inconvenient for our needs, and we’ll come up with a better representation in a moment.

在思考表示方式之前，先想想要表示什么。以下是一些（算术）程序的例子： Before thinking about represent ations , let’s think about what we’re represent ing . Here are some example (arithmetic) programs:

1

0

-1

2.3

1 + 2

3 + 4

问题已经出现了。程序该怎么写呢？你能看出这个问题的走向：1 与 2 的和应该写成 Already we have a question. How should we write  our program? You can see where this is going: should we be writing the sum of 1 and 2 as

1 + 2

还是写成 or as

(+ 1 2)

+ 1 2

1 2 +

等等。（甚至还可以问，基本数字该用哪种记数系统：例如，应该写 3 还是 III？如果你真的愿意，用后者也能编程。） and so on. (For that matter, we can even ask what numeral system to use for basic numbers: e..g, should we write 3  or III ? You can program with the latter  if you’d really like to.)

这些都是该采用何种表层语法的问题。它们非常重要！而且有趣！而且重要！人们往往特别偏爱某些表层语法而不喜欢另一些（对于 Racket 的括号语法，你可能已经有了些感受……我当然有）。在 Scratch 和 Snap! 中，你甚至可以把那个表达式写成 These are questions of what surface syntax  to use. And they are very important! And interesting! And important! People get really attached to some surface syntaxes over the other (you may already be having some feelings about Racket’s parenthetical syntax…I certainly do). You can even write that expression as

这种形式，而这种语法对帮助年幼儿童学习编程极其宝贵，让他们不必面对文本语法的各种变幻莫测。 in Scratch and Snap!, and this syntax has been invaluable in getting young children to learn how to program without all the vagaries of textual syntax.

因此，这些都是很有价值的人因考量。但就理解语言的底层模型而言，它们眼下会分散注意力。所以，我们需要一种表示所有这些不同程序的方法，使其忽略这些区别。 Thus, these are great human-factors considerations. But for now these are a distraction in terms of getting to understand the models  underlying languages. Therefore, we need a way to represent all these different programs in a way that ignores these distinctions.

抽象语法 Abstract Syntax

这就引出了 SImPl（标准实现方案）的第一部分：创建所谓的抽象语法。在抽象语法中，我们表示输入的本质，忽略表面的语法细节。因此，在抽象语法中，上面的所有程序都会有完全相同的表示。 This leads us to the first part of SImPl  (the Standard Implementation Plan): the creation of what is called abstract syntax . In abstract syntax, we represent the essence of the input, ignoring the superficial syntactic details. Thus, in abstract syntax, all of the above programs will have the exact same representation.

抽象语法是程序在计算机内部的一种表示。可以用许多种数据作为表示，所以让我们想想，可能想要表示什么样的程序。为简单起见，假设我们的语言只有数字和加法；一旦能够处理它们，再处理更多运算就容易了。以下是一些（表层语法）程序示例： An abstract syntax is an in-computer representation of programs. There are many kinds of data we can use as a representation, so let’s think about the kinds of programs we might want to represent. For simplicity, we’ll assume that our language has only numbers and addition; once we can handle that, it’ll be easy to handle additional operations. Here are some sample (surface syntax) programs:

1

2.3

1 + 2

1 + 2 + 3

1 + 2 + 3 + 4

当然，在传统算术记法中，必须考虑运算顺序，以及哪些运算优先于哪些运算。在抽象语法中，这又是一个我们想忽略的细节；我们转而假定，内部使用的表示相当于加上全部括号的表达式，这些问题都已解决。因此，上面最后两个表达式就好像被写成了 In conventional arithmetic notation, of course, we have to worry about the order of operations and what operations take precedence over what others. In abstract syntax, that’s another detail we want to ignore; we’ll instead assume that we are working internally with the equivalent of fully-parenthesized expressions, where all these issues have been resolved. Thus, it’s as if the last two expressions above were written as

(1 + 2) + 3 或 1 + (2 + 3) (1 + 2) + 3     or     1 + (2 + 3)

1 + ((2 + 3) + 4)

那么请注意，加法运算的每一边，本身都可以是一个完整的表达式。这强烈地提示了内部应采用哪种表示：树。事实上，抽象语法树的使用如此普遍，以至于它的缩写 AST 经常不加解释就直接使用；在有关这个主题的书籍、论文、博客文章等资料中，你都会看到它。 Observe, then, that each side of the addition operation can be a full-blown expression in its own right. This gives us a strong hint as to what kind of representation to use internally: a tree . Indeed, it’s so common to use abstract syntax trees  that the abbreviation, AST, is routinely used without explanation; you can expect to see it in books, papers, blog posts, etc. on this topic.

你很可能以前见过这个想法：它叫作句子图解（可在维基百科了解更多）。例如，下面是句子“He studies linguistics at the university”（他在大学学习语言学）的图解： You have quite possibly seen this idea before: it’s called sentence diagramming  (read more on Wikipedia ). Here, for instance, is a diagram of the sentence “He studies linguistics at the university”:

作者：Xbarst1.jpg：Russky1802；衍生作品：Maxdamantus。此文件衍生自 Xbarst1.jpg，公有领域，https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=21979041 By Xbarst1.jpg: Russky1802 derivative work: Maxdamantus - This file was derived from: Xbarst1.jpg:, Public Domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=21979041

NP 是名词短语，V 是动词，依此类推。请看，句子图解如何把一个线性的句子转变成语法结构的树形表示。我们想对程序做同样的事。 An NP is a Noun Phrase, V is a Verb, and so on. Observe how the sentence diagram takes a linear  sentence and turns it into a tree-shaped  representation of the grammatical structure. We want to do the same for programs.

表示抽象语法 Representing Abstract Syntax

在本书的其余部分，除非另有说明，我们都会用 Racket 的 plait 语言来实现各种东西。请确保已安装 plait，以便跟着操作。 In the rest of this book, except where indicated otherwise, we will implement things in the plait   language of Racket. Please make sure you have plait installed to follow along.

我们将在 plait 中创建一个新的树数据类型来表示 AST。在上面的句子图解中，树叶是单词，节点是语法术语。在我们的 AST 中，树叶将是数字，而节点则是对表示各子表达式的树进行的运算。目前只有一种运算：加法。下面是在 plait 语法中的表示方法： We will create a new tree datatype in plait to represent ASTs. In the sentence diagram above, the leaves of the tree are words, and the nodes are grammatical terms. In our AST, the leaves will be numbers, while the nodes will be operations on the trees representing each sub-expression. For now, we have only one operation: addition. Here’s how we can represent this in plait syntax:

(define-type Exp

  [num (n : Number)]

  [plus (left : Exp) (right : Exp)])

它的意思是： This says:

  • 我们正在定义一个新类型 Exp We are defining a new type, Exp
  • 有两种构造 Exp 的方式 There are two ways of making an Exp
  • 一种方式是通过构造器 num： One way is through the constructor num :
  • num 接收一个参数 A num  takes one argument
  • 这个参数必须是一个真正的数字 That argument must be an actual number
  • 另一种方式是通过构造器 plus： The other way is through the constructor plus :
  • plus 接收两个参数 A plus  takes two arguments
  • 两个参数都必须是 Exp Both arguments must be Exp s

如果对理解后文有帮助，可以把它看作与下面的 Java 伪代码骨架非常相似（用 Python 的 dataclass 也有类似写法）： If it helps as you read what follows, this is very analogous to the following Java pseudocode skeleton (or the analog with Python dataclasses):

abstract class Exp {}

class num extends Exp {

  num(Number n) { … }

}

class plus extends Exp {

  plus(Exp left, Exp right) { … }

}

来看看前面的一些例子会如何表示： Let’s look at how some of the previous examples would be represented:

表层语法 Surface Syntax

AST

1

(num 1)

2.3

(num 2.3)

1 + 2

(plus (num 1) (num 2))

(1 + 2) + 3

(plus (plus (num 1) (num 2))

      (num 3))

1 + (2 + 3)

(plus (num 1)

      (plus (num 2) (num 3)))

1 + ((2 + 3) + 4)

(plus (num 1)

      (plus (plus (num 2)

                  (num 3))

            (num 4)))

注意这些例子中的几点： Observe a few things about these examples:

  • 这个数据类型定义不允许我们直接表示 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 这样的表层语法项；在构造相应 AST 项的时候，所有歧义都必须已经得到处理。 The datatype definition does not let us directly  represent surface syntax terms such as 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 ; any ambiguity has to be handled by the time we construct the corresponding AST term.
  • 数字的表示可能看起来有点奇怪：我们有一个 num 构造器，它唯一的工作就是“包裹”一个数字。这样做是为了让表示保持一致。等到开始编写处理这些数据的程序时，就会明白为什么这样做。 The number representation might look a bit odd: we have a num  constructor whose only job is to “wrap” a number. We do this for consistency of representation. As we start writing programs to process these data, it’ll become clear why we did this.
  • 注意，表达式中每个重要部分都进入了它的 AST 表示，尽管方式未必相同。尤其是，加法中的 + 由构造器表示；它不是参数的一部分。 Notice that every significant part of the expression went into its AST representation, though not always in the same way. In particular, the +  of an addition is represented by the constructor ; it is not part of the parameters.
  • AST 完全不在乎使用了什么表层语法。最后一项也可以写成 (+ 1 (+ (+ 2 3) 4))，甚至写成图中的形式，想必都会产生相同的 AST。 The AST really doesn’t care what surface syntax was used. The last term could instead have been written as



    (+ 1

      (+ (+ 2 3)

         4))



    or even as







    and it would presumably produce the same AST.

简言之，AST 是在程序中表示程序的树形数据。这是一个深刻的思想！事实上，它是 20 世纪的伟大思想之一，建立在 Gödel（编码）、Turing（通用机）、von Neumann（存储程序计算机）和 McCarthy（元循环解释器）的杰出工作之上。 In short, ASTs are tree-structured data that represent programs in programs . This is a profound idea! In fact, it’s one of the great ideas of the 20th century, building on the brilliant work of Gödel (encoding), Turing (universal machine), von Neumann (stored program computer), and McCarthy (metacircular interpreter).

旁注：源程序并非每个部分都在 AST 中有所表示。例如，1 + 2 和 1 + 2 想必会用相同方式表示，忽略其中的空格。实际上，真正的语言实现确实需要了解某些语法信息：例如，像 DrRacket 那样，在出错时高亮显示程序源代码的相应部分。因此，现实中的实现使用抽象语法，但还附带元数据，将其关联回源代码。 Aside:  Not every part of the source program has been represented in the AST. For instance, presumably both 1 + 2  and 1    +  2  would be represented the same way, ignoring the spaces. In practice, a real language implementation does need to know something about the syntax: for instance, to highlight pieces of the program source when there is an error, as DrRacket does. Therefore, real-world implementations use abstract syntax but with metadata relating it back to the source.

算术求值 Evaluating Arithmetic

定义求值器 Defining the Evaluator

看过如何表示算术程序之后，我们转向编写一个求值器程序，把它们变成答案。 Having seen how to represent arithmetic programs, we turn to writing an evaluator program that turns them into answers.

这个求值器的类型是什么？显然，它接收程序，这里程序用 Exp 表示。它生成什么？在当前情况下，所有这些表达式都会生成数字。因此，我们暂时把它叫作计算器，简称 calc。于是，可以给 calc 赋予如下类型 What is the type of this evaluator? Clearly it consumes programs, which here are represented by Exp s. What does it produce? In this case, all these expressions are going to produce numbers. For this reason, we’ll call this a calculator, or calc  for short, for now. We can thus give calc  the type

(calc : (Exp -> Number))

现在尝试定义它的函数体。显然，我们必须有 Let’s now try to define its body. Clearly we must have

(define (calc e)

  …)

在函数体中，给定一个 Exp，我们要用 type-case 将它拆开。type-case 告诉我们有两种可能，每种都带有一些额外数据（这在实质上等同于我们在 Java 中会采用的方法分派）： In the body, given an Exp , we will want to take it apart using type-case , which tells us there are two options, each with some additional data (this is the moral equivalent of the method dispatch we’d have used in Java):

  (type-case Exp e

    [(num n) …]

    [(plus l r) …])

如果整个表达式已经是一个数字，会怎样呢？既然已经有了答案，直接返回即可。否则，就必须将两边相加： What happens in the case that the whole expression is already a number? Well, we have our answer, so we just return it. Otherwise, we have to add the two sides:

  (type-case Exp e

    [(num n) n]

    [(plus l r) (+ l r)])

这样，整个函数体就是： giving us an overall body of:

(define (calc e)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(num n) n]

    [(plus l r) (+ l r)]))

让我们运行它……哎呀！出现类型错误了！它告诉我们，加法期待一个数字，但 l 不是数字：它是一个 Exp。啊，这是因为 l 和 r 仍然表示表达式，而不是表达式求值所得的答案。要解决这个问题，我们需要某种能把表达式变成数字的东西……这恰恰就是我们正在定义的东西！因此，我们改为这样写 Let’s run it to…oops! We get a type error! It tells us that addition is expecting a number, but l  is not a number: it’s an Exp . Ah, that’s because l  and r  still represent expressions , not the answer  that the expressions evaluate to. To fix that, we need something that can turn an expression into a number…which is precisely what we’re defining! Thus, we instead write

(define (calc e)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(num n) n]

    [(plus l r) (+ (calc l) (calc r))]))

现在类型检查器满意了。果然，可以确认这些例子得到了预期结果。例如： The type-checker is happy now. And sure enough, we can confirm that our examples produce what we expect. For instance:

(calc (num 1))

得到 1， produces 1 ,

(calc (plus (num 1) (num 2)))

得到 3，而 produces 3 , and

(plus (num 1)

      (plus (num 2) (num 3)))

得到 6。 produces  6 .

旁注：我们略过了一个细节：我们假定 + 总是表示数字加法（在 AST 中将它命名为“plus”，就已隐含了这一点）。但有些语言允许“相加”的类型有很多种：例如，它也可以连接字符串。在这样的语言中，AST 中的名称可能会更通用，求值器也需要处理各种可能的行为。 Aside:  We’ve glossed over a detail: we’ve assumed that +  always means numeric addition (which was already implicit in calling it “ plus ” in the AST). But some languages allow any number of different types to be “added”: e.g., it can also concatenate strings. In such languages, the name in the AST might be something more generic, and the evaluator would need to handle the different possible behaviors.

事实上，我们还略过了更基本的事情：数字加法是什么意思，甚至数字本身究竟是什么。正如在“神秘语言：算术”中所见，这里有许多选择。在我们的计算器中，采用的是 plait 的数字（在 num 中）和 plait 的加法（通过使用 +）。calc 中的这些位置也告诉我们，要改变这些选择，应当到哪里修改。 In fact, we’ve glossed over something even more basic: what numeric addition means, or for that matter, even what numbers are. As we see from the Mystery Language: Arithmetic, there are many choices here. In our calculator, we have adopted numbers from plait (in num ) and addition from plait (by using + ). Those places in calc  also tell us where we would go to change those choices.

测试求值器 Testing the Evaluator

上面的例子不错，但应该用测试的语法将它们写出来，让计算机自动替我们检查： The examples above are fine, but we should write these in the syntax of tests , so that the computer checks them for us automatically:

(test (calc (num 1)) 1)

(test (calc (num 2.3)) 2.3)

(test (calc (plus (num 1) (num 2))) 3)

(test (calc (plus (plus (num 1) (num 2))

                  (num 3)))

      6)

(test (calc (plus (num 1)

                  (plus (num 2) (num 3))))

      6)

(test (calc (plus (num 1)

                  (plus (plus (num 2)

                              (num 3))

                        (num 4))))

      10)

果然，运行后，Racket 确认所有这些测试都通过了。 Sure enough, when we run this, Racket confirms that all these tests pass.

专业小窍门：逐一查看所有测试输出，判断是否有测试失败，会令人厌烦。只要在测试之前加上 Pro Tip:  It can get annoying to scan through all this testing output to see whether any of the tests failed. Simply add

(print-only-errors #true)

Racket 就会不再报告通过的测试，让你专注于失败的测试：换句话说，没有消息就是好消息。 before your tests and Racket will suppress reporting on the passing tests, so you can focus on the ones that failed: in other words, no news is good news.

一般来说，测试要早、要勤、要全面。编程语言求值器把我们的思想转换成计算机的行动。因此，它们能精确完成这件事至关重要。这就是为什么语言实现是你能想到的测试最充分的软件之一（上一次因为语言实现中的错误而受阻是什么时候？），而且，那些几乎能容忍其他任何软件中的错误的人，对于语言实现中的错误却远没有那么宽容。 In general, test early, often, and extensively. Programming language evaluators translate our thoughts into computer actions. Therefore, it’s critical that they do so precisely. This is why language implementations are some of the most tested software you can imagine (when’s the last time you were stopped by a bug in your language implementation?), and people who will tolerate bugs in just about any other software are much less forgiving of bugs in implementations.

一些更微妙的测试 Some Subtler Tests

试试下面的测试： Try the following test:

(test (calc (plus (num 0.1) (num 0.2))) 0.3)

它成功了！我们满意了吗？假设改写成这样： It succeeds! Are we happy? Suppose we instead write it as:

(test (calc (plus (num 0.1) (num 0.2))) 1/3)

不出所料，它失败了：但错误消息显示，左边求值为 0.30000000000000004。这应该提醒我们，实际得到的是浮点加法。这是因为 plait 会把像 0.1 这样带小数点的数字视为浮点位串。然而，浮点位串无法精确表示数字 0.3。事实上，plait 的 test 允许少许数值误差，所以上面通过的那个测试能够成立。（这是因为，在 plait 中，0.3 确实精确地表示数字 0.3，因为它是直接写出的字面量，而不是浮点计算的结果。） As expected, it fails: but the error message reveals that the left-hand side evaluated to 0.30000000000000004. This should be a cue that we have actually gotten floating point  addition. This is because plait treats numbers written with a decimal point, like 0.1 , as floating point  bitstrings. However, floating point bitstrings cannot precisely represent the number 0.3. In fact, plait’s test  allows a little bit of numeric slack so that the passing test above works. (This is because in plait, 0.3  really does precisely represent the number 0.3, because it was written literally and not the result of a floating-point computation.)

这强化了前面顺带提过、因而容易被忽略的一点：采用 plait 的原语，也就继承了它的语义。这可能是我们想要的，也可能不是！因此，用宿主语言编写求值器时，必须确保它的语义就是我们想要的，否则可能会遇到令人不快的意外。如果想要不同的行为，就必须明确地实现它。 This reinforces a point we made in passing above and was therefore easy to miss: by adopting plait’s primitives, we have also inherited its semantics. This may or may not be what we wanted! Therefore, when writing an evaluator using a host language, we have to make sure that its semantics are the one we want, otherwise we could be in for an unpleasant surprise. If we want different behavior, we have to implement it explicitly.

结语 Conclusion

至此，我们对 SImPl 的初次考察就结束了：我们在程序中表示了一个程序，又在程序中处理了这个被表示的程序。我们刚刚编写了第一个处理程序的程序——现在可以大展身手了！ This concludes our first look at SImPl: we have represented  a program in a program, and we have processed  that represented program in a program. We have just written our first program that processes programs—now we’re off to the races!

解析：从源代码到 AST Parsing: From Source to ASTs

问题 The Problem

前面我们走过了 SImPl 的基本步骤，但留下了一个大问题：如何把程序转换成 AST 表示？当然，最简单的方法就是已经做过的：直接写 AST 构造器，例如， Earlier we went through the basic steps of the SImPl, but we left open a big question: how do we get programs into  the AST representation? Of course, the simplest way is what we already did: to write the AST constructors directly, e.g.,

(num 1)

(plus (num 1) (num 2))

(plus (num 1)

      (plus (num 2) (num 3)))

正如前面指出的，这种方式的优点是还能忽略程序源代码究竟如何书写。 which, as we noted, has the virtue of also ignoring exactly how the program source was written.

然而，这可能非常繁琐。例如，我们不希望每次想写一个数字时，都得写 (num …)！尤其是，越繁琐，我们就越不可能编写数量多或复杂的测试，这就特别令人遗憾。因此，我们希望有一种更方便的表层语法，以及一个将它翻译成 AST 的程序。 However, this can get very tedious. We don’t want to have to write (num …)  every time we want to write a number, for instance! In particular, the more tedious it is the less likely we are to write many or complex tests, and that would be especially unfortunate. Therefore, we’d like a more convenient surface syntax, along with a program  to translate that into ASTs.

正如已经看到的，我们可以使用大量不同的表层语法，甚至不局限于文本语法：它可以是图形的、口语的、手势的（想象你置身于虚拟现实环境中），等等。正如前面指出的，这种广泛的交互方式很重要——尤其当程序员有身体方面的限制时——但它不在当前研究范围内。即使采用文本语法，也必须处理歧义等问题（例如算术的运算顺序）。 As we have already seen, there is a large number of surface syntaxes we can use, and we aren’t even limited to textual syntax: it could be graphical; spoken; gestural (imagine you’re in a virtual reality environment); and so on. As we have noted, this wide range of modalities is important—especially so if the programmer has physical constraints—but it’s outside the range of our current study. Even with textual syntax, we have to deal with issues like ambiguity (e.g., order of operations in arithmetic).

一般来说，将输入语法转换成 AST 的过程称为解析。仅仅解析这个主题，就足以写一整本小册子……所以我们不这么做。相反，我们选择一种在便利和简单之间取得合理平衡的语法，即 Racket 的括号语法，plait 对它有专门支持。也就是说，我们会把上面的例子写成 In general, the process of converting the input syntax into ASTs is called parsing . We could write a whole booklet just on parsing…so we won’t. Instead, we’re going to pick one syntax that strikes a reasonable balance between convenience and simplicity, which is the parenthetical syntax of Racket, and has special support in plait. That is, we will write the above examples as

1

(+ 1 2)

(+ 1 (+ 2 3))

并看看 Racket 如何帮助我们方便地处理它们。事实上，本书将遵循一个约定（Racket 并不在乎这个约定，因为它对 ()、[] 和 {} 一视同仁）：我们用 {} 而不是 () 来书写要表示的程序。因此，上面的三个程序变成 and see how Racket can help us make these convenient to work with. In fact, in this book we will follow a convention (that Racket doesn’t care about, because it treats () , [] , and {}  interchangeably): we’ll write programs to be represented using {}  instead of () . Thus, the above three programs become

1

{+ 1 2}

{+ 1 {+ 2 3}}

S 表达式 S-Expressions

这种语法有个名称：S 表达式（s- 的来历是历史原因）。在 plait 中，书写这些表达式时，我们会在前面加一个反引号（`）。反引号后面跟一个 Racket 项，其类型就是 S-Exp。以下是一些 S 表达式的例子： There is a name for this syntax: these are called s-expressions  (the s-  is for historical reasons). In plait, we will write these expressions preceded by a back-tick  ( ` ). A back-tick followed by a Racket term is of type S-Exp . Here are examples of s-expressions:

`1

`2.3

`-40

这些都是数字 S 表达式。我们还可以写 These are all numeric s-expressions. We can also write

`{+ 1 2}

`{+ 1 {+ 2 3}}

这并不明显，但它们实际上是列表 S 表达式。可以这样询问来判断 It’s not obvious, but these are actually list  s-expressions. We can tell by asking

> (s-exp-list? `1)

- Boolean

#f

> (s-exp-list? `{+ 1 2})

- Boolean

#t

> (s-exp-list? `{+ 1 {+ 2 3}})

- Boolean

#t

所以第一个不是，但后两个是；类似地， So the first is not but the second two are; similarly,

> (s-exp-number? `1)

- Boolean

#t

> (s-exp-number? `{+ 1 {+ 2 3}})

- Boolean

#f

S-Exp 类型是包裹实际数字或列表的容器，我们可以把它们提取出来： The S-Exp  type is a container around the actual number or list, which we can extract:

> (s-exp->number `1)

- Number

1

> (s-exp->list `{+ 1 2})

- (Listof S-Exp)

(list `+ `1 `2)

现在动手！如果将 s-exp->number 应用于列表 S 表达式，或将 s-exp->list 应用于数字 S 表达式，会发生什么？如果把其中任一个应用于根本不是 S 表达式的东西呢？现在就试试看！得到的结果是否略有不同？ Do Now: What happens if you apply s-exp->number  to a list s-exp or s-exp->list  to a number s-expression? Or either to something that isn't an s-expression at all? Try it right now and find out! Do you get somewhat different results?

更仔细地看一下上面的最后一个输出。所得列表有三个元素，其中两个是数字，而第三个是别的东西： Let’s look at that last output above a bit more closely. The resulting list has three elements, two of which are numbers, but the third is something else:

`+

它是一个符号 S 表达式。符号类似字符串，但在操作和性能上有些不同。字符串有许多操作（例如取子串），而符号被作为原子对待；除转换为字符串外，它们唯一支持的其他操作就是相等性判断。作为回报，符号的相等性可以在常数时间内检查。 is a symbol  s-expression. Symbols are like strings but somewhat different in operations and performance. Whereas there are numerous string operations (like substrings), symbols are treated atomically; other than being converted to strings, the only other operation they support is equality. But in return, symbols can be checked for equality in constant  time.

符号与 Racket 变量具有相同的语法，因此特别适合表示类似变量的东西。于是 Symbols have the same syntax as Racket variables, and hence are perfect for representing variable-like things. Thus

> (s-exp-symbol? `+)

- Boolean

#t

> (s-exp->symbol `+)

- Symbol

'+

这个输出展示了 Racket 中符号的写法：使用单引号（'）。 This output shows how symbols are written in Racket: with a single-quote ( ' ).

还有其他种类的 S 表达式，但目前这些就够了！有了这些，我们就能编写第一个解析器了！ There are other kinds of s-expressions as well, but this is all we need for now! With this, we can write our first parser!

解析器中的第一位 Primus Inter Parsers

现在动手！想想我们希望解析器具有什么类型。 Do Now: Think about what type we want for our parser.

解析器需要生成什么？计算器所接收的东西，也就是 Exp。它接收什么？以“方便”的语法书写的程序源表达式，也就是 S-Exp。因此，它的类型必须是 What does our parser need to produce? Whatever the calculator consumes, i.e., Exp . What does it consume? Program source expressions written in a “convenient” syntax, i.e., S-Exp . Hence, its type must be

(parse : (S-Exp -> Exp))

也就是说，它把对人（比较）友好的语法转换为计算机的内部表示。 That is, it converts the human-friendly(ier) syntax into the computer’s internal representation.

编写它需要一定程度的细致较真。首先，需要一个条件判断，检查给定的是哪种 S 表达式： Writing this requires a certain degree of pedantry. First, we need a conditional to check what kind of s-exp we were given:

(define (parse s)

  (cond

    [(s-exp-number? s) …]

    [(s-exp-list? s) …]))

如果是数字 S 表达式，就要提取其中的数字，再传给 num 构造器： If it’s a numeric s-exp, then we need to extract the number and pass it to the num  constructor:

(num (s-exp->number s))

否则，就要提取列表，检查列表的第一个元素是不是加法符号。如果不是，就发出错误信号： Otherwise, we need to extract the list and check whether the first thing in the list is an addition symbol. If it is not, we signal an error:

     (let ([l (s-exp->list s)])

       (if (symbol=? '+

                     (s-exp->symbol (first l)))

           …

           (error 'parse "list not an addition")))

否则，通过递归处理两个子部分，创建一个 plus 项。 Otherwise, we create a plus term by recurring on the two sub-pieces.

            (plus (parse (second l))

                  (parse (third l)))

 

把这些合在一起： Putting it all together:

(define (parse s)

  (cond

    [(s-exp-number? s)

     (num (s-exp->number s))]

    [(s-exp-list? s)

     (let ([l (s-exp->list s)])

       (if (symbol=? '+

                     (s-exp->symbol (first l)))

           (plus (parse (second l))

                 (parse (third l)))

           (error 'parse "list not an addition")))]))

这确实有点繁琐，不过幸运的是，本书中解析的难度差不多也就到此为止了！从现在起，你看到的基本都会是同一种模式，可以随意照着写。 It’s all a bit much, but fortunately this is about as hard as parsing will get in this book! Everything you see from now on will basically be this same sort of pattern, which you can freely copy.

当然，我们应当确保为解析器编写了良好的测试。例如： We should, of course, make sure we’ve got good tests for our parser. For instance:

(test (parse `1) (num 1))

(test (parse `2.3) (num 2.3))

(test (parse `{+ 1 2}) (plus (num 1) (num 2)))

(test (parse `{+ 1

                 {+ {+ 2 3}

                    4}})

      (plus (num 1)

            (plus (plus (num 2)

                        (num 3))

                  (num 4))))

现在动手！还有哪些种类的测试是我们应该编写的？ Do Now:  Are there other kinds of tests we should have written?

我们只编写了正向测试。对于预期会出错的情况，也可以编写负向测试： We have only written positive  tests. We can also write negative  tests for situations where we expect errors:

(test/exn (parse `{1 + 2}) "")

test/exn 接收一个字符串，它必须是错误消息的子串。上面的测试使用空字符串，而不是诸如 "addition" 这样的字符串，你可能会感到意外。试运行这个例子，探究原因。可以如何改进解析器来解决这个问题？ test/exn  takes a string that must be a substring of the error message. You might be surprised that the test above uses the empty string rather than, say, "addition" . Try out this example to investigate why. How can you improve your parser to address this?

还应检查的情况包括子部分太少或太多。例如，加法被定义为恰好接收两个子表达式。如果源程序中一个都没有，或者有一个、三个、四个……呢？解析所要求的，就是这种细致较真。 Other situations we should check for include there being too few or too many sub-parts. Addition, for instance, is defined to take exactly two sub-expressions. What if a source program contains none, one, three, four, …? This is the kind of pedantry that parsing calls for.

考虑完这些情况，我们就处在一个很理想的位置了，因为 parse 生成的输出可以被 calc 接收。因此，我们可以组合这两个函数！更好的是，可以编写一个辅助函数替我们完成组合： Once we have considered these situations, we’re in a happy place, because parse  produces output that calc  can consume. We can therefore compose the two functions! Better still, we can write a helper function that does it for us:

(run : (S-Exp -> Number))

(define (run s)

  (calc (parse s)))

现在，我们可以用方便得多的方式重写原来的求值器测试： So we can now rewrite our old evaluator tests in a much more convenient way:

(test (run `1) 1)

(test (run `2.3) 2.3)

(test (run `{+ 1 2}) 3)

(test (run `{+ {+ 1 2} 3})

      6)

(test (run `{+ 1 {+ 2 3}})

      6)

(test (run `{+ 1 {+ {+ 2 3} 4}})

      10)

把它与先前的 calc 测试比较一下！ Compare this against the calc  tests we had earlier!

条件式求值 Evaluating Conditionals

到目前为止，我们的语言只有算术。在“神秘语言：条件式”的基础上，现在来研究如何扩展语言，使其也支持条件式。实际语言中的条件表达式可能相当复杂，但就我们的目标而言，拥有三个部分的 if 就足够了：条件、then 分支和 else 分支。稍后，学会如何扩展语言之后，就能看到如何在此之上叠加更复杂的条件表达式。 So far our language has had only arithmetic. Building on Mystery Language: Conditionals, we will now examine how to extend our language to also support conditionals. There can be quite complex conditional expressions in real languages, but for our purposes it will suffice to have an if  with three parts: the conditional, the then-branch, and the else-branch. Later, when we learn how to extend the language, we can see how to layer more sophisticated conditional expressions atop this.

按照 SImPl，我们至少必须做两件事： In SImPl, we have to do at least two things:

  1. 扩展表示表达式的数据类型，使其包括条件式。 Extend the datatype representing expressions to include conditionals.
  2. 扩展求值器，使其能够处理这些新表达式（的表示）。 Extend the evaluator to handle (the representation of) these new expressions.

可选地，如果有解析器，我们还应当 Optionally, if we have a parser, we should also

  1. 扩展解析器，使其能够生成这些新表示。 Extend the parser to produce these new representations.

扩展 AST Extending the AST

由于已经规定条件式有三个部分，我们只需在 AST 中表示这三个部分。这很直接： Because we have fixed our conditionals to have three parts, we just need to represent that in the AST. This is straightforward:

(define-type Exp

  [num (n : Number)]

  [plus (left : Exp) (right : Exp)]

  [cnd (test : Exp) (then : Exp) (else : Exp)])

真正的工作将发生在求值器中。 The real work will happen in the evaluator.

扩展计算器 Extending the Calculator

显然，加入条件式并不改变计算器先前的行为，所以可以保留原有部分，只关注 if 的处理： Clearly, adding conditionals doesn’t change what our calculator previously did, we can leave that intact, and just focus on the handling of if :

(define (calc e)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(num n) n]

    [(plus l r) (+ (calc l) (calc r))]

    [(cnd c t e) …]))

事实上，我们可以递归地求值每一项，以备有用： Indeed, we can recursively evaluate each term, in case it’s useful:

(define (calc e)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(num n) n]

    [(plus l r) (+ (calc l) (calc r))]

    [(cnd c t e) … (calc c) … (calc t) … (calc e) …]))

让我们逐一来看。 Let’s take these one at a time.

但现在遇到了一个问题。调用 (calc c) 的结果是什么？我们预期它是某种布尔值。但语言中还没有布尔值！ But now we run into a problem. What is the result of calling (calc c) ? We expect it to be some kind of Boolean value. But we don’t have  Boolean values in the language!

问题还不止如此。上面，我们同时写了 (calc t) 和 (calc e)。然而，条件式的要点恰恰是，我们不想对两者都求值，而只对其中一个求值。因此，必须根据某种标准选择求值哪一个。 That’s not all. Above, we have written both (calc t)  and (calc e) . However, the whole point of a conditional is that we don’t  want to evaluate both, only one. So we have to pick which one to evaluate based on some criterion.

条件式的设计空间 The Design Space of Conditionals

即便最简单的条件式，也会让我们接触到语言设计中的许多变化。其意图是先对 test-expression 求值；如果结果为真，就（只）对 then-expression 求值，否则就（只）对 else-expression 求值。（通常把这两部分称为分支，因为程序的控制流必须选择其中一个。）然而，即便这样一个简单构造，也会带来至少三个不同且大体独立的设计决策： Even the simplest conditional exposes us to many variations in language design. The intent is that test-expression is evaluated first; if it results in a true value then (only) the then-expression is evaluated, else (only) the else-expression is evaluated. (We usually refer to these two parts as branches , since the program’s control must take one or the other.) However, even this simple construct results in at least three different, mostly independent design decisions:

  1. test-expression 可以得到哪种值？在有些语言中，它们必须是布尔值（两个值，一个表示真，另一个表示假）。在另一些语言中，这个表达式几乎可以求值为任何值，其中某个集合——俗称真值（truthy）——表示真（也就是说，它们导致执行 then-expression），而其余值是假值（falsy），意味着它们导致执行 else-expression。起初，设计一种拥有多个真值和假值的语言，似乎颇有吸引力：毕竟，这看上去能给程序员更多便利，允许在条件式中使用结果非布尔值的函数和表达式。然而，这可能导致不同语言之间出现令人困惑的不一致： What kind of values can the test-expression be? In some languages they must be Boolean values (two values, one representing truth and the other falsehood). In other languages this expression can evaluate to just about any value, with some set—colloquially called truthy —representing truth (i.e., they result in execution of the then-expression) while the remaining ones are falsy , meaning they cause the else-expression to run.



    Initially, it may seem attractive to design a language with several truthy and falsy values: after all, this appears to give the programmer more convenience, permitting non-Boolean-valued functions and expressions to be used in conditionals. However, this can lead to bewildering inconsistencies across languages:

当然，不一定要这么复杂。例如，Scheme 只有一个假值：false 本身（写作 #false）。其他所有值都是真值。对于重视在条件式中允许非布尔值的人来说，这是一种优雅的权衡：这意味着，函数不必担心计算所得的某个类型一致的值会让条件判断反转。（例如，如果函数返回字符串，就不必担心空字符串可能受到与其他所有字符串不同的对待。）注意，部分受到 Scheme 启发的 Ruby 采用了这种简单模型。另一种受到 Scheme 启发的语言 Lua，其假值也同样精简。

Of course, it need not be so complex. Scheme, for instance, has only one value that is falsy: false itself (written as #false ). Every  other value is truthy. For those who value allowing non-Boolean values in conditionals, this represents an elegant trade-off: it means a function need not worry that a type-consistent value resulting from a computation might cause a conditional to reverse itself. (For instance, if a function returns strings, it need not worry that the empty string might be treated differently from every other string.) Note that Ruby, which is inspired in part by Scheme, adopted this simple model. Lua, another Scheme-inspired language, is also spartan in its falsy values.

  1. 分支是什么样的项？有些语言区分语句和表达式；在这样的语言中，设计者必须决定允许其中哪一种。有些语言甚至用两种条件式语法形式来反映这两个选择：例如，在 C 中，if 使用语句（不返回任何值），而“三元运算符”（(...?...:...)）允许表达式并返回一个值。 What kind of terms are the branches? Some languages make a distinction between statements  and expressions ; in such languages, designers need to decide which of these are permitted. In some languages, there are even two syntactic forms of conditional to reflect these two choices: e.g., in C, if  uses statements (and does not return any value) while the “ternary operator” ( (...?...:...) ) permits expressions and returns a value.

  2. 如果分支是表达式，因而允许求值为值，这些值之间有什么关系？许多（但并非所有）具有静态类型系统的语言要求两个分支具有相同类型 [ 👉 ]。没有静态类型系统的语言通常不加限制。 If the branches are expressions and hence allowed to evaluate to values, how do the values relate? Many (but not all) languages with static type systems expect the two branches to have the same type [ 👉 ]. Languages without static type systems usually place no restrictions.

旁注：在撰写本章较早版本时，我偶然发现了 Pyret 编程语言中的一个奇怪错误：所有数字 S 表达式都被解析为 s-num 值，唯独 0 被解析成了 s-sym。最后，Justin Pombrio 报告说：“这是 JavaScript 中一个 if 引起的愚蠢错误，它拿到 0，就以为它是 false。”真是应景。 Aside: While writing an earlier version of this very chapter, I stumbled on a strange bug in the Pyret programming language: all numeric s-expressions parsed as s-num  values except 0 , which parsed as a s-sym . Eventually Justin Pombrio reported: “It’s a silly bug with an if  in JavaScript that’s getting 0  and thinking it’s false.” Seems fitting.

使用真值与假值 Using Truthy-Falsy Values

有些语言使用真值和假值来处理偏函数。无法处理参数时，它们不发出错误信号，而是返回一个假值。例如，在 Racket 中返回 #false、在 Python 中返回 None 作为错误码，而在正常执行时返回一个恰当的值，是很常见的。考虑下面这个 Racket 例子： Some languages use truthy-falsy values to handle partial functions. Instead of signaling an error, they return a falsy value when the argument cannot be handled. For instance, it is common to return #false  in Racket or None  in Python as an error code, and a proper value for normal execution. Consider this Racket example:

(define (g s)

  (+ 1 (or (string->number s) 0)))

这个函数接收一个字符串，它可能表示数字，也可能不表示。如果表示数字，就返回比它大 1 的数字；否则返回 1： This function accepts a string that may or may not represent a number. If it does, it returns one bigger number; otherwise it returns 1 :

(test (g "5") 6)

(test (g "hello") 1)

这之所以可行，是因为 string->number 会返回一个数字，或者在字符串不合法时返回 #false。在 Racket 中，除 #false 之外的所有值都是真值。因此，合法字符串会使 or 的求值短路，而非数字字符串会得到 0。所以，在没有（或曾经没有）正规数据类型构造器的语言中，这些值可以充当一种简便粗略的选项类型。 This works because string->number  returns a number or, if the string is not legal, #false . In Racket, all values other than #false  are truthy. Thus, legitimate strings short-circuit evaluation of the or , while non-numeric strings result in 0 . These therefore serve as a rough-and-ready option types in languages that don’t (or didn’t) have proper datatype constructors.

我们将在本书稍后进一步讨论这个问题 [ 👉 ]。 We will discuss this issue further later in the book [ 👉 ].

实现条件式 Implementing Conditionals

好了，我们有许多决定要做！为了先得到一个可运行的求值器，而不必超出数字的范围，可以使用一种稍有不同的条件构造：检查求值结果是否为某个特殊数字，例如 0。也就是说，我们实际上使用的不是正规的 if，而是一种可以称为 if0 的、只适用于数字的东西。 Okay, so we have many decisions to make! To first get a working evaluator, without having to go beyond numbers, we can use a slightly different conditional construct: one that checks whether evaluates to a special numeric value, such as 0 . That is, instead of a proper if , we really have something we might call if0  that works only for numbers.

如何落实这个选择呢？幸运的是，解释器是用 plait 编写的，而 plait 当然已经有条件式。因此，可以直接复用它： How do we make this choice? Luckily, we’re writing our interpreter in plait, which of course already has a conditional. Therefore, we can just reuse it:

(define (calc e)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(num n) n]

    [(plus l r) (+ (calc l) (calc r))]

    [(cnd c t e) (if (zero? (calc c))

                     (calc t)

                     (calc e))]))

注意，条件式的语义——0 为真，其余一切为假——现在明确地体现在 calc 的函数体中。如果想要不同的语义，应当聚焦并修改的就是程序的这一部分。 Observe that the semantics of the conditional—that 0  is true, and everything else is false—is now made manifest in the body of calc . If we want a different semantics, that’s the part of the program to zero into and change.

这个解决方案，乃至到目前为止的整个求值器，可能让人觉得有点……失望？没错，我们有了数字和条件式，但所做的（基本上）只是把处理交给 plait。对此，有几点想法： This solution, and indeed so far our entire evaluator, might feel a bit… disappointing? We have numbers and conditionals, sure, but all we’ve done is (mostly) deferred to plait to handle these. Here are some thoughts on this:

  1. 确实如此！ This is true!
  2. 也不完全如此。我们有意识地作出了一些决定，比如如何处理条件式。 This is not entirely true. We have made some conscious decisions, like the handling of conditionals.
  3. 事实上，不管是否意识到，我们作出的决定还更多，比如如何处理数字。我们只是恰好把它们交给 plait，但如果愿意，完全可以作出其他决定。 In fact, we have made even more decisions, whether or not we were conscious of them, such as the handling of numbers. We just happened to defer those to plait, but we could have made other decisions if we wanted.
  4. 这种复用，实际上正是解释器力量的一部分：它让你利用已经构建好的特性，而不必从零重新实现一切。 This reuse is actually part of the power  of an interpreter: it lets you exploit features that have already been built instead of having to re-implement all of them from scratch.
  5. 复用宿主语言（这里是 plait），让我们能够聚焦于差异（例如条件式的处理）；如果必须实现一切，这些差异反倒会被淹没。稍后，我们会看到与 plait 语义偏离得更大的情况。 By reusing the host  language (here, plait), we can zero in on the differences (like the handling of conditionals), which would otherwise be lost if we had to implement everything. Later we will see stronger departures from the semantics of plait.

加入布尔值 Adding Booleans

好了，如果想要真正的布尔值，该怎么办？ Okay, so what if we wanted proper Booleans?

同样，按照 SImPl，我们需要修改 AST、求值器和解析器。 Again, to employ SImPl, we need to alter the AST, the evaluator, and the parser.

加入布尔值的方式可以与加入数字类似：使用一个构造器，包裹布尔值在 plait 中的表示。 We can add Booleans much like we did numbers: with a constructor that wraps a plait representation of the Boolean.

(define-type Exp

  [num (n : Number)]

  [bool (b : Boolean)]

  [plus (left : Exp) (right : Exp)]

  [cnd (test : Exp) (then : Exp) (else : Exp)])

务必记住 num 和 bool 构造器代表什么。回想一下，这是抽象语法：我们只是（抽象地）表示用户编写的程序，而不是其求值结果。因此，这些构造器捕获的是源程序中的语法常量：前者如 3.14 和 -1，后者如 #true 和 #false。它们不表示那些会求值为数字或布尔值的复合表达式。目前，一个表达式会求值为什么，只能通过运行来确定。稍后 [ 👉 ]，我们会看到还有其他确定方法！ It’s very important to keep in mind what the num  and bool  constructors stand for. Recall that this is abstract syntax : we are just (abstractly) representing the program that the user wrote , not the result of its evaluation. Therefore, these constructors are capturing syntactic constants  in the source program: values like 3.14  and -1  for the former and #true  and #false  for the latter. They do not  represent compound expressions that will evaluate to  numbers or Booleans. What an expression will evaluate to, for now, can only be determined by running it. Later [ 👉 ], we will see there are other ways of doing it too!

旁注：抽象语法不规定使用哪种具体语法。例如，数字可以写成 3，也可以写成 III。布尔值可以写成 #t、#true、true、True，等等。同一种抽象语法甚至可以有不同的具体语法。这正是抽象语法所提供的抽象！ Aside:  The abstract syntax does not dictate what concrete syntax we use. For instance, we may write numbers as 3  or as III . We might write Boolean values as #t , #true , true , True , …. We may even have different concrete syntaxes for the same abstract syntax. This is precisely the abstraction  that abstract syntax provides!

小菜一碟！这自然提示了求值器中应该怎么做： Easy peasy! This naturally suggests what we should do in the evaluator:

(define (calc e)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(num n) n]

    [(bool b) b]

    [(plus l r) (+ (calc l) (calc r))]

    [(cnd c t e) (if (zero? (calc c))

                     (calc t)

                     (calc e))]))

哦……糟了。这一版 calc 无法通过类型检查，因为我们的计算器应当只返回数字，而不是布尔值！ Oh…oops. This version of calc  doesn’t type-check, because our calculator is supposed to return only numbers, not Booleans!

事实上，我们早该知道这种局面不会一直持续。我们感兴趣的不只是计算器；我们想构建完整的编程语言。它们有各种各样的值，也就是答案：数字、布尔值、字符串、图像、函数，等等。 In fact, we had to know that this couldn’t last. We aren’t interested only in calculators; we want to build full-fledged programming languages. They have a wide range of values, i.e., answers: numbers, Boolean, strings, images, functions, and more.

Value 数据类型 The Value Datatype

因此，首先需要定义一个数据类型，反映求值器可能生成的不同种类的值。我们将遵循一个约定，把返回类型的构造器命名为 …V，以与输入区分。相应地，把输入命名为 …E（表示表达式），以与输出区分。 Therefore, we first need to define a datatype that reflects the different kinds of values that an evaluator can produce. We will follow a convention and call the return type constructors …V  to distinguish from the inputs. Dually, we’ll call the inputs …E  (for expressions) to distinguish from the outputs.

首先，给表达式重新命名： First we’ll rename our expressions:

(define-type Exp

  [numE (n : Number)]

  [boolE (b : Boolean)]

  [plusE (left : Exp) (right : Exp)]

  [cndE (test : Exp) (then : Exp) (else : Exp)])

（除了构造器名称之外，没有任何变化）。 (nothing has changed other than the names  of the constructors).

现在，引入一个 Value 数据类型，表示求值器能够生成的答案类型： Now we introduce a Value  datatype to represent the types of answers our evaluator can produce:

(define-type Value

  [numV (the-number : Number)]

  [boolV (the-boolean : Boolean)])

更新求值器的类型： We update the type of our evaluator:

(calc : (Exp -> Value))

而前面的部分很容易： and the early parts are easy:

(define (calc e)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(numE n) (numV n)]

    [(boolE b) (boolV b)]

    …))

更新求值器 Updating the Evaluator

现在，假设尝试使用现有代码： Now suppose we try to use our existing code:

[(plusE l r) (+ (calc l) (calc r))]

这里有两个问题。首先，不能返回一个数字；必须返回一个 numV： This has two problems. The first is we can’t return a number; we have to return a numV :

[(plusE l r) (numV (+ (calc l) (calc r)))]

但现在遇到了一个更微妙的问题。类型检查器对这个程序并不满意。为什么？ But now we run into a subtler problem. The type-checker is not happy with this program. Why?

因为 calc 的结果是一个 Value，而 + 只接收 Number。事实上，类型检查器正迫使我们在这里作出决定：如果 + 的某一边没有求值为数字，会怎么样？ Because the result of calc  is a Value , and +  consumes only Number s. Indeed, the type checker is forcing us to make a decision  here: what happens if one of the sides of +  does not evaluate to a number?

首先，构建一个抽象来处理这个问题，以保持解释器核心相对简洁： First, let’s build an abstraction to handle this, so that we can keep the core of the interpreter relatively clean:

[(plusE l r) (add (calc l) (calc r))]

现在，可以把 + 的所有求值逻辑交给 add。接下来必须作出一个语义决定。应该允许“相加”两个布尔值吗？把数字加到布尔值上，或反过来，又如何？虽然 SMoL 在这里没有完全一致的决定——有些语言非常严格，另一些则十分宽松——但最不偏离标准的策略，是要求两边都求值为数字，可以这样表达： Now we can defer all the logic of evaluating +  to add . Now we have to make a semantic decision . Should we be allowed to “add” two Boolean values? What about adding a number to a Boolean or vice versa? Though there isn’t quite a SMoL decision here—some languages are very strict while others are very permissive—the least-non-standard policy is to require both branches to evaluate to numbers, which we would express as follows:

(define (add v1 v2)

  (type-case Value v1

    [(numV n1)

     (type-case Value v2

       [(numV n2) (numV (+ n1 n2))]

       [else (error '+ "expects RHS to be a number")])]

    [else (error '+ "expects LHS to be a number")]))

注意，这些 else 子句很容易表示其他决定。通过各种可用选择，我们可以在这里嵌入一整族神秘语言！ Observe that these else  clauses can easily represent other decisions. We can embed an entire family of mystery languages in the different choices available!

练习：为什么把 numV 构造器写在 add 中，而不是 calc 中？ Exercise:  Why did we write the numV constructor in add  rather than in calc ?

专业小窍门：你刚刚加入了一大块复杂代码。现在正是测试求值器的好时机。有两件事值得考虑： Pro Tip:  You’ve just added a complex chunk of code. Now would be a very good time to test your evaluator. Here are two things to consider:

  1. 目前，条件式的代码也无法通过类型检查。你可能会觉得，把整个右侧替换为语义不正确但类型正确的东西（如 (numV 0)）很方便，这样可以恢复一个能运行的求值器。 Right now the code for conditionals also  does not type-check. You may find it convenient to replace the entire RHS with something semantically incorrect but type-correct, like (numV 0) , so you restore your working evaluator.

  2. 别忘了测试错误情况！可以使用 test/exn。例如：(test/exn (calc (plusE (numE 4) (boolE #false))) "RHS") Don’t forget to test for the error cases! You would do so using test/exn . For instance:



    (test/exn (calc (plusE (numE 4) (boolE #false))) "RHS")

现在把注意力转向条件式（构造器名称已经更新）： Let’s now turn our attention to the conditional (with the constructor name updated):

[(cndE c t e) …]

核心逻辑显然应该类似：检查条件的某个性质，并据此只对另外两个子句中的一个求值。同样，必须决定如何处理条件：严格要求布尔值，还是采用真值/假值的判断？我们仍然可以把它交给一个辅助函数： The core logic must clearly be similar: check something about the condition, and based on it, evaluate only one of the other two clauses. Once again, we have to make decisions about how we handle the conditional: should we strictly require a Boolean value, or should we make a truthy/falsy decision? We can again defer that to a helper function:

    [(cndE c t e) (if (boolean-decision (calc c))

                      (calc t)

                      (calc e))]))

同样，最不偏离标准、也为后续内容铺路的策略，是严格要求布尔值： Again, the least non-standard policy, and one that sets up later material, is to be strict about requiring a Boolean:

(define (boolean-decision v)

  (type-case Value v

    [(boolV b) b]

    [else (error 'if "expects conditional to evaluate to a boolean")]))

不过，同样从严格的解释出发，可以看出，如果我们忍不住想设计更宽松的语义，可以在哪里放宽要求：替换 else 子句即可。 But again, starting from a strict interpretation, we can see where we can give in to any urges we feel to design a more liberal semantics: by replacing the else  clause.

顺便注意，对于条件式，我们的做法与加法不同。对于 add，我们对两边都求值，并把相应的 Value 交给它。若对条件式也这么做，那就糟透了，因为条件式的全部意义就是不对其中一个分支求值！我们本可以把分支的 AST 传给辅助函数，但上面的做法同样很好：它将语义的变化局限在辅助函数中，同时把预期不会改变的部分（条件语法导致条件求值这一事实）保留在求值器核心。 Observe, by the way, that we did something different with conditionals than we did for addition. With add , we evaluated both branches and gave it their corresponding Value s. It would be a terrible idea to do that with conditionals, because the entire point of a conditional is to not  evaluate one of the branches! We could have sent the ASTs for the branches to a helper function, but what we have done above also works well: it localizes the variation  in the semantics to the helper function, but keeps what is not expected to change (the fact that a conditional syntax leads to a conditional evaluation) in the core of the evaluator.

局部绑定求值 Evaluating Local Binding

大多数编程语言都有某种局部绑定的概念。这里有两个词，我们把它们分开来看： Most programming languages have some notion of local binding . There are two words there, which we’ll tease apart:

  • 绑定，指的是把名称与值关联起来。例如，调用函数时，调用这一动作会将形式参数与实际值关联（“绑定”）起来。 Binding  means to associate names with values. For instance, when we call a function, the act of calling associates (“binds”) the formal parameters with the actual values.
  • 局部，指的是它们被限制在程序的某个区域内，在该区域之外不可用。 Local  means they are limited to some region of the program, and not available outside that region.

例如，在许多语言中，可以写出类似这样的代码 For instance, in many languages we can write something like

fun f(x):

  y = 2

  x + y

这似乎很清楚。但下面这个程序更微妙： This seems clear enough. But here is a more subtle program:

fun f(x):

  for(y from 0 to 10):

    print(x + y)

  y

这样合法吗？这取决于 y 是否仍然“活着”、“活动着”、“可见”，或者你喜欢的任何其他说法；形式化地说，取决于 y 是否在作用域中。具体来说，我们会问，最后那个 y 是否是 for 中所建立绑定的一个受绑定实例。 Is that legal? It depends on whether the y  is still “alive” or “active” or “visible” or whatever other phrase you would like; formally, we would say, it depends on whether y  is in scope . Specifically, we’d ask whether the last y  is a bound  instance of the binding  that takes place in the for .

这很复杂！许多语言的行为相当古怪、复杂，而且肯定不直观，你会在神秘语言中看到。这些古怪行为其实并不属于 SMoL；真要说的话，它们违背了 SMoL。 This is complicated! Many languages do rather odd, complicated, and certainly unintuitive things, as you will see from Mystery Languages. These odd things are not really part of SMoL; if anything, they are a violation of it.

局部绑定的语法 A Syntax for Local Binding

问题有一部分实际上在于语法。写出上面这样的程序时，y 的作用域（也就是 y 被绑定的区域）没有明确的起点和终点。这其实正是括号语法的一大优点：它暗示了一个明确的区域（括号之间）。当然，我们有责任确保变量实际上就是在这个区域被绑定（不过，再过一会儿就会发现，这并非那么简单）。 Part of the problem is actually syntactic. When we write a program like the above, there’s no clear beginning or ending of the scope of y  (i.e., the region where y  is bound). This is actually a great virtue of parenthetical syntax: it suggests  a clear region (between the parentheses). Of course, we have a responsibility to make sure that that’s where the variable is  actually bound (though this is something that we’ll find, in a little while, is not so trivial).

仿照 Racket 的语法，我们将在语言中加入一个新构造。到了这一步，要记住完整语法已经有点困难了，所以我们会使用一种叫作 BNF 的记法（Backus-Naur Form，即巴科斯—诺尔范式的缩写）。先从算术语言开始： Following the syntax of Racket, we’ll add a new construct to our language. At this point it’s getting a bit tricky to keep track of the full syntax, so we’ll use a notation called BNF (short for Backus-Naur Form). Let’s start with our arithmetic language:

<expr> ::= <num>

         | {+ <expr> <expr>}

它读作：“把（::=）expr（expression，即表达式的缩写）定义为一个数字，或者（|）由左花括号（{）、加号（+）、一个 expr、另一个 expr 和右花括号构成的表层语法。”BNF 通过具体语法，为描述语言的文法提供了一种方便的记法，而我们的抽象语法通常会以非常自然的方式，与 BNF 直接对应。（不过请注意，在 BNF 中，只需说每个子表达式都是一个 expr，因为要正确构造程序，只需知道这些。但在 AST 中，我们会给各部分起不同名称，以区分它们。） which reads as “define ( ::= ) expr  (short for expression) to be either a number or ( | ) the surface syntax consisting of an opening brace ( { ), a plus sign ( + ), an expr , another expr , and a closing brace”. BNF gives us a convenient notation for the grammar  of a language through its concrete syntax, and our abstract syntax will usually correspond very directly to the BNF in a very natural manner. (Observe, however, that in the BNF, we simply say that each sub-expression is an expr , because that’s all we need to know to properly form programs. However, in the AST, we give the parts different names to tell them apart.)

记法：BNF 分为终结符和非终结符。非终结符是像上面的 expr 和 num 这样的占位符：它们代表许多可能性（上面的 expr 目前可以替换为两种可能之一，而 num 的写法则有许多种）。之所以这样命名，是因为文法不会在这里“终结”：这个名称是一个可以（而且必须）进一步展开的占位符。 Notation:  BNF is divided into terminals  and non-terminals . Non-terminals are placeholders like expr  and num  above: they stand for many more possibilities (an expr  above can be replaced with one of two possibilities (for now), while there are many possible ways to write num s). They are given this name because the grammar doesn’t “terminate” here: the name is a place-holder that can (and must) be further expanded.

惯例是把非终结符写在 < 尖括号 > 中。相比之下，终结符是具体语法，比如上面的 {、} 和 +。之所以叫终结符，是因为它们就代表自身，不能再展开。有时也称它们为字面量，因为必须按所示的字面形式书写。因此，它们周围不加任何装饰性符号。一切都按字面书写，除非它是非终结符；若是非终结符，则按照该非终结符的定义，用某种东西替换。 The convention is to write non-terminals inside < pointy brackets > . Terminals, in contrast, are concrete syntax, like { , } , and +  above. They are so-called because they stand for themselves and can’t be expanded further. They are sometimes also called literals , because they must be written literally as shown. For this reason, they are not surrounded by any decorative symbols. Everything is written literally unless it’s a non-terminal, in which case it’s replaced by something according to the definition of the non-terminal.

现在可以定义一种扩展后的语言： Now we can define an extended language:
