<expr> ::= <num>

         | {+ <expr> <expr>}

         | {let1 {<var> <expr>} <expr>}

也就是说，我们加入了一个新语言构造 let1，它有三个部分：一个变量（var）和两个表达式（两个 expr）。 That is, we’re adding a new language construct, let1 , which has three parts: a variable ( var ) and two expressions (the two expr ’s).

局部绑定的含义 The Meaning of Local Binding

现在动手！下面是这个新构造的一些例子；你预期它们各自得到什么结果？ Do Now:  Here are some examples of this new construct; what do you expect  each one to produce?

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ x x}}

{let1 {x 1}

  {let1 {y 2}

    {+ x y}}}

{let1 {x 1}

  {let1 {y 2}

    {let1 {x 3}

      {+ x y}}}}

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ x

     {let1 {x 2} x}}}

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ {let1 {x 2} x}

     x}}

x

现在动手！哦，你发现什么了吗？上面的程序没有一个在语法上合法！为什么？ Do Now: Oh, did you notice something? None of the above programs is syntactically legal! Why?

这是因为还没有变量的语法。我们的语法允许绑定变量，却不允许使用变量。因此，必须修正这一点： It’s because there is no syntax yet for variables. Our syntax permits us to bind  variables but not to use  them. So we have to fix that:

<expr> ::= <num>

         | {+ <expr> <expr>}

         | {let1 {<var> <expr>} <expr>}

         | <var>

 

现在，上面的项在语法上都有效了，可以回到它们应该求值为什么的问题。 Now the above terms are all syntactically valid, so we can go back to the question of what they should evaluate to.

前两个程序相当明显： The first two programs are pretty obvious:

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ x x}}

应当求值为 2，而 should evaluate to 2, and

{let1 {x 1}

  {let1 {y 2}

    {+ x y}}}

应当求值为 3。 should evaluate to 3.

这个程序呢？ How about this program?

{let1 {x 1}

  {let1 {y 2}

    {let1 {x 3}

      {+ x y}}}}

这里可以看到括号记法的优势。在更常规的语法中，它可能对应于 Here we see the advantage of the parenthetical notation. In a more conventional syntax, this might correspond to

x = 1

y = 2

x = 3

x + y

其中可能发生各种事情：可能有两个不同的 x；可能先绑定一个 x，再修改它；在某些语言中，x 的引入还可能被“提升”，使哪个 x 最新变得不再清楚。但采用我们的括号语法，所需的作用域就相当明确了。为了确定值，可以依靠老朋友——替换。不过，替换外层 x 时，我们期望在内层 x 开始的位置停止：也就是说，内层 x 遮蔽外层 x。因此，结果应该是 5。 where any number of things could happen: we might have two different x ’s; we might have an x  bound and then modified; and in some languages, an introduction of x  could be “lifted” so that it’s no longer clear which x  is most recent. With our parenthetical syntax, though, it’s pretty clear what scopes we want. To determine the value, we can rely on our old friend, substitution. However, when we substitute the outer x , we expect that to stop at the point where the inner x  begins: that is, the inner x   shadows  the outer one. Hence, the result should be 5 .

现在动手！上面的例子不太有意思，因为外层 x 根本没有被使用。可以写出什么样的程序，让其中有两个对 x 的 let 绑定，并且能清楚看出确实有两个 x？ Do Now: The example above is uninteresting in that the outer x  never sees any use. What kind of program might we write that has two let  bindings of x  that lets us clearly see that there are two x ’s?

下面这个程序就展示了这一点： That’s what this program shows:

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ x

     {let1 {x 2} x}}}

 

看来相当清楚，加法左边的 x 应该是 1，而右边表达式中的 x 应当被遮蔽，因此应求值为 2。所以和应当是 3。顺便说一下，在这种情况下 DrRacket 很有用，因为可以用 #lang racket 写一个等价表达式—— It seems fairly clear that the left x  in the addition should be 1 , while x  in the right expression should be shadowed and hence should evaluate to 2 . The sum should therefore be 3 . Incidentally, DrRacket is useful in such cases, because we can write an equivalent expression in #lang racket—

(let ([x 1])

  (+ x

     (let ([x 2])

       x)))

——然后将鼠标悬停在最后一个 x 上，DrRacket（对于 Racket，这是一种相当理想的 SMoL 形式）就会自动画出一条蓝色箭头，标明变量的绑定位置： —and hover over the last x , and DrRacket (for Racket, which represents a fairly ideal form of SMoL) will automatically draw a blue arrow showing where the variable is bound:

现在来看一个更复杂的例子： Now for a more complex example:

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ {let1 {x 2} x}

     x}}

这里，借助替换来确定答案尤其有用。同样，左边表达式中的 x 被遮蔽，因而应为 2，这似乎很清楚。当然，关键问题是，加法右侧（也就是最后一行）的 x 怎么办？ Here, it’s especially useful to turn to substitution to determine the answer. Again, it seems clear that x  in the left expression is shadowed and hence should be 2 . The big question, of course, is what about the x  on the right hand side of the addition (i.e., on the last line)?

在这里，常规文本语法再次充满歧义：左边的 Here, again, conventional textual syntax is fraught with ambiguity: is

x = 2

究竟是绑定一个新的 x，还是修改外层 x？这是两件完全不同的事！但使用我们的语法，就清楚得多：应该是前者，而非后者。因此，通过替换，外层 x 被替换为 1，得到 on the left a binding  of a new x  or a  modification  of the outer x ? Those are two very different things! But with our syntax it’s much clearer that it should  be the former, not the latter. Thus, by substitution, the outer x  is replaced by 1 , giving

{+ {let1 {x 2} x}

   1}

在其中再做一次替换，得到 in which we perform one more substitution, producing

{+ 2

   1}

所以结果是 3。这次，DrRacket 尤其有助于确认这一点： and hence 3 . This time, DrRacket is especially useful confirmation:

这样就只剩一个程序了： That leaves just one program:

x

由于 x 没有在任何地方绑定，这就是一个语法错误。 Because x  is not bound anywhere, this is just a syntax error.

静态作用域 Static Scoping

这个程序 The program

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ {let1 {x 2} x}

     x}}

为我们引出了一个非常重要的概念：事实上，它是 SMoL 背后的核心思想之一。那就是，一个变量的绑定由它在源程序中的位置决定，而不是由程序的执行顺序决定。也就是说，无论求值之前发生了哪些其他绑定，最后一行的 x 都由同一位置绑定——因而获得相同的值。为了更好地理解这一点，来看一系列逐步变化的程序： introduces us to a very important concept: indeed, one of the central ideas behind SMoL. This is that a variable’s binding is determined by its position in the source program , and not  by the order of the program’s execution . That is, the x  on the last line is bound by the same place—and hence obtains the same value—irrespective of other bindings that took place before it was evaluated. To understand this better, let’s see a progression of programs:

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ {let1 {x 2} x}

     x}}

你可能觉得，它得到 3 还是 4 都没关系。那这个呢？ You might think it’s okay whether it produces 3  or 4 . How about this?

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ {if true

         {let1 {x 2} x}

         4}

      x}}

你应该预期它得到同样的结果：条件总为真，显然我们总会对内层绑定求值，所以它的答案应该与前一个程序相同。但这个呢？ You should expect the same out of this: the conditional is always true, so clearly we are always going to evaluate the inner binding, so its answer should be the same as for the previous program. But how about this?

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ {if true

         4

          {let1 {x 2} x} }

      x}}

现在你可能没那么确定了。既然条件分支从不执行，你大概不希望内层绑定产生影响。也就是说，你愿意让程序的控制流影响绑定。乍听之下这很合理，但现在这个程序又如何？ Now you might not be so sure. Since the conditional is never taken, you probably don’t want the inner binding to have an influence. That is, you are willing to let the program’s control flow influence the bindings . On its face that sounds reasonable, but now how about this program?

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ {if {random}

         4

         {let1 {x 2} x}}

      x}}

或者 or

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ {if {moon-is-currently-full}

         4

         {let1 {x 2} x}}

      x}}

你能接受绑定结构每两周变化一次吗？那这个版本呢： Are you okay with the binding structure changing every two weeks? What about this version:

{let1 {x 1}

  {+ {if {moon-is-currently-full}

         4

         {let1 { y  2} x}}

      y }}

这样，取决于月相，程序要么得到一个答案，要么产生未绑定变量错误。 Then, depending on the phase of the moon, the program either produces an answer or results in an unbound-variable error.

上面这一系列代码牵涉到几个不同的概念。其中一些——让控制流决定绑定——是动态作用域的变体。动态作用域是编程语言中一个毫无疑问的错误设计决策。它有一段漫长而不光彩的历史：最初的 Lisp 就采用了它，直到十多年后，Scheme 才修正这个问题。（遗憾的是，不了解历史的人注定要重蹈覆辙：早期的 Python 和 JavaScript 也有某种形式的动态作用域。要将其移除，费了九牛二虎之力。）在上面的程序中，仅凭观察，我们无法确定程序的绑定结构。 There are a few different concepts caught up in the above sequence of code. Some of these—letting the control flow determine binding—are variants of dynamic scope . Dynamic scope is one of the unambiguously wrong  design decisions in programming languages. It has a long and sordid history: the original Lisp had it, and it was not until over a decade later that Scheme fixed it. (Unfortunately, those who don’t know history are doomed to repeat it: early versions of Python and JavaScript also had forms of dynamic scope. Taking it back out has been a herculean effort.) In the programs above, we can’t be sure about the binding structure of our programs just by looking at them.

然而，“观察”程序的不只有我们：编程工具也会！例如，程序重构工具需要知道绑定结构：即使一个简单的“变量重命名”工具，也需要知道该重命名哪些变量。在 DrRacket 中，没有歧义，所以变量重命名能正确工作。其他语言却未必如此：例如，可以参看这篇关于 Python 语义的论文的附录 2。 However, we aren’t the only entities that “look” at programs: so do our programming tools! For instance, a program refactoring tool needs to know binding structure: even a simple “variable renaming” tool needs to know which variables to rename. In DrRacket, there is no ambiguity, so variable renaming works correctly. This is not true in other languages: see, for instance, Appendix 2 of this paper  on the semantics of Python.

相比之下，我们想要的是这样一个系统：沿着 AST 的结构就能确定绑定，也就是所谓静态作用域。这样，就不必知道程序将如何运行——运行可能涉及随机数或月相——也能理解作用域结构。例如，这让 IDE 能在受绑定实例与建立绑定的实例之间画出箭头，并对它们重命名。静态作用域是 SMoL 的一个界定性特征。 In contrast, what we want is a system where we can determine the binding by following the structure of the AST: what is called static scope . Then we don’t need to know how a program will run—which may involve references to random numbers or phases of the moon—to understand the scoping structure. This enables, for instance, an IDE to draw arrows between bound and binding instances, and to rename them. Static scope is a defining characteristic of SMoL.

早期语言采用动态作用域，是因为在实现中很容易得到它：它是默认行为。正如将要看到的，实现静态作用域需要我们多费一点工夫。 Early languages had dynamic scope because it was easy to obtain in the implementation: it was the default behavior. We have to work a bit harder to implement static scope, as we will see.

局部绑定的求值器 An Evaluator for Local Binding

既然已看清想要的行为，就应该实现它。也就是说，我们将扩展计算器来处理局部绑定（你很可能也希望自己的计算器拥有这个特性）。为了体现计算器正在成长，从现在起，我们称它为解释器，在代码中缩写为 interp。 Now that we’ve seen what behavior we want, we should implement it. That is, we’ll extend our calculator to handle local binding (a feature you may well have wished your calculator had). To reflect that our calculator is growing up, from now on we’ll call it an interpreter , abbreviated in code to interp .

先从新的 AST 开始。为简单起见，忽略条件式，反正它与处理局部绑定的目标是正交的。回想一下，我们在 BNF 中增加了两个新分支，因此 AST 中也需要两个相应的新分支： Let’s start with the new AST. For simplicity, we’ll ignore conditionals, which are anyway orthogonal to our goal of handling local binding. Recall that we added two new branches to the BNF, so we’ll want two new corresponding branches to the AST:

(define-type Exp

  [numE (n : Number)]

  [plusE (left : Exp) (right : Exp)]

  [varE (name : Symbol)]

  [let1E (var : Symbol)

         (value : Exp)

         (body : Exp)])

还可以把之前的计算器复制过来，但很快就会遇到麻烦： We can also copy over our previous calculator, but we pretty quickly run into trouble:

(define (interp e)

  (type-case (Exp) e

    [(numE n) n]

    [(varE s) …]

    [(plusE l r) (+ (interp l) (interp r))]

    [(let1E var val body) …]))

遇到 let1E 时，该做什么？同样，遇到变量时，又该做什么？事实上，这两者应该紧密相连：前者引入的变量绑定，应当替换后者中的变量使用。 What do we do when we encounter a let1E ? For that matter, what do we do when we encounter a variable? In fact, these two should be intimately connected: the variable binding introduced by the former should substitute the variable use in the latter.

缓存替换 Caching Substitution

我们反复地——也理所当然地——借助替换来理解程序应当如何工作，事实上稍后还会再次这样做。但把替换当作求值技术却很麻烦。它要求不断改写程序文本，每次变量绑定所需的时间都与程序大小成线性关系（而程序可能相当大）。大多数实际语言实现并不是这样工作的。 We repeatedly—and rightly—refer back to substitution to understand how programs should work, and indeed will do so again later. But substitution as an evaluation  technique is messy. This requires us to constantly keep rewriting the program text, which takes time linear in the size of the program (which can get quite large) for every  variable binding. Most real language implementations do not work this way.

相反，可以考虑用空间换时间：使用少量额外空间，省下大量时间。也就是说，把替换缓存在一个称为环境的数据结构中。环境记录名称及其对应的值：也就是说，它是键值对的集合。因此，每当遇到绑定，就记住它的值；遇到变量时，就查找它的值。 Instead, we might think of employing a space-time tradeoff: we’ll use a little extra space to save ourselves a whole lot of time. That is, we’ll cache  the substitution in a data structure called the environment . An environment records names and their corresponding values: that is, it’s a collection of key-value pairs. Thus, whenever we encounter a binding we remember its value, and when we encounter a variable, we look up its value.

旁注：和所有缓存一样，我们希望它只在某个维度上改善性能，而不改变含义。也就是说，我们不再希望用替换来定义如何生成答案。但仍然希望它告诉我们应当生成什么答案。这一点在下面会很重要。 Aside: A s with all caches, we want them to only improve performance along a dimension, not change the meaning. That is, we no longer want substitution to define how  we produce an answer. But, we still want it to tell us what  answer to produce. This will become important below.

我们将用哈希表来表示环境： We will use a hash table to represent the environment:

(define-type-alias Env (Hashof Symbol Value))

(define mt-env (hash empty)) ;; "empty environment"

解释器需要实际接收一个环境作为形式参数，用来取代替换。因此： We will need the interpreter to actually take an environment as a formal parameter, to use in place of substitution. Thus:

(interp : (Exp Env -> Value))

(define (interp e nv) …)

现在，遇到变量时会怎样？我们尝试在环境中查找它。查找可能成功，也可能像上面最后一个例子那样失败。我们会使用 hash-ref，它在哈希表中查找键，并返回 Optionof 类型，以表达失败的可能。可以把它封装进一个之后会反复用到的函数： Now what happens when we encounter a variable? We try to look it up in the environment. That may succeed or, in the case of our last example above, fail. We will use hash-ref , which looks up keys in hash tables, and returns an Optionof  type to account for the possibility of failure. We can encapsulate it in a function that we will repeatedly find useful:

(define (lookup (s : Symbol) (n : Env))

  (type-case (Optionof Value) (hash-ref n s)

    [(none) (error s "not bound")]

    [(some v) v]))

如果查找成功，我们就要那个被包裹在 some 中的查找结果。这个函数能让解释器保持非常简洁易读： In the event the lookup succeeds, then we want the value found, which is wrapped in some . This function  enables our interpreter to stay very clean and readable:

    [(varE s) (lookup s nv)]

最后，可以着手处理 let1 了。这里会发生什么？我们必须 Finally, we are ready to tackle let1 . What happens here? We must

  • 对表达式的主体求值，所用的 evaluate the body of the expression, in
  • 环境已经扩展，其中 an environment that has been extended, with
  • 新的名称 the new name
  • 绑定到了它的值。 bound to its value.

呼！ Phew!

幸运的是，这并没有听起来那么糟。同样，一个函数会很有帮助： Fortunately, this isn’t as bad as it sounds. Again, a function will help a lot:

(extend : (Env Symbol Value -> Env))

(define (extend old-env new-name value)

  (hash-set old-env new-name value))

有了它，就能清楚看出结构： With this, we can see the structure clearly:

    [(let1E var val body)

     (let ([new-env (extend nv

                            var

                            (interp val nv))])

（注意，我们在 plait 中使用 let 来定义 let1。之后还会看到更多这种情况……） (Observe that we used let  in plait to define let1 . We’ll see more of this…)

总之，核心解释器现在是： In sum, our core interpreter is now:

(define (interp e nv)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(numE n) n]

    [(varE s) (lookup s nv)]

    [(plusE l r) (+ (interp l nv) (interp r nv))]

    [(let1E var val body)

     (let ([new-env (extend nv

                            var

                            (interp val nv))])

       (interp body new-env))]))

练习： Exercise:  

  1. 如果上面没有调用 (interp val nv)，会怎样？ What if we had not called (interp val nv)  above?
  2. 如果调用 interp 时使用 nv 而不是 new-env，会怎样？ What if we’d used nv  instead of new-env  in the call to interp ?
  3. 解释器中还有其他因复制之前的内容而产生的错误吗？ Are there any other errors in the interpreter based on copying what we had before?
  4. 我们似乎一直扩展环境，却从不移除任何东西。这样可以吗？如果不可以，就应该会引发错误。什么程序能展示这个错误？它实际上确实会出错吗？（如果不会，为什么？） We seem to extend the environment but never remove anything from it. Is that okay? If not, it should cause an error. What program would demonstrate this error, and does it actually do so? (If not, why not?)

至此，我们第一个有意思的“编程语言”就完成了。我们已经被迫处理了一些相当微妙的作用域问题，以及如何解释它们。从这里起，事情只会越来越有趣！ This concludes our first interesting “programming language”. We have already been forced to deal with some fairly subtle questions of scope, and with how to interpret them. Things will only get more interesting from here!

函数求值 Evaluating Functions

现在有了算术和条件式，让我们继续加入函数，创建一种完整的编程语言。 Now that we have arithmetic and conditionals, let’s proceed to creating a full-fledged programming language by adding functions.

语言中的函数 Functions in the Language

可以从许多角度考虑如何给语言加入函数。例如，许多语言有顶层函数；比如： There are many ways to think about adding functions to the language. Many languages, for instance, have top-level functions; e.g.:

fun f(x):

  x + x

确实，有些语言（例如 C）只有顶层函数。不过，大多数现代语言都能够在顶层之外编写函数：例如， Indeed, some languages (such as C) only  have top-level functions. Most modern languages, however, have the ability to write functions outside the top-level: e.g.,

fun f(x):

  fun sq(y):

    y * y

  sq(x) + sq(x)

甚至能返回这些函数，还允许以匿名方式编写它们。由于几乎每一种现代语言都支持这一点，我们将把它视为 SMoL 的一个组成部分。事实上，有了这种能力，就不再真正需要专门的具名函数构造了：我们可以改写成 and even to return  those functions, and even to allow them to be written anonymously . Since just about every modern language supports it, we’ll think of this as a component of SMoL. Indeed, with such a facility, we don’t really need a named function construct per se: we could instead have written

fun f(x):

  sq = lam(y): y * y

  sq(x) + sq(x)

接着，也可以用名称绑定和 lam 来替代 f。 And in turn we can replace f  with a name-binding and lam , too.

扩展表示 Extending the Representation

因此，来想想在 SMoL 中对作为值的函数求值，需要做些什么。函数本身不必有名称，因为命名可以通过 let1 完成。为简单起见，假设所有函数都只接收一个参数；将其扩展到多个参数，留作练习。 Therefore, let’s think about what it takes to evaluate functions-as-values to SMoL. We don’t need functions to inherently have a name, because naming can be done by let1 .  We’ll assume, for simplicity, that all functions take only one argument; extending this to multiple arguments is left as an exercise.

练习：把函数从只有一个参数扩展到多个参数时，可能需要处理哪些问题？ Exercise:  What issues might we have to deal with when we extend functions from having one argument only to having multiple arguments?

首先，需要扩展抽象语法。 First, we need to extend our abstract syntax.

现在动手！需要向抽象语法中加入几个新构造？ Do Now:  How many new constructs do we need to add to the abstract syntax?

你可能记得，加入 let1 时，只增加一个构造还不够；需要两个：一个用于变量绑定，一个用于变量使用。向语言中加入值时，经常会看到这种模式。对于任何一种新值，通常都应有一种或多种构造它的方式，以及一种或多种使用它的方式。（即便算术也是如此：数字常量是构造数字的方式，算术运算则使用它们——但也会构造它们。） When we added let1 , you may recall that it didn’t suffice to add one construct; we needed two: one for variable binding  and one for variable use . You’ll often see this pattern when adding values to the language. For any new kind of value,  you can expect to see one or more ways to make  it and one or more ways to use  it. (Even arithmetic: numeric constants were a way to make them, arithmetic operations consumed them—but also made them.)

函数也一样，我们需要一种方式来同时表示 Likewise with functions, we need a way to represent both

lam(x): x * x

用于定义新函数的构造，以及 for defining new functions, and

sq(3)

用于使用函数的构造。 to use them.

术语：在更高级的书籍中，有时会看到“引入”和“消去”这两个术语（形式上正确，但或许稍有些令人困惑）：引入带来新概念，消去则使用它们。因此，lam 引入新函数，而应用则消去它们。 Terminology:  In more advanced texts, you will sometimes see the (formally correct, but perhaps slightly confusing) terms introduction  and elimination : introduction brings the new concept in, elimination uses them. Thus, the lam  introduces new functions, and an application eliminates them.

因此，我们把 We therefore add

  [lamE (var : Symbol) (body : Exp)]

  [appE (fun : Exp) (arg : Exp)]

加入 AST。 to our AST.

假设已经扩展了解析器，使下面这样的程序合法： Let’s assume we’ve already extended our parser, so that programs like the following are legal:

{let1 {f {lam x {+ x x}}}

      {f 3}}

{let1 {x 3}

      {let1 {f {lam y {+ x y}}}

            {f 3}}}

它们分别解析成 These parse, respectively, into

(let1E 'f (lamE 'x (plusE (varE 'x) (varE 'x)))

       (appE (varE 'f) (numE 3)))

(let1E 'x (numE 3)

       (let1E 'f (lamE 'y (plusE (varE 'x) (varE 'y)))

              (appE (varE 'f) (numE 3))))

并且都应求值为 6。 and should both evaluate to 6 .

函数求值 Evaluating Functions

现在来考虑求值器，到了这一步，可以认为它正演变成一个完整的解释器。 Now let’s think about the evaluator, which by now we can think of as turning into a full-blown interpreter.

先从（几乎）最简单的一种新程序开始： Let’s start with the (almost) simplest kind of new program:

{lam x {+ x x}}

它表示为 which is represented as

(lamE 'x (plusE (varE 'x) (varE 'x)))

现在动手！我们希望这个程序求值为什么？从类型的角度想一想！ Do Now:  What do we want this program to evaluate to? Think in terms of types!

记住，calc 生成数字。上面的表达式求值为哪个数字？你期望它生成哪个数字？ Remember that calc  produces numbers. What number  does the above expression evaluate to? What number do you expect  it to produce?

如果真要勉强找个说法，可以编造一种把它编码成数字的方法，或者使用内存中的某个数字。但这两者都不是我们期望的！来看看其他一些语言怎么做： If we really want to stretch our credibility, we could either make up an encoding of it in a number, or use a number in memory. But neither of these is what we would expect ! Let’s look at what some other languages do:

> (lambda (x) (+ x x))

#<procedure>

> (number? (lambda (x) (+ x x)))

#f

>>> lambda x: x + x

<function <lambda> at 0x108fd16a8>

>>> isinstance(lambda x: x + x, numbers.Number)

False

Racket 和 Python 的做法一致：创建匿名函数的结果是函数这一类值，而不是数字。这意味着，必须扩大 interp 可以生成的值的种类。 Both Racket and Python agree: the result of creating an anonymous function is a function-kind of value, not a number. What this says is that we have to broaden the kinds of values that interp  can produce.

术语：副作用，是指对系统作出的、在函数体外部可见的改变。典型的副作用包括修改在函数外部定义的变量、与网络通信、修改文件，等等。 Terminology: A side-effect  is a change to the system that is visible from outside the body of a function. Typical side-effects are modifications to variables that are defined outside the function, communication with a network, changes to files, and so on.

术语：如果函数对于给定输入，总是生成相同输出，并且没有副作用，就称它是纯的。实际上，计算总会有一些副作用，例如消耗能量和产生热量，但由于这些现象普遍存在，我们通常忽略它们。不过，在少数场景中，它们可能很重要：例如，如果通过测量这些副作用就能窃取加密密钥。 Terminology:  A function is pure  if, for a given input, it always produces the same output, and has no side-effects. In reality, a computation always has some  side-effects, such as the consumption of energy and production of heat, but we usually overlook these because they are universal. In a few settings, however, they can matter: e.g., if a cryptographic key can be stolen by measuring these side-effects.

术语：传统上，有些语言使用“过程”和“函数”来表示相似但不相同的概念。两者都是类似函数的实体，封装了一段代码体，并且可以被应用（或“调用”）。过程是一种不生成值的封装；因此，它必须有副作用才有用。相比之下，函数总会生成一个值（而且可能被期望没有任何副作用）。多年来，这套术语已经彻底混乱，人们现在常把两者混用，但如果有人似乎在区分它们，大概指的就是上述区别。 Terminology:  Traditionally, some languages have used the terms procedure  and function  for similar but not identical concepts. Both are function-like entities that encapsulate a body of code and can be applied (or “called”). A procedure is an encapsulation that does not produce a value; therefore, it must have side-effects to be of any use. In contrast, a function always produces a value (and may be expected to not have any side-effects). This terminology has gotten completely scrambled over the years and people now use the terms interchangeably, but if someone seems to be making a distinction between the two, they probably mean something like the above.

扩展值 Extending Values

对函数求值时会发生什么？Racket 和 Python 似乎都表明，我们返回一个函数。 What happens when evaluating a function? Both Racket and Python seem to suggest that we return a function.

我们可以不保留关于函数的任何额外信息： We could have no additional information about the function:

(define-type Value

  [numV (the-number : Number)]

  [boolV (the-boolean : Boolean)]

  [funV])

（这个语法表示 funV 是一个没有参数的构造器。除了说明它是 funV 这一事实之外，不传递任何信息；由于不能混用类型，具体来说，它表示一个值不是数字，也不是布尔值——仅此而已。）但现在想想下面这样的程序（假设 x 已绑定）： (That syntax means funV  is a constructor of no parameters. It conveys no information at all other than the fact that it’s a funV ; because we can’t mix types, it says, in particular, that a value is not numeric or a Boolean—and nothing more.) But now think about a program like this (assuming x  is bound):

{{if0 x

      {lam x {+ x 1}}

      {lam x {- x 2}}}

 5}

两种情况下，都会得到一个不含额外信息的 funV 值，因此当我们尝试执行应用时，就……做不到。 In both cases we’re going to get a funV  value with no additional information, so when we try to perform the application, we…can’t.

相反，显然函数值必须告诉我们有关函数的信息。需要知道函数体，因为那是要进行求值的部分；但函数体可以（而且很可能会）引用形式参数的名称，因此也需要这个名称。所以，真正需要的是 Instead, it’s clear that the function value needs to tell us about the function. We need to know the body, because that’s what we need to evaluate; but the body can (and very likely does) reference the name of the formal parameter, so we need that too. Therefore, what we really need is

(define-type Value

  [numV (the-number : Number)]

  [boolV (the-boolean : Boolean)]

  [funV (var : Symbol) (body : Exp)])

到了这一步，我们似乎白费了许多工夫。拿到数字和布尔值，只是用新构造器重新包裹一遍，现在对函数也做同样的事。这让人想到莎士比亚某部戏剧的名字。 At this point, it seems like we’ve gone to a lot of trouble for nothing. We take numeric and Boolean values and simply re-wrap them in new constructors, and now we’re doing the same thing for functions.  A certain Shakespeareian play’s title comes to mind.

耐心点。 Patience.

凭借现有内容，已经能得到一个可运行的解释器了。lam 的情况显然非常简单： With what we have, we can already have a functioning interpreter. The lam case is obviously very simple:

    [(lamE v b) (funV v b)]

应用的情况稍微复杂一些。我们需要： The application case is a bit more detailed. We need to:

  1. 对函数位置求值，弄清它是哪一类值。 Evaluate the function position, to figure out what kind of value it is.
  2. 对参数位置求值，因为我们已经约定 SMoL 就是这么做的。 Evaluate the argument position, since we’ve agreed that’s what happens in SMoL.
  3. 检查函数位置是否确实求值为函数。如果不是，抛出错误。 Check that the function position really does evaluate to a function. If it does not, raise an error.
  4. 对函数体求值。但由于函数体可以引用形式参数…… Evaluate the body of the function. But because the body can refer to the formal parameter…
  5. ……先确保形式参数已绑定到实际参数的值。 …first make sure the formal is bound to the actual value of the argument.

分阶段把这些写成代码： Codifying this, in stages:

    [(appE f a) (let ([fv (interp f nv)]

                      [av (interp a nv)])

                  …) ]

    [(appE f a) (let ([fv (interp f nv)]

                      [av (interp a nv)])

                  (type-case Value fv

                    [(funV v b) …]

                    [else (error 'app "didn't get a function")] ))]

    [(appE f a) (let ([fv (interp f nv)]

                      [av (interp a nv)])

                  (type-case Value fv

                    [(funV v b)

                      (interp b …) ]

                    [else (error 'app "didn't get a function")]))]

    [(appE f a) (let ([fv (interp f nv)]

                      [av (interp a nv)])

                  (type-case Value fv

                    [(funV v b)

                     (interp b (extend nv v av) )]

                    [else (error 'app "didn't get a function")]))]

退后一步 Stepping Back

把这一切组合起来，得到如下解释器： Putting it all together, we get the following interpreter:

(interp : (Exp Env -> Value))

(define (interp e nv)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(numE n) (numV n)]

    [(varE s) (lookup s nv)]

    [(plusE l r) (add (interp l nv) (interp r nv))]

    [(lamE v b) (funV v b)]

    [(appE f a) (let ([fv (interp f nv)]

                      [av (interp a nv)])

                  (type-case Value fv

                    [(funV v b)

                     (interp b (extend nv v av))]

                    [else (error 'app "didn't get a function")]))]

    [(let1E var val body)

     (let ([new-env (extend nv

                            var

                            (interp val nv))])

       (interp body new-env))]))

练习：上面写出了一个特定顺序，并在代码中落实了它。但这与实际语言采用的顺序相同吗？具体来说，非函数错误是在对参数求值之后还是之前报告？做实验找出答案！ Exercise:  We wrote down a particular ordering above, which we put into practice in the code. But is that the same ordering that actual languages use? In particular, are non-function errors reported after or before evaluating the argument? Experiment and find out!

走过好几个步骤才到这里，很容易忘记我们刚刚完成了什么。只用 20 行代码（外加几个辅助函数），我们就描述了一种完整编程语言的实现。不仅如此，这种语言还能够表达所有计算。图灵奖得主 Alan Kay 首次看到等价的程序时，他说： Since we’ve taken several steps to get here, it’s easy to lose sight of what we’ve just done. In just 20 lines of code (with a few helper functions), we have described the implementation of a full programming language . Not only that, a language that can express all computations . When Turing Award winner Alan Kay  first saw the equivalent program, he says ,

是的，那是我读研究生时的一次重大启示——我终于明白，Lisp 1.5 手册第 13 页底部那半页代码，本身就是 Lisp。这就是“软件的麦克斯韦方程组”！整个编程世界，就在这几行我一只手便能盖住的代码里。 Yes, that was the big revelation to me when I was in graduate school—when I finally understood that the half page of code on the bottom of page 13 of the Lisp 1.5 manual was Lisp in itself. These were “Maxwell’s Equations of Software!” This is the whole world of programming in a few lines that I can put my hand over.

我意识到，每当想弄清自己在做什么时，只需用半页纸写下这个东西的内核，就丝毫不会损失能力。事实上，它的能力反而会增强，因为它能够更容易地重新进入自身，而大多数采用另一种方式构建的系统根本做不到这一点。 I realized that anytime I want to know what I’m doing, I can just write down the kernel of this thing in a half page and it’s not going to lose any power. In fact, it’s going to gain power by being able to reenter itself much more readily than most systems done the other way can possibly do.

我们刚刚重新发现了同一个优美而强大的思想！如果想看原版，这就是那本手册（作者为 McCarthy、Abrahams、Edwards、Hart、Levin）。下面是复制的内容： We’ve just rediscovered this same beautiful, powerful idea! If you want to see the original, here’s that manual  (by McCarthy, Abrahams, Edwards, Hart, Levin). Here it is, copied:

好了，现在我们有了一个针对完整语言的、可运行的解释器。但在确信这一点之前，应该再试几个例子，确认现有结果确实令人满意。 Alright, so we now have a working interpreter for a full-fledged language. But before we can feel sure of that, we should try a few more examples to confirm that we’re happy with what we have.

扩充测试 Extending Tests

嗯，其实我们不应该太高兴。考虑以下例子： Well, actually, we shouldn’t be too happy. Consider the following examples:

(let1E 'x (numE 1)

       (let1E 'f (lamE 'y (varE 'x))

              (let1E 'x (numE 2)

                     (appE (varE 'f) (numE 10)))))

我们预期它得到什么结果？如果拿不准，可以把同样的内容写成一个 Racket 程序： What do we expect it to produce? If in doubt, we can write the same thing as a Racket program:

(let ([x 1])

  (let ([f (lambda (y) x)])

    (let ([x 2])

      (f 10))))

我们看到，在 Racket 中，内层 x 的绑定不会覆盖外层的绑定，也就是定义绑定给 f 的那个函数时存在的绑定。因此，这在 Racket 中得到 1。 What we see is that in Racket , the inner binding of x  does not  override the outer one, the one that was present at the time the function bound to f  was defined. Therefore, this produces 1  in Racket.

这应该正是我们想要的！否则，考虑这个程序： We should want this! Otherwise, consider this program:

(let1E 'f (lamE 'y (varE 'x))

       (let1E 'x (numE 1)

              (appE (varE 'f) (numE 10))))

它对应于 This corresponds to

(let ([f (lambda (y) x)])

  (let ([x 1])

    (f 10)))

其中存在一个未绑定标识符（x）错误。但我们的解释器却得到 1，而不是报错并停止，这就把我们直接带回了 ☠️ 动态作用域 ☠️！ which has an unbound identifier ( x ) error. But our interpreter produces 1  instead of halting with an error, which leads us right back to ☠️ dynamic scope ☠️!

回到静态作用域 Return to Static Scope

练习：在 Stacker 中运行以下程序。 Exercise: Run the following programs in the Stacker.

那么，如何修复这个问题？上面的例子实际上给了一条线索，但还有另一个灵感来源。记得我们是从替换开始的吗？我们将在 Racket 中逐步走过这些例子，这样你就能直接运行每个例子，检查它们是否得到相同答案。再次考虑这个程序： So how do we fix this? The examples above actually give us a clue, but there is another source of inspiration as well. Do you remember that we started with substitution ? We’ll walk through these examples in Racket, so that you can run each of them directly and check that they produce the same answer. Consider again this program:

(let ([x 1])

  (let ([f (lambda (y) x)])

    (let ([x 2])

      (f 10))))

用 1 替换 x，得到： Substituting 1  for x  produces:

  (let ([f (lambda (y) 1)])

    (let ([x 2])

      (f 10)))

替换 f，得到： Substituting f  produces:

    (let ([x 2])

      ((lambda (y) 1) 10))

最后，用 2 替换 x，得到（注意，程序中已经没有任何 x 了！）： Finally, substituting x  with 2  produces (note that there are no x s left in the program!):

      ((lambda (y) 1) 10)

这样看，就清楚为什么后来对 x 的绑定不应产生影响了：那是另一个 x，而先前的 x 实际上已经被替换了。既然已经认定替换就是我们希望程序遵循的工作方式，那么现在的任务就是确保环境确实正确地实现了这一点。 When you see it this way, it’s clear why  the later binding of x  should have no impact: it’s a different x , and the earlier x  has effectively already been substituted. Since we have agreed that substitution is how we want our programs to work, our job now is to make sure that the environment actually implements that correctly .

方法是认识到，环境表示尚待进行的替换，然后把它们记住。也就是说，函数的表示还需要记录创建函数那一刻的环境： The way to do it is to recognize that the environment represents the substitutions waiting to happen, and just remember  them. That is, our representation of a function needs to also keep track of the environment at the moment of function creation:

(define-type Value

  [numV (the-number : Number)]

  [boolV (the-boolean : Boolean)]

  [funV (var : Symbol) (body : Exp) (nv : Env) ])

这种新的、内容更丰富的 funV 值有个专门的名字：闭包。这是因为，表达式在其定义时的环境之上被“闭合”起来了。 This new and richer kind of funV  value has a special name: it’s called a closure . That’s because the expression is “closed” over the environment in which it was defined.

术语：闭项是不含未绑定变量的项。函数体可能有未绑定变量——例如上面的 x——但闭包确保它们并非真正未绑定，因为它们可以从存下来的环境中取得值。 Terminology:  A closed  term is one that has no unbound variables. The body of a function may have unbound variables—like x  above—but the closure makes sure that they aren’t really  unbound, because they can get their values from the stored environment.

引语：“拯救环境！今天就创建一个闭包吧！”——Cormac Flanagan Quote:  “Save the environment! Create a closure today!” — Cormac Flanagan

引语：“Lambda 一直默默无闻，直到 Java 因为没有它们而让它们走红。”——James Iry，《一部简短、不完整且大多错误的编程语言史》 Quote:  “Lambdas are relegated to relative obscurity until Java makes them popular by not having them.” — James Iry, A Brief, Incomplete, and Mostly Wrong History of Programming Languages

这意味着，创建闭包时，必须记录创建当时的环境： That means, when we create a closure, we have to record the environment at the time of its creation:

    [(lamE v b) (funV v b nv )]

最后，使用函数（由闭包表示）时，必须确保使用存下来的环境，而不是函数调用点存在的环境，后者是动态的环境： Finally, when we use a function (represented by a closure), we have to make sure we use the stored  environment, not the one present at the point of calling the function, which is the dynamic  one:

    [(appE f a) (let ([fv (interp f nv)]

                      [av (interp a nv)])

                  (type-case Value fv

                    [(funV v b nv )

                     (interp b (extend nv v av))]

                    [else (error 'app "didn't get a function")]))]

说清楚一点：在上面的代码中，funV 分支中的 nv 有意遮蔽了解释器顶端绑定的 nv。因此，对 extend 的调用扩展的是来自闭包的环境，而不是调用点存在的环境。 Just to be clear: in the code above, the nv  in the funV  case intentionally shadows  the nv  bound at the top of the interpreter. Thus, the call to extend  extends the environment from the closure , rather than the one present at the point of the call.

练习：注意，函数表达式和参数表达式（分别是 f 和 a）在传给解释器的环境中求值，而不是在闭包内部的环境中。这正确吗？还是应该使用闭包的环境？ Exercise:  Notice that the function and argument expressions ( f  and a , respectively) are evaluated in the environment given to the interpreter, not the one inside the closure. Is this correct? Or should they be using the closure’s environment?

可以做两件事：从第一性原理出发论证，或者用例子论证。对于后者，你要修改解释器，让它采取另一个选择。然后使用一个示例输入，使其根据所用环境的不同而得到不同答案，指出哪个答案正确（展示等价的 Racket 程序会得到什么结果，是一种不错的论证），再据此说明为什么应选择那个环境。提示：其中一个需要从第一性原理出发论证，另一个应该能够用程序来论证。 You can do two things: argue from first principles or argue with examples. In the latter case, you would modify the interpreter to make the other choice. You would then use a sample input that produces different answers depending on which environment is used, indicate which one is correct (showing what the equivalent Racket program would produce can be a good argument), and use that to justify the chosen environment. Hint:  One of these you will need to argue from first principles, the other you should be able to argue using a program.

一个微妙的测试 A Subtle Test

在上面的例子中，我们总是在定义闭包的作用域内使用它。然而，我们的语言实际上更强大：可以返回一个闭包，并在定义它的作用域之外使用它。下面是一个 Racket 程序示例： In the examples above, we always use the closure in the scope in which it was defined. However, our language is actually more powerful than that: we can return  a closure and use it outside  the scope in which it was defined. Here’s a sample Racket program:

((let ([x 3])

   (lambda (y) (+ x y)))

 4)

现在动手！花点时间仔细阅读。它应该得到什么结果？ Do Now:  Take a moment to read it carefully. What should it produce?

首先绑定 x，然后对 lambda 求值。这会创建一个记住 x 的绑定的闭包。这个闭包就是下面这个表达式返回的值： First we bind the x , then we evaluate the lambda. This creates a closure that remembers the binding to x . This closure is the value returned by this expression:

( (let ([x 3])

   (lambda (y) (+ x y)))

 4)

接着，把这个值应用于 4。这样做是合法的，因为返回的值是一个函数。将它应用于 4 时，会对 4 与 3 的和求值，得到 7。果然，把它翻译后交给我们的解释器，得到 7： This value is now applied to 4 . It’s legal to do this, because the value returned is a function. When we apply it to 4 , that evaluates the sum of 4  and 3 , producing 7 . Sure enough, translating this and sending it to our interpreter produces 7 :

(test (interp (appE (let1E 'x (numE 3)

                           (lamE 'y (plusE (varE 'x) (varE 'y))))

                    (numE '4))

              mt-env)

      (numV 7))

练习：这里还有一个值得尝试的测试，写成了 Racket 程序： Exercise:  Here’s another test to try out, written as a Racket program:

((let ([y 3])

   (lambda (y) (+ y 1)))

 5)

它在 Racket 中得到什么结果？将它翻译后，在你的解释器中试一试。 What does it produce in Racket? Translate it and try it in your interpreter.

••••• 语法糖 ••••• ••••• Syntactic Sugar •••••

我们现在已经看到了一个小型核心语言的精髓。在实践中，编程语言还需要好用。为此，它们必须提供让编程更方便的功能。我们将看到，它们可以在尽量减少自身工作量和痛苦的同时做到这一点。 We have now seen the essence of a small core language. In practice, programming languages need to also be usable . To do this, they have to provide features that make programming convenient. We will see they can do this while minimizing their effort and pain.

SMoL 如何变大 How SMoL Becomes Large

我们已经介绍过 SImPl，即标准实现方案。其核心思想是：用一个（相互）递归的代数数据类型，将程序的语法表示为抽象语法，然后编写一个类似的（相互）递归程序来处理它。这个程序产生什么，取决于我们想要实现的处理过程：解释器产生值，编译器产生程序（用另一种语言编写），类型检查器产生关于类型正确性的判断（以及更多内容，我们很快就会看到），等等。不过，它们都有相同的基本结构。 We have already been introduced to the idea of SImPl, the Standard Implementation Plan. The core idea is that the program’s syntax is represented as abstract syntax using a (mutually) recursive algebraic datatype, and we then write a similar (mutually) recursive program to process it. What that program produces depends on the process we are trying to implement: an interpreter produces values , a compiler produces programs  (in another language), a type-checker produces judgments about type-correctness  (and more, as we’ll soon see), and so on. But they all have the same basic structure.

实际上，这意味着 SImPl 必须为语言中的每一种构造提供一个处理分支。这在原则上不是问题，但实践中可能变得很繁重。假设有两种构造，其中包含大量重复内容。这不仅意味着我们必须重复编程，还意味着我们必须重复维护：如果在其中一处修复了一个错误，就必须记得在另一处以相应方式修复它。 In practice, this means that a SImPl needs to have a case to handle each of the constructs in the language. This is not a problem in principle, but it can become onerous in practice. Suppose we have two constructs that have a lot of repetition. Not only does it mean we have to duplicate programming, it also means we have to duplicate maintenance : if we fix a bug in one, we have to remember to fix it in the other in the corresponding way.

语言中的冗余 Redundancy in Languages

我们会在哪里发现这样的冗余呢？现实语言中有好几个例子。例如，许多语言既有 for 循环，也有 while 循环。考虑一个典型的 C 语言 for 循环： Where might we find such redundancy? There are several examples in real languages. For instance, many languages have both for  and while  loops. Consider a typical for  loop in C:

for(x = 0; x < 10; x++) {

  sum += x;

}

这与下面的代码完全相同 This is exactly  the same as

x = 0;

while (x < 10) {

  sum += x;

  x++;

}

事实上，这里有一个一般模式： There is, in fact, a general pattern:

for(INITIAL; CONDITIONAL; UPDATE) {

  sum += x;

}

与下面的代码相同（语法上稍作变通） is the same (with some syntactic liberties) as

INITIAL;

while (CONDITIONAL) {

  sum += x;

  UPDATE;

}

现在，设想你要为此编写一个解释器。显然，while 循环的实现必须进行若干次递归调用、迭代、检查，或许还要做一些其他簿记工作（甚至可能要管理作用域的临时扩展）。对于 for，所有这些工作都得再做一遍！如果只实现一次，再把 for 的主体翻译为 while 的主体，岂不是简单得多？ Now imagine you’re writing an interpreter for this. Clearly, the while  loop’s implementation has to make several recursive calls, iterate, check, and perhaps perform some other bookkeeping (and maybe even manage temporary scope extensions). All  of that work has to be duplicated  for for ! Wouldn’t it be much simpler to instead implement it just once, and translate the for  body into a while  body?

那为什么还要同时保留这两种构造呢？因为它们各自在不同用途下都很方便。特别是，while 有一种特定风格的用法，如果混在一大堆 while 代码里就较难辨认，而 for 会自动为我们把它归类出来。这丰富了我们作为程序员的词汇，只不过也恰好增加了我们作为实现者的痛苦。我们希望获得便利和更丰富的词汇，却不想承受这份痛苦。 Why have both constructs at all? Because each one is convenient for different purposes. In particular, there’s a certain stylistic use of while  that would be harder to spot from a mass of while  code that is automatically classified for us with for . It adds to our vocabulary as programmers. It just happens to also add to our pain as implementors. We’d like the convenience and richer vocabulary without the pain.

脱糖 Desugaring

由此就引出了核心语言和表层语言的区别。表层语言可以提供各种便利，但它们都会被翻译成核心语言，而核心语言的构造则全都直接处理。那些让编程变得更“甜”的额外构造，就叫作语法糖。将表层程序翻译为核心程序的程序叫作脱糖器，因为它会去掉糖。（原则上，脱糖器其实是一个从表层语言到核心语言的编译器。不过，由于核心语言是表层语言的子语言，这是一种非常特殊的编译情形，因此我们觉得，值得用一个专门的术语将它与一般编译区分开。就像我们觉得，值得用一个专门的术语将 for 与一般的 while 区分开一样……） This introduces a distinction between a core  language and a surface  language. The surface language may have various conveniences, but these get translated into the core language, whose constructs are all handled directly. The extra constructs—those that make it “sweeter” to program—are called syntactic sugar . The program that translates surface programs down to the core is called a desugarer , because it removes sugar. (In principle, a desugarer is actually a compiler  from the surface language to the core language. However, since the core language is a sub -language of the surface, this is a very special case of compilation, and we find it useful to have a special term to distinguish it from general compilation. Just like we find it useful to have a special term to distinguish for  from the general while …)

旁注：在实际实现中，这种编译需要更加小心。假如你在使用 for 时犯了一个错误，报错信息却用 while 来描述，你就会很困惑，因为你根本没有输入过 while。特别是，你可能还是一个甚至不知道 while 是什么的学生！现代脱糖系统，比如 Racket 中的系统，都有专门的支持，能够处理大多数常见情况下的这类问题。 Aside:  In a real implementation, this compilation requires a little more care. Suppose you make an error using for , but the error was reported in terms of while : you’d be pretty confused, because you never did type the while . As a special case, you may be a student who doesn’t even know what while   is ! Modern desugaring systems, such as that in Racket, have special support to take care of this in most of the common cases.

现实语言中的脱糖其实还有很多。例如，and 和 or 可以脱糖为嵌套的 if。在 JavaScript 中，o.x 会脱糖为 o["x"]（这一点过一会儿就会用到）。在许多语言中，x += y 是 x = x + y 的语法糖。在 Python 中，+ 会脱糖为 __add__ 方法。事实上，Python 有一大堆这样的脱糖；这些方法叫作“dunder”方法（double-underscore，即双下划线的缩写），围绕它们还发展出了一整套“协议”编程风格。许多语言（例如 Haskell 和 Python）都有列表推导式，它们会脱糖为函数调用和方法调用。诸如此类。简而言之，脱糖在编程中无处不在。如果你没注意到它，这在某种程度上正是它的目的：你感觉自己使用的表层语法，比实现者需要管理的语法更大。 There are actually many more desugarings in real languages. For instance, and  and or  can desugar into nested if s. In JavaScript, o.x  desugars into o["x"]  (which will be relevant in a while). In many languages, x += y  is sugar for x = x + y . In Python, +  desugars into the method __add__ . In fact, Python has a whole bunch of these desugarings; these methods are called “dunder” methods (short for double-underscore), and a whole programming style of “ protocols ” has evolved around it. Many languages (like Haskell and Python) have list comprehensions, which desugar into function and method calls. And so on. In short, desugaring is everywhere in programming. If you don’t notice it, that’s part of the point: it feels like you’re working with a larger surface syntax than the implementor has to manage.

实现脱糖的方法有很多。一种方法是照常解析程序，然后将 AST 重写为同一种 AST 的一个子集。但在有些语言中，尤其是采用括号语法的语言中，解析分为两个层次：较粗的括号层次和较细的 AST 层次。这意味着我们可以对括号项进行重写，而内部 AST 完全不必知道那些语法糖（也就是说，它只需要涵盖核心语言）。这样的系统通常叫作宏系统：它们在解析之前，将程序源代码（略作抽象）重写为程序源代码。重要的是要理解，大多数语言都有语法糖，但极少有语言提供宏系统，直接把程序重写能力交给程序员，而不是将它藏在编译器内部。 There are many ways in which desugaring can be implemented. One way is to parse the program normally, then rewrite the AST into a subset of the same AST. But in some languages, especially those with parenthetical syntax, there are two levels of parsing: the coarser parenthetical level and the finer level of ASTs. This means we can perform rewriting on the parenthetical terms, and the internal AST never needs to know about the sugars (i.e., it need cover only the core language). These are typically called macro  systems: systems in which program source (slightly abstracted) is rewritten into program source, before parsing takes place. It’s important to understand that most  languages have syntactic sugar, but very few  languages have macro systems, which provide program rewriting capabilities directly to the programmer (as opposed to hiding them inside the compiler).

通过示例学习宏 Macros By Example

Racket 是少数拥有宏系统的语言之一，而且它的宏系统非常强大。它的罕见意味着，我们通过宏学到的思想，需要费些工夫才能移植到其他语言；但它的强大意味着，我们可以借助 Racket 的全部能力编写相当复杂的系统，而我们也确实会这样做。本质上，Racket 宏会把一种扩展版 Racket——你愿意的话，可以叫它 Racket++——编译为 Racket，随后我们就可以充分利用现有 Racket 框架的能力。 Racket is one of the few languages to have a macro system, and in fact has a very powerful one. Its rarity means ideas we learn using macros will take some effort to port to other languages; but its power means we can write quite sophisticated systems by leveraging the full power of Racket, and we will do so. In essence, Racket macros compile an extended version of Racket—call it Racket++, if you like—down to Racket, where we can then exploit the full power of the existing Racket framework.

我们将通过一系列示例介绍 Racket 的宏系统。在下面的内容中，请改用 We will introduce the Racket macro system through a series of examples. In what follows, please switch to using

#lang racket

因为 plait 的限制和类型虽然非常适合编写解释器，却会妨碍我们接下来要编写的某些内容。 because the restrictions and types of plait , while very useful for writing interpreters, can get in the way of some of what we’ll write.

一种新的条件构造 A New Conditional

回想一下，Racket 是一种使用真性值／假性值的语言，if 将任何非假值都视为真。假设我们想要一个只接受布尔值的严格 if。也就是说，我们希望为 Racket 本身扩展一个 strict-if。来试试这个： Recall that Racket is a truthy/falsy language, where if  takes any non-false value to be true. Suppose we want a strict if  that takes only Booleans. That is, we want to extend Racket itself with a strict-if . Let’s try this:

(define (strict-if C T E)

  (if (boolean? C)

      (if C T E)

      (error 'strict-if "expected a boolean")))

试试这样的例子： Try examples like:

(strict-if true 1 2)

(strict-if 0 1 2)

看起来正如我们所愿！ Seems to work as desired!

现在动手！你看出问题在哪里了吗？ Do Now:  Do you see what the problem is?

问题在于，我们使用的是一种急切求值的语言（SMoL 总体上都是如此！），因此 strict-if 的参数会在函数体开始执行前求值。但是，条件构造的全部意义就是避免对求值过程中的一部分进行求值：试试 The problem is that we have an eager language (this is true of SMoL in general!), so strict-if s arguments are going to be evaluated before the body begins to execute. However, the whole point of a conditional is to avoid evaluating part of the evaluation: Try

(strict-if true 1 (/ 1 0))

将它与下面代码的行为比较一下 Compare this to what happens with

(if true 1 (/ 1 0))

好吧，所以我们无法用函数来达到这个目的。我们需要另一种定义机制，它接收语法并重写语法，而不是立即让它求值。这就是宏。 Okay, so we can’t use functions for this purpose. We need some other definition mechanism that consumes the syntax  and rewrites that, instead of letting it evaluate right away. These are macros.

让我们深入看看宏是怎么写的，因为它与函数的写法并没有那么不同： Let’s dive into how the macro is written, because it’s not so different from the function:

(define-syntax strict-if

  (syntax-rules ()

    [(strict-if C T E)

     (if (boolean? C)

         (if C T E)

         (error 'strict-if "expected a boolean"))]))

这些部分分别是什么？define-syntax 表示我们在定义一种新的语法，而不是函数。syntax-rules 引入一个模式匹配器（暂时忽略 () 的含义，不过你确实需要把它写上）。每条规则都放在方括号中，由一个模式和一个输出组成：如果输入匹配该模式，那么脱糖器（在这里叫作宏展开器）就产生相应的输出，但模式中的名称（此处为 C、T 和 E）会作为程序源代码复制到输出中。因此，对于 What are the pieces? define-syntax  says we’re defining a new piece of syntax  (as opposed to a function). syntax-rules  introduces a pattern-matcher (for now, ignore what the ()  means: but you do need to include it). Each rule, in brackets, is a pattern and output: if the input matches the pattern, then the desugarer (here called a macro expander ) produces the corresponding output, but with the names  in the pattern (here, C , T , and E ) copied as program source into the output. Thus, given

(strict-if true 1 (/ 1 0))

上面的宏定义会将它转换为 the above macro definition transforms it into

(if (boolean? true)

    (if true 1 (/ 1 0))

    (error 'strict-if "expected a boolean"))

随后，它的求值结果就完全符合我们的预期。 which then evaluates exactly as we’d expect.

Racket 的一个好用功能是宏步进器（Macro Stepper）（）。它会展示程序逐步展开的过程，对于理解宏和调试宏都很有用。如果有必要，请将左下角的“Macro hiding”选项改为“Standard”。 One nice feature of Racket is the Macro Stepper ( ). It shows the program expanding step-by-step, which is useful both for understanding macros and debugging them. If necessary, change the “Macro hiding” option at the bottom-left to read “Standard”.

练习：用上面的宏定义和用法试试它，看看会得到什么。观察它如何在每一步中先高亮即将展开的宏用法，再高亮展开结果。 Exercise:  Try it out with the above macro definition and use. See what you get. Observe how, at each step, it highlights the macro use about to be expanded followed by the result of that expansion.

注意：宏步进器不是求值器。它不会显示求值步骤，只会显示展开步骤！因此，如果你编写的程序会在运行时产生错误，宏步进器不会显示该错误。它只显示语法错误。 Note:  The Macro Stepper is not an evaluator . It does not show the steps of evaluation, only the steps of expansion! Thus, if you write a program that will produce an error at run-time, the Macro Stepper does not show that error. It only shows syntax  errors.

注意：第一次使用宏步进器时，请检查左下角的“Macro hiding”菜单。如果它不是 Standard，就改成 Standard。否则，你会看到许多对学习宏没有帮助的步骤。最终，你可能会遇到足够棘手的程序，需要使用 Disable hiding 或 Custom hiding，但大多数时候，Standard 都最方便、最有用。 Note:  When you first use the Macro Stepper, check the “Macro hiding” menu at the bottom-left. If it is not set to Standard, change it to Standard. Otherwise you will see many more steps than are useful for learning about macros. Eventually, you may have a sufficiently thorny program that makes you Disable hiding or use Custom hiding, but most of the time, Standard is the most convenient and useful.

局部绑定 Local Binding

现在，来看看我们一直在使用的 let 绑定。设想我们希望为 Racket 扩展一种 let1 构造：例如，我们希望 Now let’s look at the let  bindings we’ve been using until now. Imagine we want to extend Racket with a let1  construct: for example, we want

(let1 (x 3) (+ x x))

求值得到 6。 to evaluate to 6.

现在动手！let1 能定义为函数吗？为什么能，或者为什么不能？ Do Now:  Can let1  be defined as a function? Why or why not?

let1 不可能是函数。如果它是函数，我们就会先尝试将各个子项作为参数求值。这里有两个看起来像参数表达式的东西：(x 3) 和 (+ x x)。假设我们尝试对 (x 3) 求值。首先，它看起来像一次应用。其次，x 甚至没有被绑定。第三，它无法产生任何有意义的“值”：它唯一的职责其实是绑定 x。不，let1 也是一种新的语法。 let1  can’t be a function. If it were, we would first try to evaluate each of the sub-terms as arguments. There are two things here that look like argument expressions: (x 3)  and (+ x x) . Suppose we try to evaluate   (x 3) . First of all, it looks like an application. Second, x  isn’t even bound. Third, there is no meaningful “value” it could produce: its only job is instead to bind   x . No, let1  is also a new piece of syntax.

术语：我们经常将这些新的语法称为构造（比如“一种新的语言构造”）。在 Lisp/Scheme/Racket 社区中，它们有时也叫作特殊形式，因为它们是具有自身特殊绑定规则和求值规则的语法形式。 Terminology:  We will often refer to these new pieces of syntax as constructs  (as in, “a new language construct”). In the Lisp/Scheme/Racket community, these are sometimes also called special forms , because they are syntactic forms with their own special rules for binding and evaluation.

从现在起，我们会给宏加上 my- 前缀，因为不想与 Racket 内置宏的名称冲突。 From now on we’ll use the prefix my-  on our macros, because we don’t want to clash with the names of macros already built into Racket.

根据上面学到的内容，我们大概能写出 my-let1 宏的一半： From what we’ve seen above, we can probably figure out half of the macro for my-let1 :

(define-syntax my-let1

  (syntax-rules ()

    [(my-let1 (var val) body)

     …]))

但它应该展开成什么呢？我们当然可以直接把它展开为 Racket 现有的 let 构造，但还有另一个有趣的选择。 But what would it expan d into? We certainly could  just expand it into the existing let  construct in Racket, but there’s another interesting option.

想一想 my-let1 做了什么：它将一个名称绑定到一个值，然后立即在由该名称扩展的环境中对主体求值。那么，我们还能想到什么东西也会把名称绑定到值吗？没错，函数。而且，函数也在扩展后的环境中对主体求值。函数什么时候对主体求值？当它们被应用于某个实参时。因此，我们可以用一个立即应用的匿名函数来表达 my-let1： Let’s think about what my-let1  does: it binds  a name to a value, and then immediately evaluates  its body in an environment extended by its name. Now, can we think of anything else that binds names to values? Yes, functions. And functions evaluate a body in an extended environment. When do functions evaluate their body? When they are applied to an argument. Therefore, we can express my-let1  in terms of an anonymous function that is applied immediately:

(define-syntax my-let1

  (syntax-rules ()

    [(my-let1 (var val) body)

     ((lambda (var) body) val)]))

果然， Sure enough,

(my-let1 (x 3) (+ x x))

会产生 6。用宏步进器看看这是怎么发生的！ will produce 6 . Use the Macro Stepper to see how!

术语：这种定义一个匿名函数后立刻使用它的模式，通常叫作 left-left-lambda（其中的“left”代表左括号）。很长一段时间，这都是 Lisp/Scheme 社区里一个冷僻的术语。但由于早期 JavaScript 版本的作用域处理存在问题，这种模式又以“立即调用函数表达式”（Immediately Invoked Function Expression，IIFE）之名在 JavaScript 中流行起来。如果你觉得这里的括号看着很糟，不妨上网找找 IIFE 的例子。 Terminology:  This pattern, of an anonymous function that is used right away, is commonly called left-left-lambda  (where “left” stands for left-parenthesis). For a long time this remained an obscure term in the Lisp/Scheme community. But JavaScript made this pattern popular again under the name Immediately Invoked Function Expression  (IIFE), because of problems with the handling of scope in earlier versions of the language. If you think the parentheses look bad here, look up some examples of IIFE on the Web.

练习：假设我们在宏中犯了一个错误，交换了两个部分： Exercise:  Suppose we make a mistake in the macro and swap two parts:

(define-syntax my-let1

  (syntax-rules ()

    [(my-let1 (var val) body)

     ((lambda (var) val) body)]))

当我们尝试对下面的表达式求值时，会发生什么 What happens when we try to evaluate

(my-let1 (x 3) (+ x x))

？用宏步进器看看发生了什么。 ? Use the Macro Stepper to see what happened.

绑定更多局部名称 Binding More Locals

不过，正如我们在 Racket 中已经注意到的那样，let 可以同时绑定许多名称，而不只是一个。现在其实现方式已经很清楚了：函数接收若干形参，并应用于同样数量的实参。想要多少个都可以！但我们该如何用宏语法表达这一点呢？ As we have noticed in Racket, however, the let  can bind many names at once, not only one. It becomes clear how: the function takes formal arguments, and is applied to just as many actual arguments. There can be as many as we want! But how do we express this in macro syntax?

在数学中，通常用省略号（…）表示一个任意长度的序列。因此，如果能写出下面这样的东西，就很好了： In mathematics, it’s common to use ellipses (…) to denote a sequence of arbitrary length. Therefore, it would be nice if we could write something like this:

(define-syntax my-let2

  (syntax-rules ()

    [(my-let2 ([var val] ...) body)

     ((lambda (var ...) body) val ...)]))

它的意思是，my-let2 后面跟着任意数量的 var-val 对，再跟着一个主体。将它转换成一个 lambda，以所有 var 为形参，以 body 为主体，再将它应用于所有对应的 val，作为实参表达式。我们会像下面这样使用它（额外的括号是为了帮助我们将各个绑定归组）： This would say, my-let2  is followed by any number of var - val  pairs, followed by a body. Turn that into a lambda  with all the var s as formal arguments, whose body is body , applied to all the same val s as the actual argument expressions. We would use it like so (the extra parens are to help us group the bindings):

(my-let2 ([x 3] [y 4]) (+ x y))

事实上，这正是 Racket 支持的语法！试试上面的程序：运行它，也在宏步进器里查看它！ In fact, that is exactly  the syntax supported by Racket! Try out the above program: run it, and also examine it in the Macro Stepper!

多分支条件构造 Multi-Armed Conditionals

最后再看一个例子，它会说明 … 的含义：“前一个模式的零个或多个实例”。用它，我们可以定义自己的多分支条件构造。假设我们想定义一个名为 sign 的函数，根据数字的正负号产生一个字符串： Here’s one last example that clarifies what … means: it means “zero or more instances of the preceding pattern”. Using it, we can define our own multi-armed conditional. Suppose we want to define a function called sign  that produces a string based on the sign of a number:

(define (sign n)

  (my-cond

   [(< n 0) "negative"]

   [(= n 0) "zero"]

   [(> n 0) "positive"]))

同样，显然 my-cond 不可能是函数；我们需要用宏为语言扩展一种新的构造。 Again, it’s clear that my-cond  can’t be a function; we need to extend the language with a new construct, using a macro.

我们的多分支条件构造应该有多少个分支呢？当然是程序员想要多少就有多少。我们进一步规定：如果所有问题都用完了，仍然没有一个得到真值，那么这种“穿透到底”的情况就产生一个错误。 How many arms should our multi-armed conditional have? As many as the programmer wants, of course. We’ll further stipulate that if we have exhausted all the questions and none has yielded a true value, the “falling through” produces an error.

因此，我们希望剥下第一个问题—答案对，并对问题求值。如果它成功，就对答案求值。否则，我们希望递归处理剩余问题……而这本质上就是一个更小的 my-cond 实例。（没错，我们现在是在对语法递归！） Thus, we want to peel off the first question-answer pair and evaluate the question. If it succeeds, we evaluate the answer. Otherwise, we want to recur on the remaining questions…which is essentially a smaller instance of my-cond . (That’s right, we’re recurring on syntax  now!)

由于 … 表示“零个或多个”，我们最终会得到一个重复某个模式的模式：第一份剥下第一个实例，第二份后面带着 …，捕获所有剩余实例： Since …  means “zero or more”, we end up with a pattern where we repeat a pattern: the first copy peels off the first instance, while the second, followed by a … , captures all the remaining instances:

(define-syntax my-cond

  (syntax-rules ()

    [(my-cond) (error 'my-cond "should not get here")]

    [(my-cond [q0 a0] [q1 a1] ...)

     (if q0

         a0

         (my-cond [q1 a1] ...))]))

练习：仔细研究这段代码，并试试上面的例子。务必让它在宏步进器中运行一遍：你会从这个例子中学到很多关于宏的知识！ Exercise:  Examine this code in detail. Try out the example above. It’s essential  that you run this through the Macro Stepper: you’ll learn a lot about macros from this example!

关于宏的更多内容 More on Macros

注意：本章所有示例都能在 YouTube 的一个视频中找到，所以你愿意的话，也可以改看视频：More on Macros。务必在每个示例之后停下来思考，并亲自尝试每一个例子！ Note:  All the examples from this chapter you can find in a video on YouTube, so if you prefer, you can watch that instead: More on Macros . Be sure to stop and reflect after each example, and try each of them out for yourself!

现在，我们开始了解使用 Racket 宏时的各种惯用方式。我们需要掌握这些知识，因为接下来会用到其中好几种功能。我们将看到五件具体的事情： Now let’s start to look at various idiomatic aspects of using Racket macros. We’ll want this understanding under our belt because we’ll make use of several of these features. Here are five concrete things we’ll see:

  • 定义上的一个便利 A convenience in definitions
  • 宏的一项重大而关键的功能 A major and critical macro feature
  • 真性值／假性值语言中的一种重要惯用法 An important idiom in truthy/falsy languages
  • 宏定义中的一个隐患 A hazard in macro definitions
  • 对定义进行泛化的推动 A push to generalize definitions

定义上的一个便利 A Definitional Convenience

假设我们想定义一个“单分支 if”（例如，它可以用于检查错误条件，只有一切正常时才继续）：这通常叫作 unless。我们可以这样编写它： Supposing we want to define a “one-armed if ” (e.g., useful for checking erroneous conditions and proceeding only if the coast is clear): this is commonly called unless . We can write it this way:

(define-syntax unless

  (syntax-rules ()

    [(_ cond body ...)

     (if (not cond)

         (begin

           body

           ...)

         (void))]))

例如，我们可以这样使用它： For instance, we can use it this way:

(unless false

  (println 1)

  (println 2))

注意，在模式中，我们不必重复 unless；直接用一个 _ 就行。 Notice that in the pattern, we don’t have to repeat the unless ; we can just use an _  instead.

旁注：完整地说，这并不只是一项便利。它们实际做的事情略有不同，在某些微妙的情形中可以观察到这种差别。你可以放心使用 _ 来代替重复宏名，而且也应该这样做。 Aside:  The full truth is, this isn’t just a convenience . They actually do slightly different things that you can detect in subtle situations. You can safely, and should, just use _  instead of repeating the name of the macro.

名称捕获 Name Capture

不过，如果我们在这样的上下文中使用上面的代码，会怎样呢： But now, what if we use the above code in this kind of context:

(let ([not (λ (v) v)])

  (unless false

    (println 1)

    (println 2)))

这似乎有问题：它似乎会展开为 This seems problematic: it seems to expand into

(let ([not (λ (v) v)])

  (if (not false)

      (begin

        (println 1)

        (println 2))

      (void)))

这几乎与我们想要的结果完全相反。这是因为，宏外部的 not 似乎捕获了宏内部的 not。这与动态作用域大致类似：任何使用上下文都可能改变抽象内部发生的事情。如果真是这样，当一个宏作者可就太可怕了！ which is pretty much the opposite of what we want. That’s because the not  outside the macro seems to have captured the not  inside the macro. This is roughly analogous to dynamic scope: any use context can modify what happens inside the abstraction. If this were true, it would be terrifying to be a macro writer!

现在动手！运行这两个版本。它们产生的答案相同吗？ Do Now:  Run both versions. Do they produce the same answer?

但运行宏版本就会发现，名称 not 并没有被捕获。最重要的是，用宏步进器看看展开过程。关键在于，变量不仅仅是名称；它们还记录着绑定信息，使在不同情境中引入的名称保持分离。打印出来可能一样，但在内部，Racket 会将它们区分开（并在宏步进器中用颜色展示这种区分）。也就是说，就好像我们从这个程序出发： But running the macro version makes clear that the name not  is not  being captured. Most of all, use the Macro Stepper to see how the expansion works. The important thing is that variables are more than just names ; they record binding information, which keeps names introduced in different settings separate. They may print the same way, but internally Racket keeps them separate (and shows this separation in the Macro Stepper using colors). That is, it’s as if we start with this program:

(let ([not (λ (v) v)])

  (unless false

    (println 1)

    (println 2)))

经过展开后，它变成了这个程序（使用了不同的颜色）： which, after expansion, turns into this program (which uses different colors):

(let ([not (λ (v) v)])

  (if (not false )

      (begin

        (println 1)

        (println 2) )

      (void)) )

这样，我们就能轻松区分这些标识符：红色的 not 与蓝色的 not 不同。实际的内部表示是颜色标记的一种高效对应物。如果有必要，宏展开器也可以使用彼此不同的新鲜名称（即之前没有用过的名称），如 not1、not2 等，来表示这些同名的不同变量。 So now we can easily keep the identifiers apart: the red not  is different from the blue not . The actual internal representation is an efficient analog to colors. If necessary, the macro expander can also use distinct fresh  (i.e., previously unused) names— not1 , not2 , etc.—to represent the different variables of the same name.

这一性质为宏恢复了一种类似静态作用域的机制，叫作卫生性。卫生性是宏的一项关键功能（值得注意的是，C 预处理器没有这项功能）。它让程序员可以在宏定义中任意选用名称，而不必担心使用上下文会绑定哪些名称；同样，它也让用户可以任意选用变量名，而不必担心宏里的代码。 This property, which recovers an analog of static scoping for macros, and is called hygiene . Hygiene is a critical feature for macros (and, notably, is one not  given by the C pre-processor). It lets programmers use whatever name they want in the macro definition without worrying about what names will be bound in the use context; and similarly, lets users use whatever variable names they want without worrying about the macro’s code.

话虽如此，你可能会想，卫生性是不是只对 not 这样的内置函数有效。我们会看到，答案是……不是。不过，在那之前，我们先看几个其他的惯用示例。 That said, you may wonder whether hygiene is just for built-in functions like not . We’ll see that it’s … not. But to get there, we’ll work through some other idiomatic examples.

真性值／假性值的一种惯用法 A Truthy/Falsy Idiom

下面这件事与宏无关，却经常出现在真性值／假性值语言中。考虑一个双分支 or，我们可以将它定义为宏： Unrelated to macros, here’s something we often see in truthy/falsy languages. Consider a two-arm or , which we can define as a macro:

(define-syntax or-2

  (syntax-rules ()

    [(_ e1 e2)

     (if e1

         true

         e2)]))

对于下面的情况，它工作得不错 This works well enough for

(or-2 true false)

(or-2 false false)

(or-2 false true)

不过，考虑一下 member 这样的函数： However, consider a function like member :

(member 'y '(x y z))

成功时，它不只是返回 true，而是返回列表中整个剩余部分（这是真性值）。但如果将它与 or-2 组合起来： When it succeeds, it doesn’t just return true , it returns the entire rest of the list (which is a truthy value). But if we combine this with or-2 :

(or-2 (member 'y '(x y z)) "not found")

这显然不是我们想要的结果：有用的返回值丢了。因此，下面是另一个宏，它会返回那个结果，而不是将它压掉： This is clearly not the result we want: we’ve lost the useful return value. Instead, here’s a different macro that returns rather than suppressing that result:

(define-syntax or-2

  (syntax-rules ()

    [(_ e1 e2)

     (if e1

         e1

         e2)]))

这样就让 This makes

(or-2 (member 'y '(x y z)) "not found")

按预期工作了。 work as expected.

宏定义中的一个隐患 A Macro Definition Hazard

不过，这个宏包含一个微妙（几乎隐藏起来）但很重要的隐患。考虑这个例子： However, this macro contains a subtle (almost hidden), important hazard. Consider this example:

(or-2 (print "hello") "not found")

它也会返回一个真性值，但现在我们看到打印发生了两次。所以，我们需要 That also returns a truthy value, but now we see the print twice . So we need

(define-syntax or-2

  (syntax-rules ()

    [(_ e1 e2)

     (let ([v e1])

       (if v v e2))]))

练习：确认它会产生正确答案。 Exercise:  Confirm that this produces the correct answer.

这里的问题是，我们忘了宏是语法抽象。因此，写下 (if e1 e1 e2) 时，我们就是要求把 e1 复制到输出中两次。无论如何，这都会带来麻烦（例如，在真分支中，任何计算都会发生两次；还会让生成的程序体积膨胀！），但当计算具有可观察的效果时，问题尤其严重。因此，我们必须避免对它计算多次。 The problem here is that we’ve forgotten that macros are syntactic  abstractions. Thus, when we write (if e1 e1 e2)  we are asking for e1  to get copied into the output twice. This is messy no matter what (e.g., it causes any computation to happen twice in the truth case; it also blows up the size of the generated program!), but it is especially problematic if the computation has an observable effect. Thus, we have to avoid computing it more than once.

注意，我们的修改之所以有效，是因为 e1 本来就一定会被求值。否则，let 就会让它在原本可能不求值的情况下也被迫求值。因此，将 let 放在正确位置很重要：应当放在它本来就会被求值的地方。 Observe that our modification works because e1  is guaranteed to be evaluated. Otherwise, the let  would force it to be evaluated in situations where it might not otherwise. It is therefore important to put the let  in the right place: where it was going to be evaluated anyway.

再谈卫生性 Back to Hygiene

现在，打印示例已经能正常工作了。但我们又得担心 This now works fine for the printing example. But now we have to worry about

(let ([v 1])

  (or-2 false v))

使用新鲜名称时，它可能展开成下面两种形式： Using fresh names, there are two things this could expand into:

(let ([v 1])

  (let ([v false])

    (if v

        v

        v)))

(let ([v0 1])

  (let ([v1 false])

    (if v1

        v1

        v0)))

宏版本会产生哪一种？没错，是后一种，也就是对应于 Which does the macro version produce? That’s right, the latter: the one corresponding to

(let ([v 1])

  (let ([v false])

    (if v

        v

        v )) )

换句话说，卫生性对局部变量同样有效，并非只对内置函数有效！再换句话说，我们花了好长时间，讨论一件你根本不用操心的事。作为回报，这意味着你在宏程序中可以放心使用名称，就像有了静态作用域之后，你在函数和方法内部所做的那样。 In other words, hygiene works just as well for local variables, not just for built-in functions! In other words, we have spent a whole bunch of time on something you don’t  need to worry about. In return, it means you can use names with impunity in your macro programs, just as you do inside functions and methods because of static scoping.

泛化宏 Generalizing Macros

最后，与那些困在中缀语法和二元运算符中的可怜程序员不同，使用括号语法的程序员可以把构造推广到任意元数。我们已经见过 …；现在就用它来创建一个 n 元的 or。一个自然的初始定义是 Finally, unlike the poor programmers stuck with their infix syntaxes and binary operators, parenthetical syntax programmers can generalize constructs to arbitrary arity. We’ve seen …  already; let’s put it to work here to create an n -ary or . A natural first definition is

(define-syntax orN

  (syntax-rules ()

    [(_ e1 e2 ...)

     (let ([v e1])

       (if v v (orN e2 ...)))]))

现在动手！不过，看看尝试下面代码时会发生什么： Do Now:  However,  see what happens when we try:

(let ([v true])

  (orN false v))

好吧，这样不行。一定要注意错误信息： Okay, so that doesn’t work. It’s important to pay attention to the error message:

orN：语法错误，出现在：(orN) orN: bad syntax in: (orN)

这凸显了基本情况的必要性。问题在于，上面的定义要求一个或多个子表达式：e1 是第一个，而 e2 … 表示从第二个位置开始的零个或多个。但没有任何规则涵盖没有子项的情况。因此，我们需要 This highlights the need for a base case. The problem is our definition above requires one or more sub-expressions: e1  is the first, and e2 …  means zero or more  from the second position onward. But nothing covers the case of no sub-terms. So we need

(define-syntax orN

  (syntax-rules ()

    [(_) false]

    [(_ e1 e2 ...)

     (let ([v e1])

       (if v v (orN e2 ...)))]))

当然，这样就能正常工作了。 and of course this works fine.

练习：上面的问题看起来是我们自找的：为什么一开始要用 (_ e1 e2 ...) 这个模式，它要求一个或多个（e1 是第一个，e2 … 是零个或多个）？我们本该直接写 (_ e...)，这样就是零个或多个了！用这个模式重写 orN 宏：你能让它工作吗？ Exercise: The problem above appears to have been self-inflicted: why did we start with the pattern (_ e1 e2 ...) , which requires one-or-more ( e1  is the first, e2 …  is zero or more)? We should have just written (_ e...)  instead, which would be zero-or-more! Rewrite the orN  macro using this pattern: can you make it work?

注意：你也可以在本书第二版第 13 章“作为语言功能的脱糖”中阅读更多示例和细节［PDF，HTML］。 Note: You can also read more examples and details from chapter 13, “Desugaring as a Language Feature”, from the second edition  of this book [ PDF , HTML ].

••••• 对象 ••••• ••••• Objects •••••

对象——将数据及其上的操作捆绑在一起——是闭包的泛化。许多语言都有对象，但形式各不相同。 Objects—the bundling of data with operations over them—are a generalization of closures. Many languages have objects, but in a variety of different forms.

对象的一种标准模型 A Standard Model of Objects

现在，我们已经准备好考察第一个超出 SMoL 的主要语言功能：对象。并非所有 SMoL 语言都有对象；虽然很多语言有，但方式却各不相同。尽管如此，我们会发现，跨越所有这些语言，仍然存在一种相当统一的对象思考方式，而且这种思考方式确实建立在我们对 SMoL 的理解之上。 Now we’re ready to start looking at our first major language feature that goes beyond SMoL: objects. Not all SMoL languages have objects; though many do, they have them in very different ways. Nevertheless, what we will see is that there is a fairly uniform way to think about objects across all these languages, and furthermore this way of thinking really builds on our understanding of SMoL.

不过，在构建对象的本质机制时，我们现在有一个选择：既可以在核心语言中实现，也可以通过语法糖实现。前者在几个方面令人头疼： When building the essence of objects, though, we now have a choice: we can do it either in the core or through syntactic sugar. The former is frustrating in several ways:

  • 我们必须处理更多底层簿记工作（例如环境），而这些工作未必有助于学习。 We have to do more low-level bookkeeping (e.g., with environments) that may not necessarily be instructive .
  • 解释器会变得更大、更难处理，因为所有新构造都堆在同一处，而不是各自作为独立定义存在。 The interpreter gets larger and more unwieldy, because all the new constructs go in the same place rather than each being independent definitions.
  • 最重要的是，编写演示程序和测试会变得困难得多，因为核心语言可能并不具备让这些工作方便进行的所有必要功能。 Most of all: it becomes a lot harder to write illustrative programs and tests, because the core language may not have all the features we need to make this convenient.

相比之下，如果改用语法糖，所有这些问题都消失了。因此，尽管真实实现很可能至少会把对象的某些部分（尤其是为了效率所必需的部分）放进核心语言，我们还是要用宏，完全通过脱糖来构建对象。事实上，在本书中，我们会采取更简单的做法：给出程序脱糖后形式的具体示例。推导一般性的脱糖规则，会留给你作为练习。为了帮助完成这一过程，我们会尽可能以程式化的形式编写代码，不采用任何可能遮蔽宏规则的捷径。 In contrast, all these problems go away if we use syntactic sugar instead. Therefore, even though a real implementation may well have at least parts of objects (especially the parts needed for efficiency) in the core language, we are going to build objects entirely through desugaring, using macros. In fact, in this book, we will do something even simpler: we will give concrete examples of what programs desugar to . Figuring out the general desugaring will be left as an exercise for you. To aid in that process, we will write code in as stylized a form as possible, not using any short-cuts that might obscure the macro rules.

注意：本节中的程序不能用 plait 语言编写。我们将改用 #lang racket，它不进行静态类型检查。在顶部添加下面这一行 Note:  The programs in this section cannot be written in the language plait . Instead, we will use   #lang racket , which does not perform static type-checking. Add the line

(require [only-in plait test print-only-errors])

以便使用 plait 中的测试运算符和打印控制参数。 at the top to access the testing operator and printing control parameter from plait .

练习：找出类型检查器会在哪一点开始造成问题。提示：最简单的办法，当然是继续使用 #lang plait，直到遇到问题。一定要弄清问题是什么！ Exercise:  Spot the point at which the type-checker would become problematic. Hint:  The easiest way is, of course, to keep using #lang plait  until you run into a problem. Make sure you understand what the problem is!

什么是对象？ What is an Object?

在开始考虑实现之前，我们必须回答的核心问题是：对象是什么。不同语言之间有很多差异，但它们似乎都同意，对象是 The central question we must answer, before we start thinking about implementations, is what an object is. There is a lot of variation between languages, but they all seem to agree that an object is

  • 一个值，它 a value, that
  • 将名称映射到 maps names to
  • 某种东西：其他值，或者“方法”。 stuff: either other values or “methods”.

从极简的角度看，方法似乎只是函数，而我们的语言中已经有函数了，所以可以先不考虑这种区别。 From a minimalist perspective, methods seem to be just functions, and since we already have those in the language, we can put aside this distinction.

术语：当我们不想区分字段和方法时，会用“成员”这个词泛指对象中的条目。 Terminology:  We will use the term member  to refer to a generic entry in an object, when we don’t want to make a distinction between fields and methods.

如何刻画这一点呢？对象不过是一个根据给定名称进行分派的值。为简单起见，我们用 lambda 表示对象，用 Racket 的 case 构造实现分派。下面这个对象会响应 add1 或 sub1，并分别返回一个递增或递减的函数： How can we capture this? An object is just a value that dispatches on a given name. For simplicity, we’ll use lambda  to represent the object and Racket’s case  construct to implement the dispatching. Here’s an object that responds to either add1 or sub1, and in each case returns a function that either increments or decrements:

(define o

  (lambda (m)

    (case m

      [(add1) (lambda (x) (+ x 1))]

      [(sub1) (lambda (x) (- x 1))])))

我们会这样使用它： We would use this as follows:

(test ((o 'add1) 5) 6)

旁注：注意，基本对象是对 lambda 的一种泛化，让它具有多个“入口点”。反过来，lambda 就是只有一个入口点的对象；因此，它不需要“方法名”来消除歧义。 Aside:  Observe that basic objects are a generalization of lambda  to have multiple “entry-points”. Conversely, a lambda  is an object with only one  entry-point; therefore, it doesn’t need a “method name” to disambiguate.

当然，用这些嵌套的函数调用来编写方法调用很不方便（而且马上会变得更不方便），所以最好给自己配上一种方便的方法调用语法： Of course, writing method invocations with these nested function calls is unwieldy (and is about to become even more so), so we’d be best off equipping ourselves with a convenient syntax for invoking methods:

(define (msg o m . a)

  (apply (o m) a))

这样，我们就可以重写测试： This enables us to rewrite our test:

(test (msg o 'add1 5) 6)

旁注：我们利用了 Racket 的可变元数语法：. a 表示“将所有剩余的实参——零个或多个——绑定为一个名为 a 的列表”。apply 函数会将这样的实参列表“拼接”进去，用来调用函数。 Aside:  We’ve taken advantage of Racket’s variable-arity syntax: . a  says “bind all the remaining—zero or more—arguments to a list named a ”. The apply  function “splices” in such lists of arguments to call functions.

注意我们语言中一件非常微妙的事：没有任何东西阻止我们在 msg 调用的第二个位置写任意表达式。也就是说，我们可以计算出自己想访问哪个成员。例如： Observe something very subtle about our language: nothing precludes us from writing an arbitrary expression in the second position of a call to msg . That is, we can compute  which member we want to access. For instance:

(test (msg o (first '(add1)) 5) 6)

这与许多具有对象的语言不同，它们会强制你直接写出成员名称的字面形式（例如 Java 在大多数情况下就是如此）。后面我们还会回到这一点！ This is unlike many languages with objects, which force you to write the literal name  of the member (e.g., in Java, in most cases). We’ll return to this later!

旁注：这是脱糖的一个普遍问题：目标语言可能允许某些在源语言中没有对应形式的表达式，因此无法将它们映射回去。幸运的是，我们不常需要进行这种逆向映射，不过某些调试工具和程序理解工具确实需要它。更微妙的是，我们必须确保目标语言不会产生在源语言中没有对应等价物的值。 Aside:  This is a general problem with desugaring: the target language may allow expressions that have no counterpart in the source, and hence cannot be mapped back to it. Fortunately we don’t often need to perform this inverse mapping, though it does arise in some debugging and program comprehension tools. More subtly, however, we must ensure that the target language does not produce values  that have no corresponding equivalent in the source.

既然已经有了基本对象，就开始加入我们习惯在大多数对象系统中看到的那些功能吧。 Now that we have basic objects, let’s start adding the kinds of features we’ve come to expect from most object systems.

“对象”模式 The “Object” Pattern

我们可以将上面编写的内容归纳为“对象”模式：看起来像下面这样的代码 We can consolidate what we have written above as the “object” pattern: code that looks like

  (lambda (m)

    (case m

      … dispatch on each of the members …))

构造器 Constructors

构造器只是一个在构造对象时调用的函数。我们目前还没有这样的功能，但只要把对象从字面量改为一个接收构造器参数的函数，就能实现这种效果： A constructor is simply a function that is invoked at object construction time. We currently lack such a feature, but by turning an object from a literal into a function that takes constructor parameters, we achieve this effect:

(define (o-constr x)

  (lambda (m)

    (case m

      [(addX) (lambda (y) (+ x y))])))

 

(test (msg (o-constr 5) 'addX 3) 8)

(test (msg (o-constr 2) 'addX 3) 5)

在第一个例子中，我们传入 5 作为构造器的实参，因此加上 3 得到 8。第二个例子类似，并且表明两次构造器调用不会相互干扰（正如我们根据静态作用域所预期的那样）。 In the first example, we pass 5 as the constructor’s argument, so adding 3 yields 8. The second is similar, and shows that the two invocations of the constructors don’t interfere with one another (just as we would expect from static scope).

“类”模式 The “Class” Pattern

通过这一点小小的添加，我们其实做出了相当重大的改变：我们从对象转向了创建对象的函数（注意函数内部的对象模式）。但传统上，是什么创建对象呢？是类！而类通常都有构造器。因此，在引入构造器的过程中，我们实际上也从对象转向了类。最简单的“类”模式是： We’ve actually made quite a momentous change with this small addition: we’ve gone from objects to functions-that-make-objects (notice the object pattern inside the function). But traditionally, what makes objects? Classes! And classes typically have constructors. So in the process of introducing constructors, we have actually also shifted from objects to classes. The “class” pattern, at its simplest, is:

(define (class constructor-params)

  … the object pattern …)

状态 State

许多人认为，对象的主要用途是封装状态。 Many people believe that objects primarily exist to encapsulate state.

旁注：有趣的是，因发明 Smalltalk 和现代对象技术而获得图灵奖的 Alan Kay 并不同意这种看法。在《Smalltalk 的早期历史》（The Early History of Smalltalk）中，他说：“［面向对象编程的动机］在小尺度上，是寻找一种更灵活的赋值形式，然后尝试将赋值彻底消除。”他又说：“不幸的是，今天很多所谓的‘面向对象编程’，不过是使用更花哨构造的旧式编程。许多程序充斥着‘赋值式’操作，只不过现在由成本更高的附带过程来完成。” Aside:  Curiously, Alan Kay, who won a Turing Award for inventing Smalltalk and modern object technology, disagrees. In The Early History of Smalltalk , he says, “[t]he small scale [motivation for OOP] was to find a more flexible version of assignment, and then to try to eliminate it altogether”. He adds, “It is unfortunate that much of what is called ‘object-oriented programming’ today is simply old style programming with fancier constructs. Many programs are loaded with ‘assignment-style’ operations now done by more expensive attached procedures.”

我们当然没有丧失这种能力。如果脱糖的目标语言具有变量，就可以轻松地让多个方法修改共同的状态，比如某个构造器参数： We certainly haven’t lost that ability. If we desugar to a language with variables, we can easily have multiple methods mutate common state, such as a constructor argument:

(define (mk-o-state count)

  (lambda (m)

    (case m

      [(inc) (lambda () (set! count (+ count 1)))]

      [(dec) (lambda () (set! count (- count 1)))]

      [(get) (lambda () count)])))

我们把名称改成 mk-o-…，以体现它是一个对象制造器，也就是类似于类的东西。例如，我们可以测试一系列操作： We have changed the name to mk-o-…  to reflect the fact that this is an object- maker , i.e., analogous to a class. For instance, we can test a sequence of operations:

(test (let ([o (mk-o-state 5)])

        (begin (msg o 'inc)

                   (msg o 'inc)

               (msg o 'dec)

               (msg o 'get)))

      6)

还可以注意到，修改一个对象不会影响另一个： and also notice that mutating one object doesn’t affect another:

(test (let ([o1 (mk-o-state 3)]

            [o2 (mk-o-state 3)])

        (begin (msg o1 'inc)

               (msg o1 'inc)

               (+ (msg o1 'get)

                  (msg o2 'get))))

      (+ 5 3))

私有成员 Private Members

在我们的对象模式中，只要将成员名称传给对象，就可以访问 case 中的任何内容。不过，对象语言通常希望某些成员是私有的，也就是说，仅在对象内部可见，在外部不可见。例如在 Java 这样的语言中，通常用关键字 private 来标记它们（既包括字段，也包括方法）。这类成员用来控制不应被外界访问的数据（例如用于给内容签名的密码学私钥）。 In our object pattern, anything in the case  can be accessed by passing its member name to the object. However, it is common for object languages to want to have some members be private , i.e., visible only inside the object, not outside it. In languages like Java, for instance, the keyword private  is often used to designate them (both fields and methods). These kinds of members are used to control data that should not be accessed by the outside world (e.g., a private cryptographic key that is used to sign content).

旁注：不过，在 Java 中，同一类型的类的其他实例也可以访问“私有”成员。否则，你根本无法实现抽象数据类型。注意，类并不是抽象数据类型！ Aside:  Except that, in Java, other instances of classes of the same type are privy to “private” members. Otherwise, you would simply never be able to implement an Abstract Data Type. Note that classes are not Abstract Data Types!

旁注：稍微想一想，你可能就会意识到，私有成员还不够。以密码学密钥为例。我们可以让一个私有成员引用它，但这不意味着没有其他并非私有的引用——也就是别名！——也指向它，从而可能将它泄露出去！因此，使用私有成员时，通常还必须结合对别名的推理。 Aside:  If you think about this a bit, you may realize that private members are not enough. Consider the cryptographic key. We may have a private member refer to it. However, that doesn’t mean there aren’t other  references to it—that is, aliases!—that are not  private, and hence may leak it! Thus, private members must often be used in conjunction with reasoning about aliasing.

私有成员看起来可能是需要额外实现的一项功能，但我们已经有了必要机制：具有局部作用域、按词法绑定的变量。为了避免深入密码学等领域的细节，我们用一个简单的计数器对象示例来说明；它提供递增、递减和显示计数的方法： Private members may seem like an additional feature we need to implement, but we already have the necessary mechanism in the form of locally-scoped, lexically-bound variables. To avoid diving into the details of domains like cryptography, we will illustrate this with a simple example of a counter object that provides methods to increment, decrement, and show the count:

(define (mk-o-state/priv init)
