  (let ([count init])

    (lambda (m)

      (case m

        [(inc) (lambda () (set! count (+ count 1)))]

        [(dec) (lambda () (set! count (- count 1)))]

        [(get) (lambda () count)]))))

上面的代码使用词法作用域，确保 count 对外界保持隐藏。试图从外部直接访问 count 会失败；唯一可见的成员是 case 所处理的那些。 The code above uses lexical scoping to ensure that count  remains hidden to the world. Trying to access count  directly from the outside will fail; the only members visible are those that case  handles.

练习：如果直接脱糖为上面的代码，公有成员显然可以引用私有成员（就像上面引用 count 一样）；但私有成员能引用公有成员吗？如果能，给出一个展示这种做法有效的例子。如果不能，请修正脱糖模式！ Exercise:  If we were to directly desugar to the code above, public members can clearly refer to private ones (as they refer to count , above); but can private members refer to public ones? If so, give an example that shows this working. If not, fix the desugaring pattern!

改进的“类”模式 A Refined “Class” Pattern

有了这一变化，我们现在可以改进类的模式： With this change, we can now refine our pattern for classes:

(define (class-w/-private constructor-params)

  (let ([private-vars …] …)

    … the object pattern …))

也可以把它写成： which we can also write as:

(define class-w/-private

  (lambda (constructor-params)

    (let ([private-vars …] …)

      … the object pattern …)))

我们很快就会看到，为什么可能想这样做。 We’ll see in a moment why we might want to do this.

静态成员 Static Members

对对象使用者而言，另一项通常很有价值的功能是静态成员：同一种对象的所有实例所共有的成员。不过，这只不过是一个具有词法作用域（使其私有）、且位于构造器外部（使其为构造器的所有使用所共有）的标识符。 Another feature often valuable to users of objects is static members: those that are common to all instances of the same type of object. This, however, is merely a lexically-scoped identifier (making it private) that lives outside the constructor (making it common to all uses of the constructor).

假设我们想记录某种对象一共创建了多少个实例。这个计数不能放在这些对象中的任何一个内部，因为它们不会“知道”彼此；相反，构造器需要跟踪这件事。这就是静态成员的作用。在下面的例子中，变量 counter 就扮演了这个角色： Suppose we want to keep a count of how many instances of a kind of object are created. This count cannot be inside any one of those objects, because they would not “know” about each other; rather, the constructor needs to keep track of this. This is the role of static members, and the variable counter  plays this role in the following example:

(define mk-o-static

  (let ([counter 0])

    (lambda (amount)

      (begin

        (set! counter (+ 1 counter))

        (lambda (m)

          (case m

            [(inc) (lambda (n) (set! amount (+ amount n)))]

            [(dec) (lambda (n) (set! amount (- amount n)))]

            [(get) (lambda () amount)]

            [(count) (lambda () counter)]))))))

我们将 counter 的递增写在了这个对象的“构造器”所在的位置，不过也完全可以在方法内部操作它。 We’ve written the counter increment where the “constructor” for this object would go, though it could just as well be manipulated inside the methods.

为了测试它，我们应该创建多个对象，并确保每个对象都会影响全局计数： To test it, we should make multiple objects and ensure they each affect the global count:

(test (let ([o (mk-o-static 1000)])

        (msg o 'count))

      1)

 

(test (let ([o (mk-o-static 0)])

        (msg o 'count))

      2)

用 Stacker 看看这个程序如何运行，会很有收获。为简单起见，我们可以忽略大部分细节，只关注静态成员的核心模式。下面是一个适合 Stacker 的翻译版本： It is productive to see how this program runs through the Stacker. For simplicity, we can ignore most of the details and focus just on the core static pattern. Here is a Stacker-friendly translation:

#lang stacker/smol/hof

(defvar mk-o-static

  (let ([counter 0])

    (lambda (amount)

      (begin

        (set! counter (+ 1 counter))

        (lambda (m)

          (if (equal? m "get")

              (lambda () amount)

              (if (equal? m "count")

                  counter

                  (error "no such member"))))))))

(defvar o1 (mk-o-static 1000))

(defvar o2 (mk-o-static 0))

(o1 "count")

(o2 "count")

运行它，看看静态成员是如何工作的！ Run this and see how the static member works!

再次改进的“类”模式 A Re-Refined “Class” Pattern

现在，我们可以进一步改进类的模式： Now we can refine our pattern for classes even further:

(define class-w/-private&static

  (let ([static-vars …] …)

    (lambda (constructor-params)

      (let ([private-vars …] …)

        … the object pattern …))))

换一种写法： Put differently:

(define class-w/-private&static

  (let ([static-vars …] …)

    … the class-w/-private pattern …))

练习：按照这里的定义，静态成员是通过对象访问的。然而，静态成员按定义属于类，而不属于对象，因此应该能够通过类本身访问——例如，即便从未创建过该类的实例也能访问。（在上面可以运行的例子中，应该在计数仍为 0 时就能访问它。）修改上面的模式，让静态成员可以直接通过类而非对象访问，以满足这一要求。 Exercise: Statics, as defined here, are accessed through objects . However, statics by definition belong to a class , not to objects, and hence should be accessible through the class itself—for instance, even if no instances of the class have ever been created. (In the working example above, one should be able to access the count when it is still 0 .) Modify the pattern above to respect this by making static members be accessible directly through the class  rather than through objects.

具有自引用的对象 Objects with Self Reference

到目前为止，我们的对象只是一些具名函数的集合：你也可以说，它们是具有多个具名入口点的函数。我们已经看到，许多在对象系统中被认为很重要的功能，其实都是建立在函数和作用域之上的简单模式，而且几十年来，掌握了 lambda 的程序员一直在使用它们，只是没有给它们命名而已。 Until now, our objects have simply been packages of named functions: functions with multiple named entry-points, if you will. We’ve seen that many of the features considered important in object systems are actually simple patterns over functions and scope, and have indeed been used—without names assigned to them—for decades by programmers armed with lambdas.

这意味着，不同成员实际上相互独立：例如，它们无法直接引用彼此。对于真正的对象系统来说，这种限制太大了；在真正的对象系统里，方法能够引用自己所属的对象，从而使用该对象的其他成员。为此，许多对象系统会自动给每个对象配上一个指向自身的引用，通常叫作 self 或 this。我们能实现这一点吗？ What this means is that the different members are actually independent of each other: they can’t, for instance, directly reference one another. This is too limiting for a true object system, where a method has a way of referencing the object it is part of so that it can use other members of that object. To enable this, many object systems automatically equip each object with a reference to itself, often called self  or this . Can we implement this?

旁注：相比对象倡导者经常采用的“了解自己”这种拟人化术语，我更喜欢这种略显枯燥的表述。事实上，注意一下：我们已经深入探讨了这么多对象系统的性质，却从未需要借助拟人化说法。 Aside : I prefer this slightly dry way of putting it to the anthropomorphic “knows about itself” terminology often adopted by object advocates. Indeed, note that we have gotten this far into object system properties without ever needing to resort to anthropomorphism.

使用修改实现自引用 Self-Reference Using Mutation

当然能！这依赖一种模式：先设置好用于递归引用的名称，再用它创建将使用递归的主体，最后通过修改，让该名称引用已定义的主体。为简单起见，我们回到对象模式，忽略与类有关的功能： Yes, we can! This relies on a pattern that sets up the name for the recursive reference, then uses that to create the body that will employ the recursion, and finally uses mutation to make the name refer to the defined body. For simplicity, we will go back to the  object  pattern, ignoring the class-related features:

(define o-self!

  (let ([self 'dummy])

    (begin

      (set! self

            (lambda (m)

              (case m

                [(first) (lambda (x) (msg self 'second (+ x 1)))]

                [(second) (lambda (x) (+ x 1))])))

      self)))

我们可以让 first 调用 second 来测试它。果然，这会产生预期答案： We can test it by having first  invoke second . Sure enough, this produces the expected answer:

(test (msg o-self! 'first 5) 7)

下面是将上述程序翻译成更简单的 smol/fun 语言后的结果。翻译后，就可以在 Stacker 中运行它： Here is the above program translated into the simpler smol/fun language. Once translated, we can run it in the Stacker:

#lang stacker/smol/hof

(defvar o-self!

  (let ([self 0])

    (begin

      (set! self

            (lambda (m)

              (if (equal? m "first")

                  (lambda (x) ((self "second") (+ x 1)))

                  (if (equal? m "second")

                      (lambda (x) (+ x 1))

                      (error "no such member")))))

      self)))

((o-self! "first") 5)

亲自运行一下！你从中学到了什么？你看懂 self 是如何工作的吗？ Run it for yourself! What do you learn from it? Do you see how self  works?

旁注：这种模式——先将变量绑定到一个占位值（使其可见），再修改它，使其具有真正的（递归）定义——正是 letrec 或其他递归 let 构造的核心。 Aside: This pattern—of binding a variable to a dummy value (so that it is visible), then mutating it to have its true (recursive) definition—is at the heart of letrec  or other recursive let  constructs.

练习：对对象模式的这一改动，基本上独立于类模式。扩展类模式，使其包含自引用。 Exercise:  This change to the object pattern is essentially independent  of the class pattern. Extend the class pattern to include self-reference.

不使用修改实现自引用 Self-Reference Without Mutation

还有另一种可以避免修改的模式：将对象本身作为参数传入： There’s another pattern we can use that avoids mutation, which is to send the object itself as a parameter:

(define o-self-no!

  (lambda (m)

    (case m

      [(first) (lambda (self x) (msg/self self 'second (+ x 1)))]

      [(second) (lambda (self x) (+ x 1))])))

现在，每个方法都接收 self 作为实参。这意味着方法调用必须修改，以遵循这个新模式： Each method now takes self  as an argument. That means method invocation must be modified to follow this new pattern:

(define (msg/self o m . a)

  (apply (o m) o a))

也就是说，在 o 上调用某个方法时，必须将 o 作为参数传给该方法。注意，调用函数时，我们可没有做过这样的事！这就区分了函数和方法。 That is, when invoking a method on o , we must pass o  as a parameter to the method. Notice that we did not do any such thing when invoking a function! This distinguishes functions and methods.

显然，这种方法很危险，因为我们可能传入另一个对象作为“self”。因此，将这一机制暴露给开发者大概不是个好主意；如果采用这种实现技巧，它应该只在脱糖中使用。（不幸的是，Python 的表层语法恰恰暴露了它。）果然： Obviously, this approach is dangerous because we can potentially pass a different object as the “self”. Exposing this to the developer is therefore probably a bad idea; if this implementation technique is used, it should only be done in desugaring. (Unfortunately, Python exposes exactly this in its surface syntax.) Sure enough:

(test (msg/self o-self-no! 'first 5) 7)

动态分派 Dynamic Dispatch

最后，我们应该确保对象能够支持对象系统的一项标志性特征：调用方法时，调用方不必知道或决定由哪个对象来处理此次调用。 Finally, we should make sure our objects can handle a characteristic attribute of object systems, which is the ability to invoke a method without the caller having to know or decide which object will handle the invocation.

假设有一种二叉树数据结构，其中树由空节点或持有一个值的叶节点组成。使用传统函数时，我们不得不实现某种条件判断——比如 type-case——穷尽地列出不同种类的树，并在其中选择。如果树的定义扩展了，包含了新的树种类，那么这些代码片段中的每一处都必须修改。 Suppose we have a binary tree data structure, where a tree consists of either empty nodes or leaves that hold a value. In traditional functions, we are forced to implement some form of conditional—such as a type-case —that exhaustively lists and selects between the different kinds of trees. If the definition of a tree grows to include new kinds of trees, each of these code fragments must be modified.

动态分派通过让这种条件分支从用户程序中消失，改由语言内置的方法选择代码处理，来解决这个问题。它提供的关键功能是一种可扩展的条件构造。这是对象所提供的可扩展性的一个维度。 Dynamic dispatch solves this problem by making that conditional branch disappear from the user’s program and instead be handled by the method selection code built into the language. The key feature that this provides is an extensible conditional. This is one dimension of the extensibility that objects provide.

先来定义两种树对象： Let’s first define our two kinds of tree objects:

(define (mt)

  (let ([self 'dummy])

    (begin

      (set! self

            (lambda (m)

              (case m

                [(sum) (lambda () 0)])))

      self)))

 

(define (node v l r)

  (let ([self 'dummy])

    (begin

      (set! self

            (lambda (m)

              (case m

                [(sum) (lambda () (+ v

                                     (msg l 'sum)

                                     (msg r 'sum)))])))

      self)))

有了它们，就能创建一棵具体的树： With these, we can make a concrete tree:

(define a-tree

  (node 10

        (node 5 (mt) (mt))

        (node 15 (node 6 (mt) (mt)) (mt))))

最后，测试它： And finally, test it:

(test (msg a-tree 'sum) (+ 10 5 15 6))

注意，无论是在测试用例中，还是在 node 的 sum 方法中，都引用了 ’sum，而没有检查接收者是 mt 还是 node。相反，语言的运行时系统会提取接收者的 sum 方法并调用它。这种从用户程序中消失、由语言自动处理的条件判断，就是动态分派的本质。 Observe that both in the test case and in the sum  method of node , there is a reference to ’sum  without checking whether the recipient is a mt  or node . Instead, the language’s run-time system  extracts the recipient’s sum  method and invokes it. This conditional missing from the user’s program, and handled automatically by the language,  is the essence of dynamic dispatch.

值得注意的是，我们不必为了加入动态分派而修改模式；它只是整个设计的其余部分自然带来的结果。 It’s worth noting that we didn’t have to change our pattern to add dynamic dispatch; it simply followed as a result of the rest of the design .

旁注：这一性质似乎使系统更易于进行黑盒扩展，因为系统的一部分可以增长，而不必修改另一部分来适应这些变化，因此它经常被誉为面向对象的一项关键优势。虽然这确实是对象相对于函数的优势，但函数相对于对象也有一个对偶的优势；事实上，许多对象程序员最终会使用访问者模式，把代码扭来扭去，使其看起来更像是按函数组织的。阅读《综合面向对象设计和函数式设计以促进复用》（Synthesizing Object-Oriented and Functional Design to Promote Re-Use），其中贯穿始终的例子会充分展现这个问题。尝试用你最喜欢的语言解决它，再看看 Racket 的解法。 Aside:  This property—which appears to make systems more black-box extensible because one part of the system can grow without the other part needing to be modified to accommodate those changes—is often hailed as a key benefit of object-orientation. While this is indeed an advantage objects have over functions, there is a dual advantage that functions have over objects, and indeed many object programmers end up contorting their code—using the Visitor pattern—to make it look more like a function-based organization. Read Synthesizing Object-Oriented and Functional Design to Promote Re-Use  for a running example that will lay out the problem in its full glory. Try to solve it in your favorite language, and see the Racket solution .

对象还有什么？ What Else do Objects Have?

成员名称的设计空间 Member Name Design Space

现在，我们重点关注成员的名称（我们用“成员”这个词，是为了不区分字段和方法）。另外，暂时先不区分类和对象：不管是否通过类，我们最终得到的都是程序所使用的对象。因此，有两个问题： Now we will focus on the names of members (a term we use to not distinguish between fields and methods). Also, let’s set aside the distinction between classes and objects for a moment: whether through classes or not, we eventually end up with objects, which programs use. So the two questions are:

  • 成员名称的集合是静态固定的，还是可以动态改变？ Is the set of member names statically fixed, or can it be changed dynamically?
  • 某处访问的成员是静态固定的，还是可以动态计算出来？ Is the member being accessed at a point statically fixed, or can it be computed dynamically?

由此得到一个 2×2 的表格，值得问一问，每个格子是否都有意义（以及我们是否在某种现实语言中见过它）。结果如下： This gives us a 2x2 table, and it’s worthwhile to ask whether each cell makes sense (and whether we’ve seen it in any real languages). We get:

名称是静态的 Name is Static

名称是计算出来的 Name is Computed

成员集合固定 Fixed Set of Members

如基本 Java。 As in base Java.

如 Java 使用反射来计算名称。 As in Java with reflection to compute the name.

成员集合可变 Variable Set of Members

难以想象（有什么用呢？）。 Difficult to envision (what use would it be?).

大多数“脚本”语言。 Most “scripting” languages.

只有一种情况不太有意义：如果要访问的成员必须在源程序中固定下来，那么名称集合就已经预先决定了，所以似乎没有必要再允许动态改变成员集合（新增成员无法访问，而删除成员会使某些现有访问失败）。不过，这个设计空间中的其他所有位置，都已经有语言探索过。 Only one case does not quite make sense: if the member being accessed must be fixed in the source program, then the set of names is pre-decided, so it doesn’t seem to make sense to be able to dynamically change the set of members (new members would not be accessible, while deleted members would cause some existing accesses to fail). All other points in this design space have, however, been explored by languages.

右下象限与使用哈希表表示对象的语言密切对应。此时，名称不过是哈希表的索引。有些语言把这一点推到极致，连数字索引也使用同样的表示，从而（例如）把对象与字典、甚至数组混为一谈。即便对象只处理“成员名称”，这种对象风格也会给类型检查带来很大困难，因此并非必然值得采用。 The lower-right quadrant corresponds closely with languages that use hash-tables to represent objects. Then the name is simply the index into the hash-table. Some languages carry this to an extreme and use the same representation even for numeric indices, thereby (for instance) conflating objects with dictionaries and even arrays. Even when the object only handles “member names”, this style of object creates significant difficulty for type-checking and is hence not automatically desirable.

所以，在本节余下内容中，我们将坚持使用“传统”对象：它们具有固定的名称集合，甚至连成员名称引用都是静态的（左上象限）。即便如此，我们仍会发现，还有非常非常多的东西值得研究。 Therefore, in the rest of this section, we will stick with “traditional” objects that have a fixed set of names and even static member name references (the top-left quadrant). Even then, we will find there is much, much more to study.

else 里面还放什么？ What (Goes In) Else?

到目前为止，我们的 case 表达式还没有 else 子句。加入它的一个理由是，对象可能具有可变的成员集合，不过这大概更适合用条件构造之外的其他表示来处理：例如上面讨论过的哈希表。相比之下，如果对象的成员集合固定，脱糖为条件构造就很适合用来演示（因为它强调了成员名称集合的固定性质，而哈希表在这一点上留下了解释的余地，也留下了出错的余地）。不过，else 子句还有另一个用途：将控制“链接”到另一个父对象。这就叫作继承。 Until now, our case  expressions have not had an else  clause. One reason to do so would be if we had a variable set of members in an object, though that is probably better handled through a different representation than a conditional: a hash-table, for instance, as we’ve discussed above. In contrast, if an object’s set of members is fixed, desugaring to a conditional works well for the purpose of illustration (because it emphasizes  the fixed nature of the set of member names, which a hash table leaves open to interpretation—and also error). There is, however, another reason for an else  clause, which is to “chain” control to another, parent, object. This is called inheritance .

回到脱糖后的对象模型。要实现继承，就必须给对象一个“东西”，让它能将自己不认识的方法调用委托给这个东西。很多事情都取决于这个“东西”究竟是什么。 Let’s return to our model of desugared objects. To implement inheritance, the object must be given “something” to which it can delegate method invocations that it does not recognize. A great deal will depend on what that “something” is.

一种答案是，它就是另一个对象： One answer could be that it is simply another object:

(case m

  ...

  [else (parent-object m)])

根据我们表示对象的方式，这次应用实际上会在父对象中查找成员（并且大概会递归地在它的各级父对象中查找）。如果找到了名称匹配的成员，就沿着这条链返回到最初在 msg 中查找该成员的调用。如果没找到，最后一个对象大概就会发出“未找到消息”的错误。 Due to our representation of objects, this application effectively searches for the member in the parent object (and, presumably, recursively in its parents). If a member matching the name is found, it returns through this chain to the original call in msg  that sought the member. If none is found, the final object presumably signals a “message not found” error.

练习：如果你知道什么是左值，可能会注意到，应用 (parent-object m) 就像“半个 msg”，正如左值是“半次值查找”一样。这之间有什么联系吗？ Exercise:  If you know what an l-value is, then you might notice that the application (parent-object m)  is like “half a msg ”, just like an l-value was “half a value lookup”. Is there any connection?

我们来扩展树，让它实现另一个方法 size，以此试一试。我们将分别为 node 和 mt 编写一个“扩展”（你可能很想说“子类”，但先别急！），以实现 size 方法。我们打算用它们扩展现有的 node 和 mt 定义，因此会采用上面描述的扩展模式。换句话说，如果之前的代码大致相当于这段 Java 代码： Let’s try this by extending our trees to implement another method, size . We’ll write an “extension” (you may be tempted to say “sub-class”, but hold off for now!) for each node  and mt  to implement the size  method. We intend these to extend the existing definitions of node  and mt , so we’ll use the extension pattern described above. In other words, if we previously had the rough equivalent of this Java code:

class Mt   { … Mt()          { … } sum() { … } }

class Node { … Node(v, l, r) { … } sum() { … } }

现在，我们希望扩展它： now we want to extend it:

class MtSize   extends Mt   { … size() { … } … }

class NodeSize extends Node { … size() { … } … }

旁注：我们不修改现有定义，因为对象继承的全部意义本该就是以黑盒方式复用代码。这也意味着，彼此互不相识的不同参与者，都可以各自扩展同一份基础代码。如果必须修改基础代码，他们首先就得找到彼此，而且其中一方可能不喜欢另一方的修改。继承的目的，就是彻底绕过这些问题。 Aside:  We’re not editing the existing definitions because that is supposed to be the whole point of object inheritance: to reuse code in a black-box fashion. This also means different parties, who do not know one another, can each extend the same base code. If they had to edit the base, first they have to find out about each other, and in addition, one might dislike the edits of the other. Inheritance is meant to sidestep these issues entirely.

旁注：与此相关，可以读一读“脆弱基类问题”。 Aside: Relatedly, read about the fragile base class problem .

绕道看看 Java A Java Excursion

先来理解 Java 中发生了什么。为简单起见，我们使用一个典型的“二维点”和“三维点”示例。从这个类开始： Let’s first understand what’s going on in Java. For simplicity, let’s use a canonical “2d point” and “3d point” example. We’ll start with this class:

class Pt2 {

    Pt2(int x, int y) {

        System.out.println("Pt2 with " + x + " and " + y);

    }

}

创建它的实例很容易： We can make instances of it easily enough:

class Main {

    public static void main(String[] args) {

        Pt2 p2 = new Pt2(1, 2);

    }

}

它会打印出预期的输出。现在假设我们扩展这个类： and this prints the expected output. Now suppose we extend this class:

class Pt3 extends Pt2 {

    Pt3(int x, int y, int z) {

        System.out.println("Pt3 with " + z);

    }

}

它甚至无法通过编译。我们会得到一条看起来有点奇怪的错误信息。错误的原因是，Java 还想创建一个 Pt2 实例，但我们没有告诉它如何创建。在没有其他说明时，它会调用一个“默认构造器”，这个构造器不接受参数（因为 Java 无从知道该传哪些参数）。如果我们将 Pt2 改为 This won’t even compile . We will get a somewhat strange-looking error. The error is because Java is expecting to make an instance of Pt2  as well, but we have not told it how to. In the absence of anything else, it invokes a “default constructor”, which takes no  parameters (because Java has no way of knowing which parameters to pass). If we modify Pt2  to instead be

class Pt2 {

   Pt2() {

       System.out.println("default constructor");

   }

    Pt2(int x, int y) {

        System.out.println("Pt2 with " + x + " and " + y);

    }

}

就会发现程序可以通过编译，而且，如果适当修改 Main， then we find that the program compiles and, if we change Main  suitably,

class Main {

  public static void main(String[] args) {

    Pt3 p3 = new Pt3(1, 2, 3);

  }

}

程序也能运行，但效果可能并非我们所期望的。用 Java 的术语来说，解决办法是显式调用超类的构造器： it runs, but perhaps without the effect we were expecting. The solution, in Java terms, is to explicitly invoke the constructor of the super-class:

class Pt3 extends Pt2 {

    Pt3(int x, int y, int z) {

        System.out.println("Pt3 with " + z);

        super(x, y);

    }

}

不过，这样仍然不行：Java 要求 super 调用必须是子类构造器中的第一件事。 but this won’t work either: Java expects the super  invocation to be the first  thing in the sub-class’s constructor.

正如上面的错误信息所揭示的那样，扩展后的类的构造器内部，潜藏着一件重要的事：它会尝试创建一个超类实例，就像我们写了 new Pt2 一样。这被 super 这层语法糖完全遮住了。真正的 Pt2 实例藏在视线之外，需要费一点工夫才能把它引出来。 As the error message above reveals, hidden in the constructor of the extended class is lurking something important: it tries to create an instance  of the super-class, just as if we had written new Pt2 . This is entirely masked by the syntactic sugar of super . The actual Pt2  instance is hidden out of sight, and it takes a little effort to coax it into view.

为了看到它，先添加几个实例变量： To see it, let’s first add some instance variables:

class Pt2 {

    public int x;

    Pt2(int x, int y) {

        this.x = x - 3;

        System.out.println("Pt2 with " + x + " and " + y);

    }

}

class Pt3 extends Pt2 {

    public int x;

    Pt3(int x, int y, int z) {

        super(x, y);

        this.x = x + 7;

        System.out.println("Pt3 with " + z);

    }

}

我们特意让实例变量的值与参数的值看起来不同，这样在检查它们时就能分辨。现在修改构造器，让它创建两个对象： We’ve purposely made the instance variables have values that look different from those of the parameters, so that when we try to examine them, we can tell them apart. Now let’s modify the constructor to make two objects:

class Main {

    public static void main(String[] args) {

        Pt3 p3345 = new Pt3(3, 4, 5);

        Pt3 p3678 = new Pt3(6, 7, 8);

    }

}

两个对象……我们究竟创建了多少个对象？嗯，至少创建了两个，因为将 Two  objects…how many objects did we really make? Well, we made at least  two, because adding

        System.out.println(p3345.x);

        System.out.println(p3678.x);

加入构造器后，就能看出有两个不同的对象，它们的 x 值也不同。到目前为止，这并不令人意外。 to the constructor shows that there are two different objects with two different values for x . So far, so unsurprising.

不过，我声称还有两个类型为 Pt2 的对象。我们能看见它们吗？能，确实可以。问题在于，它们的类型是 Pt2，而我们手里的是 Pt3 对象。不能直接创建一个 Pt2，因为那样并不会揭示隐藏的 Pt2。不过，Java 的类型系统实际上允许我们通过强制类型转换访问那个 Pt2： However, I’ve claimed that there are two more objects, of type Pt2 . Can we see  them? Yes, in fact, we can. The problem is that they’re of type Pt2 , and what we have are Pt3  objects. We can’t just make a Pt2 , because that doesn’t reveal the hidden   Pt2 . But in fact the Java type system lets us get to the Pt2  by casting :

        System.out.println(((Pt2)p3345).x);

        System.out.println(((Pt2)p3678).x);

这样，我们就能看到，实际上还潜藏着两个 Pt2 对象！ And that’s how we can see that there are actually two Pt2  objects lurking as well!

扩展类 Extending Classes

现在，得把所有这些代码移植到我们的脱糖世界中。构造器模式是这样的吗？ Now we have to port all this code over to our world of desugaring. Is this the constructor pattern?

(define (node/size parent-object v l r)

  ...)

这表明父对象与对象的构造器字段处于“同一层次”。这似乎很合理，因为一旦给定了所有这些参数，对象就“完全定义好了”。不过，我们仍然还有 That suggests that the parent is at the “same level” as the object’s constructor fields. That seems reasonable, in that once all these parameters are given, the object is “fully defined”. However, we also still have

(define (node v l r)

  ...)

这里的关键问题是，我们需要创建两个对象：一个 node/size 对象，以及另一个 node 对象。可以设想一种协议，让 node/size 的使用者构造一个 node 对象，再把它传给 node/size，但这样他们可能犯下各种各样的错误。另一种做法是，交由 node/size 调用 node，并保存这个过程中构造的对象。也就是说，node/size 的 parent 参数不应是父对象，而应是父对象的制造器。 The crucial issue here is that we need to make two  objects: one of node/size  and one more of node . We could imagine a protocol where the user of node/size  constructs a node  object and passes it to node/size , but in doing so, they could make any number of mistakes. Alternatively, we can leave it to node/size  to invoke node, and keep track of the object constructed through this process. That is, node/size ’s parent parameter should not be the parent object  but rather the parent object’s maker .

(define (node/size parent-maker v l r)

  (let ([parent-object (parent-maker v l r)]

        [self 'dummy])

    (begin

      (set! self

            (lambda (m)

              (case m

                [(size) (lambda () (+ 1

                                     (msg l 'size)

                                     (msg r 'size)))]

                [else (parent-object m)])))

      self)))

 

(define (mt/size parent-maker)

  (let ([parent-object (parent-maker)]

        [self 'dummy])

    (begin

      (set! self

            (lambda (m)

              (case m

                [(size) (lambda () 0)]

                [else (parent-object m)])))

      self)))

那么，对象构造器必须记得在每次调用时传入父对象制造器： Then the object constructor must remember to pass the parent-object maker on every invocation:

(define a-tree/size

  (node/size node

             10

             (node/size node 5 (mt/size mt) (mt/size mt))

             (node/size node 15

                        (node/size node 6 (mt/size mt) (mt/size mt))

                        (mt/size mt))))

旁注：注意调用“超”类的模式反复出现：例如 (mt/size mt)。我们更希望只做一次。本质上，mt/size 与 mt 的这种绑定，恰恰就是 Java 中 extends 子句所做的事。我们可以在这里模拟它，但在本章后面会看到一种优雅得多的做法，既能达成这一目的，又能让使用类进行编程更加灵活。 Aside:  Note the repeated pattern of invoking the “super” class: e.g., (mt/size mt) . We would instead want to do this just once. Essentially, this binding of mt/size  to mt  is precisely what the extends  clause of Java does. We could simulate that here, but later in this chapter we’ll see a much more elegant way of achieving this end while also making programming with classes much more flexible.

我们可以确认，新旧测试都仍然有效： We can confirm that both the old and new tests still work:

(test (msg a-tree/size 'sum) (+ 10 5 15 6))

(test (msg a-tree/size 'size) 4)

练习：使用自应用而不是修改，重写这一段代码。 Exercise:  Rewrite this block of code using self-application instead of mutation.

我们所做的，是捕捉类的本质。每个以父级为参数的函数都是……嗯，其实有点难说。我们暂且叫它类扩展，很快就会知道为什么。当 Java 程序员写出下面的代码时，他们所定义的就对应于一个类扩展： What we have done is capture the essence of a class. Each function parameterized over a parent is...well, it’s a bit tricky, really. Let’s call it a class extension —we’ll soon see why. A class extension corresponds to what a Java programmer defines when they write:

class NodeSize extends Node { ... }

练习：那么，为什么我们要特意不把它叫作“类”呢？ Exercise:  So why are we going out of the way to not call it a “class”?

当开发者调用 Java 类的构造器时，实际上会沿着继承链一直向上构造对象（实际中，编译器可能将它优化为只需一次构造器调用和一次对象分配）。这些实际上是各个父类所对应对象的“私有”副本（也就是说，不考虑静态成员的存在时，是各自独有的）。不过，还有一个问题：这些对象中的多少内容是可见的。与我们上面的实现不同，Java 选择：无论继承链中曾经有多少个同名（且签名相同）的方法，最终只保留一个；而所有字段都保留在结果中，并可通过强制类型转换访问。后者有一定道理，因为每个字段大概都有约束它的不变量，所以将它们保持分离（从而全部保留）是明智的。相比之下，也很容易想象一种实现，让所有方法都可用，而不仅仅是继承层次中最底层（也就是最细化）的那些方法。许多脚本语言采用的就是后一种做法。 When a developer invokes a Java class’s constructor, it in effect constructs objects all the way up the inheritance chain (in practice, a compiler might optimize this to require only one constructor invocation and one object allocation). These are effectively “personal” copies of the objects corresponding to the parent classes (personal, that is, up to the presence of static members). There is, however, a question of how much of these objects is visible. Java chooses that—unlike in our implementation above—only one method of a given name (and signature) remains, no matter how many there might have been on the inheritance chain, whereas every field remains in the result, and can be accessed by casting. The latter makes some sense because each field presumably has invariants governing it, so keeping them separate (and hence all present) is wise. In contrast, it is easy to imagine an implementation that also makes all the methods available, not only the ones lowest (i.e., most refined) in the inheritance hierarchy. Many scripting languages take the latter approach.

练习：上面的代码并不是我们作为程序员真正想要的。自引用指向的是同一个语法对象，而它需要指向最细化的对象：这称为开放递归。修改对象表示，使 self 始终引用对象最细化的版本。提示：你会发现，用自应用实现递归的方法（不使用修改实现自引用）很有帮助。 Exercise:  The code above is not what we would really  want as programmers. The self-reference is to the same syntactic object, whereas it needs to refer to the most-refined object: this is known as open recursion. Modify the object representations so that self always refers to the most refined version of the object. Hint:  You will find the self-application method (Self-Reference Without Mutation) of recursion handy.

旁注：这展示了传统对象带来的另一种可扩展性：可扩展的递归。 Aside:  This demonstrates the other form of extensibility we get from traditional objects: extensible recursion .

扩展原型 Extending Prototypes

在上面的描述中，我们为每个类提供了它的父类的描述。随后，对象构造沿继承链向上推进，依次创建它们的实例。理解父级还有另一种方式：不把它看作一个待实例化的类，而是直接看作对象本身。这样，所有具有同一父级的子对象，观察到的都是完全相同的一个对象，这意味着一个子对象对它所做的修改，对另一个子对象也可见。这个共享的父对象称为原型。 In our description above, we’ve supplied each class with a description of its parent class . Object construction then makes instances of each as it goes up the inheritance chain. There is another way to think of the parent: not as a class to be instantiated but, instead, directly as an object itself. Then all children with the same parent would observe the very same object, which means changes to it from one child object would be visible to another child. The shared parent object is known as a prototype .

旁注：基于原型的语言的典范是 Self。虽然你可能读到过，JavaScript 等语言“基于”Self，但从源头学习这个思想仍然很有价值，尤其是因为 Self 以最纯粹的形式呈现了这些思想。 Aside:  The archetypal prototype-based language is Self . Though you may have read that languages like JavaScript are “based on” Self, there is value to studying the idea from its source, especially because Self presents these ideas in their purest form.

有些语言设计者认为，原型比类更为原始：借助函数等其他基本机制，可以从原型恢复出类，但反过来不行。这本质上就是我们上面做的事：每个“类”函数内部都包含一份对象描述，所以类就是一个返回对象的函数。如果将这两者暴露为不同的操作，并选择直接继承对象，我们就会得到一种类似原型的东西。 Some language designers have argued that prototypes are more primitive than classes in that, with other basic mechanisms such as functions, one can recover classes from prototypes—but not the other way around. That is essentially what we have done above: each “class” function contains inside it an object description, so a class is an object-returning-function. Had we exposed these as two different operations and chosen to inherit directly an object, we would have something akin to prototypes.

练习：修改上面的继承模式，实现一种类似 Self、基于原型而非基于类的语言。由于类会为每个对象提供各不相同的父对象副本，原型语言可以提供一个“克隆”操作，以简化用于在原型之上模拟类的操作的创建。 Exercise:  Modify the inheritance pattern above to implement a Self-like, prototype-based language, instead of a class-based language. Because classes provide each object with distinct copies of their parent objects, a prototype-language might provide a “clone” operation to simplify creation of the operation that simulates classes atop prototypes.

多重继承 Multiple Inheritance

现在你可能会问，为什么只有一个后备选项？很容易将它推广为多个选项，这自然就引出了多重继承。实际上，我们有多个对象可以继续链接查找；当然，这也引出了一个问题：应该按什么顺序查找呢？ Now you might ask, why is there only one fall-through option? It’s easy to generalize this to there being many, which leads naturally to multiple inheritance . In effect, we have multiple objects to which we can chain the lookup, which of course raises the question of what order in which we should do so.

即便祖先排列成一棵树，情况也已经够糟了，因为树也没有唯一标准的遍历顺序：比如仅仅广度优先和深度优先遍历就不同（而且两者都有很有说服力的用途）。更糟的是，假设某个东西 A 扩展了 B 和 C，而 B 和 C 又各自扩展了 D。现在，我们必须面对这个问题：A 的实例中会有一个还是两个 D 对象？只有一个可以节省空间，也可能更符合我们的预期，但这样，我们会访问这个对象一次还是两次？访问两次应该不会产生任何区别，所以似乎没有必要。但只访问一次，就意味着 B 或 C 中某一个的行为可能会改变。诸如此类。因此，几乎每一种支持多重继承的语言，都配有一种微妙的算法，仅仅为了定义查找顺序。 It would be bad enough if the ascendants were arranged in a tree, because even a tree does not have a canonical order of traversal: take just breadth-first and depth-first traversal, for instance (each of which has compelling uses). Worse, suppose a blob A extends B and C; but now suppose B and C each extend D. Now we have to confront this question: will there be one or two D objects in the instance of A? Having only one saves space and might interact better with our expectations, but then, will we visit this object once or twice? Visiting it twice should not make any difference, so it seems unnecessary. But visiting it once means the behavior of one of B or C might change. And so on. As a result, virtually every multiple-inheritance language is accompanied by a subtle algorithm merely to define the lookup order.

这种臭名昭著的情况叫作“菱形问题”（甚至叫作“致命的死亡菱形”！）。如果你决定让语言支持多重继承，可能会在这上面的设计决策中迷失好几天。由于你极不可能找到一个公认的标准答案，痛苦才刚刚开始。多重继承只在你尚未彻底想清楚它之前显得诱人。 This infamous situation is called the “diamond problem”  (or even, “the Deadly Diamond of Death”!). If you choose to include multiple inheritance in your language you can lose yourself for days in design decisions on this. Because it is highly unlikely you will find a canonical answer, your pain will have only begun. Multiple inheritance is only attractive until you’ve thought it through.

类扩展：混入与特质 Class Extensions: Mixins and Traits

当我们在 Java 中写 class 时，左右花括号之间到底定义了什么？不是整个类：整个类取决于它扩展的父类，依此类推，递归向上。实际上，我们在花括号内部定义的是一个类扩展。只因为我们在同一处还指定了父类，它才成为一个完整的类。 When we write class  in Java, what are we really defining between the opening and closing braces? It is not the entire class: that depends on the parent that it extends, and so on recursively. Rather, what we define inside the braces is a class extension . It only becomes a full-blown class because we also identify the parent class in the same place.

自然，我们应该问：为什么？为什么不将定义扩展与将扩展应用于基类这两件事分开？也就是说，假设我们不写 Naturally, we should ask: Why? Why not separate the act of defining  an extension from applying  the extension to a base class? That is, suppose instead of

class C extends B { ... }

而改写为： we instead write:

classext E { ... }

再单独写 and separately

class C = E(B)

其中 B 是一个已经定义的类？ where B  is some already-defined class?

到目前为止，看起来我们只是费了好大劲，才得到原来就有的东西。不过，这种类似函数应用的语法意在有所暗示：我们可以把这个扩展“应用”于几个不同的基类。因此： Thus far, it looks like we’ve just gone to great lengths to obtain what we had before. However, the function-application-like syntax is meant to be suggestive: we can “apply” this extension to several different base classes. Thus:

class C1 = E(B1);

class C2 = E(B2);

等等。通过把 E 的定义与它所扩展的类的定义分开，我们所做的，就是将类扩展从固定基类的暴政中解放出来。这样的扩展有一个名称：混入。 and so on. What we have done by separating the definition of E  from that of the class it extends is to liberate class extensions from the tyranny of the fixed base class. We have a name for these extensions: they’re called mixins .

混入让类定义更具有组合性。它在单继承语言的庇护之下（也就是说，没有关于查找顺序的复杂规则），提供了多重继承的许多好处（复用多个功能片段）。注意，使用脱糖时，给语言添加混入其实相当容易。混入不过是一个“以类为输入的函数”。由于我们已经确定了类如何脱糖，脱糖的目标语言又有函数，而且类会脱糖为可以嵌套在函数内部的表达式，因此实现一个简单的混入模型几乎是轻而易举的。 Mixins make class definition more compositional. They provide many of the benefits of multiple-inheritance (reusing multiple fragments of functionality) but within the aegis of a single-inheritance language (i.e., no complicated rules about lookup order). Observe that when desugaring, it’s actually quite easy to add mixins to the language. A mixin is just a “function over classes”. Because we have already determined how to desugar classes, and our target language for desugaring also has functions, and classes desugar to expressions that can be nested inside functions, it becomes almost trivial to implement a simple model of mixins.

旁注：这是一个例子，说明脱糖目标语言更强的通用性，如果被我们映射回源语言，可以引导我们得到更好的构造。 Aside:  This is a case where the greater generality of the target language of desugaring can lead us to a better  construct, if we reflect it back into the source language.

在有类型的语言中，好的混入设计确实可以改进面向对象编程实践。假设我们正在定义一种基于混入的 Java。如果混入实际上是一个从类到类的函数，那么这个“函数”的“类型”是什么？显然，混入应该用接口描述它所要求的内容以及它所提供的内容。Java 已经允许（但不要求）后者，即类可以声明自己提供哪些接口。然而，它不允许前者，即把父级指定为一个接口：Java 中的类（扩展）扩展的是它的父类——父类的所有成员对扩展都可见——而不是代表父类（或任何其他匹配同一接口的类）的接口。这意味着，它获得的是父级的全部行为，而不是对这些行为的规约。因此，如果父级改变，这个类可能就会出问题。混入有助于打破扩展与提供之间的这种不对称。 In a typed language, a good design for mixins can actually improve object-oriented programming practice. Suppose we’re defining a mixin-based version of Java. If a mixin is effectively a class-to-class function, what is the “type” of this “function”? Clearly, mixins ought to use interfaces  to describe what they expect and what they provide. Java already enables (but does not require) the latter, namely classes can say what interfaces they provide. However, it does not enable the former, namely specifying its parent as an interface : a class (extension) in Java extends its parent class—with all the parent’s members visible to the extension—rather than an interface that stands for  the parent (or any other  class that matches that same interface). That means it obtains all of the parent’s behavior, not a specification thereof. In turn, if the parent changes, the class might break. Mixins help break this asymmetry between extension and provision.

在混入语言中，我们可以改写为 In a mixin language, we can instead write

mixin M extends I1 implements I2 { ... }

其中 I1 和 I2 是接口。那么，M 只能应用于满足接口 I1 的类，而语言又能确保，在 M 内只有 I1 中指定的成员可见。这就直接对应于：M 的客户只能看到 I2 所提供的内容，也遵循了良好软件设计的一项重要原则： where I1  and I2 are interfaces. Then M  can only be applied to a class that satisfies the interface I1 , and in turn the language can ensure that only members specified in  I1  are visible in M . This becomes directly analogous to how a client of M  can only see what is provided by I2 , and follows one of the important principles of good software design:

引文：“面向接口编程，而不是面向实现编程。”——《设计模式》 Quote:  “Program to an interface, not an implementation.” — Design Patterns

简而言之，混入就是一个被转化为以父类为输入的函数的类： In short, a mixin is a class that has been turned into a function over parent classes:

M :: I1 -> I2

好的混入设计还可以走得更远。按照定义，一个类在继承链中只能使用一次（如果某个类最终又引用回自己，继承链就会出现环，可能导致无限循环）。相比之下，组合函数时，我们对使用同一个函数两次毫无顾虑（例如：(map ... (filter ... (map ...))))。那么，使用同一个混入两次有价值吗？ A good design for mixins can go even further. A class can only be used once in an inheritance chain, by definition (if a class eventually referred back to itself, there would be a cycle in the inheritance chain, causing potential infinite loops). In contrast, when we compose functions, we have no qualms about using the same function twice (e.g.: (map ... (filter ... (map ...)))) . Is there value to using a mixin twice?

旁注：当然有！参见《类与混入》（Classes and Mixins）的第 3、4 节。 Aside:  There certainly is! See sections 3 and 4 of Classes and Mixins .

混入解决了库设计中的一个重要问题。假设有十几个不同的功能，可以用不同方式组合。我们应该提供多少个类？而且，并不是所有功能都能相互组合。生成所有类、承受整个组合爆炸，显然是不切实际的。更好的办法是，让开发者挑选自己关心的功能，同时有某种机制防止不合理的组合。这恰恰就是混入解决的问题：它们提供类扩展，开发者可以在保持接口的前提下，将它们组合成自己恰好需要的类。 Mixins solve an important problem that arises in the design of libraries. Suppose we have a dozen different features which can be combined in different ways. How many classes should we provide? Furthermore, not all of these can be combined with each other. It is obviously impractical to generate the entire combinatorial explosion of classes. It would be better if the developer could pick and choose the features they care about, with some mechanism to prevent unreasonable combinations. This is precisely the problem that mixins solve: they provide the class extensions, which the developers can combine, in an interface-preserving way, to create just the classes they need.

旁注：Racket 的 GUI 库广泛使用了混入。例如，color:text-mixin 接收基本文本编辑器接口，并实现彩色文本编辑器接口。后者本身也是一种基本文本编辑器接口，因此可以对其结果继续应用其他基本文本混入。 Aside:  Mixins are used extensively in the Racket GUI library. For instance, color:text-mixin  consumes basic text editor interfaces and implements the colored text editor interface. The latter is itself a basic text editor interface, so additional basic text mixins can be applied to the result.

练习：在你最喜欢的面向对象语言中，类似的库是如何解决同一个问题的？ Exercise:  How does the analogous library in your favorite object-oriented language solve this same problem?

混入确实有一个限制：它们强制组合呈线性。这种严格性有时并不合适，因为它给程序员施加了可能并无必要的负担。一种名为特质的混入泛化提出，我们可以扩展一组混入，而不是只扩展一个。当然，一旦扩展不止一个，就必须再次面对潜在的名称冲突。因此，特质必须配备解决名称冲突的机制，通常采用某种名称组合代数的形式。这样，特质就成了混入的良好补充，让程序员能够选择最适合自身需求的机制。因此，Racket 同时提供了混入和特质。 Mixins do have one limitation: they enforce a linearity of composition. This strictness is sometimes misplaced, because it puts a burden on programmers that may not be necessary. A generalization of mixins called traits  says that instead of extending a single mixin, we can extend a set of them. Of course, the moment we extend more than one, we must again contend with potential name-clashes. Thus traits must be equipped with mechanisms for resolving name clashes, often in the form of some name-combination algebra. Traits thus offer a nice complement to mixins, enabling programmers to choose the mechanism that best fits their needs. As a result, Racket provides both mixins and traits.

••••• 类型 ••••• ••••• Types •••••

在程序执行之前检查的类型——也就是所谓的静态类型——是编程中至关重要的一部分。越来越多的语言要么从一开始就拥有它们，要么在意识到其重要性之后，以各种形式添加它们。类型是证明程序性质时常见的第一步。如果你使用有类型的语言，那么无论是否意识到，你每天都在为自己的程序编写小小的证明。 Types that are checked before program execution—what are known as static types—are a vital part of programming, and a growing number of languages either have them from the start or, realizing their importance, are adding them in various forms. Types are a common first step towards proving properties about programs. If you use a typed language, you write small proofs about your programs every day, whether you realize it or not.

类型简介 Introduction to Types

关于对象的内容已经讲完了。为什么对象不在 SMoL 中呢？ We’re done with objects. Why weren’t objects in SMoL?

  1. 并非所有语言都有对象。 Not all languages have them.
  2. 有对象的语言似乎也无法就细节达成一致（类还是原型、单继承还是多重继承、类还是特质与混入，等等）。这里没多少“标准”可言。 The ones that do have them can’t seem to agree on the details (classes versus prototypes, single- versus multiple-inheritance, classes versus traits and mixins, etc.). There’s very little “standard” there.
  3. 我们可以通过脱糖加入其中的大多数概念！ We can add most notions through desugaring!

现在转向类型。我们将始终用“类型”一词指静态检查，也就是完全根据程序源代码就能进行的检查。这意味着，类型不能涉及动态条件，而且可能出现误报或漏报（例如，代码中虽然存在、但实践中永远不会运行的东西，仍然可能导致类型错误）；作为回报，它们让我们不必运行程序就能获得保证。当程序运行成本高昂、无法运行（例如依赖开发者无法重现的条件），或者运行起来有危险时，这一点很重要。 Now we move on to types. We will always use the term type  to refer to a static  check, i.e., one that can be done purely with the program source. This means types cannot refer to dynamic conditions, and may suffer from either false-positive or false-negative errors (e.g., something that is in the code but can never run in practice may still cause a type error); in return, they give us guarantees without ever having to run the program. This is important when the program is expensive to run, impossible (e.g., it depends on conditions that can’t be reproduced by the developer), or dangerous.

类型其实也不属于 SMoL，但不是因为我们能通过脱糖加入它们（我们做不到）；而是因为前两个原因：许多语言没有类型，而有类型的语言往往也不认同彼此的类型形式（这在很大程度上源于它们对对象本质的分歧）。不过，它们确实有一些（大体上）一致的部分，我们将从这些部分开始。 Types aren’t really a part of SMoL either, but not because we can add them through desugaring (which we can’t); rather, it’s for the first two reasons: many languages don’t have them, and those that do don’t often agree on their form (in large part because of their disagreement over the nature of objects). However, there are parts they do  (largely) agree on, which we will begin with.

类型的一种标准模型 A Standard Model of Types

可以将类型看作运行时值的抽象。也就是说，在运行时，我们可能有数量极大的数字、字符串和图像（以及两个布尔值），而我们会抹平各类内部的区别，只保留各类之间的区别。因此，从一个基本解释器出发，尝试在此基础上构建类型检查器，会很有启发： Types can be thought of as abstractions of run-time values. That is, whereas at run-time we can have a very large number of numbers and strings and images (and two Booleans), we will collapse the distinctions within  these and preserve only the distinctions between  them. Therefore, it is instructive to start with a basic interpreter and try to build a type checker from there:

(define-type BinOp

  [plus])

(define-type Exp

  [binE (operator : BinOp)

        (left  : Exp)

        (right : Exp)]

  [numE (value : Number)])

(calc : (Exp -> Number))

(define (calc e)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(binE o l r)

     (type-case BinOp o

       [(plus) (+ (calc l) (calc r))])]

    [(numE v) v]))

(test (calc (binE (plus) (numE 5) (numE 6))) 11)

现在，看看类型检查器需要做什么。包装上写着“检查器”：也就是说，类型检查器的职责是判断程序，确定它是否类型正确。因此，（类型检查器的）一个自然的类型是 Now let’s see what needs to happen with a type-checker. The label on the tin says “checker”: that is, the job of a type-checker is to pass judgment  on programs, i.e., to determine whether or not they are type-correct. Thus, a natural type (for the type checker) would be

(tc : (Exp -> Boolean ))

（当然，在实践中，如果程序类型不正确，我们会希望得到更多信息，也就是错误诊断。不过，这里先不考虑人的因素。）有了这个类型，现在就可以重写上面解释器的相关部分： (In practice, of course, we would want more information in case the program is not type-correct, i.e., we’d like an error diagnostic. But we’re ignoring human factors considerations here.) With this type, we can now rewrite the relevant parts of the interpreter above:

(define ( tc  e)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(binE o l r)

     (type-case BinOp o

       [(plus) ( and  ( tc  l) ( tc  r))])]

    [(numE v) #true ]))

(test ( tc  (binE (plus) (numE 5) (numE 6))) #true )

实际上，先仔细看一会儿。给定一个数字，类型检查器返回 #true。在递归情况下，它对各部分的类型检查结果计算 and。就这样。由于没有任何地方能返回 #false，整个类型检查器就必定总是只返回 #true。也就是说，每个程序都是类型正确的。 Actually, let’s peer at this for a moment. Given a number, the type-checker returns #true . In the recursive cases, it computes the and  of type-checking the pieces. And that’s it. Since there is no way to return #false , the entire type-checker must always only return #true . That is, every program is type-correct.

问题在于，我们只有一种类型，即数字，也只有一种操作，而且同样作用于数字，所以能出什么问题呢？我们需要扩展类型和操作，让错误真正有机会出现。因此，假设添加一个拼接字符串的 ++ 操作。 The problem is because we have only one type, numbers, and only one operation, also on numbers, so what could possibly go wrong? We need to extend the types and operations so that there are meaningful possibilities for errors. Therefore, suppose we add a ++  operation that concatenates strings.

(define-type BinOp

  [plus] [++] )

(define-type Exp

  [binE (operator : BinOp)

        (left  : Exp)

        (right : Exp)]

  [numE (value : Number)]

  [strE (value : String)] )

各种地方都坏了，需要修复。这样如何？ Various things break, and need to be fixed. How about this?

(define (tc e)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(binE o l r)

     (type-case BinOp o

       [(plus) (and (tc l) (tc r))]

        [(++)   (and (tc l) (tc r))] )]

    [(numE v) #true]

    [(strE v) #true] ))

(test (tc (binE (++) (strE "hello") (strE "world"))) #true)

这看起来相当不错，对吧？ So this looks pretty good, right?

现在动手！这完全不是我们想要的！写一个测试用例来说明这一点。 Do Now:  This is not at all what we want! Write a test case that demonstrates that.

下面两个测试展示了我们希望得到的行为： Here are two tests that demonstrate desirable  behavior:

(test (tc (binE (++) (numE 5) (numE 6))) #false)

(test (tc (binE (plus) (strE "hello") (strE "world"))) #false)

第一个对两个数字进行字符串拼接，第二个对两个字符串做加法。因此，类型检查器应该拒绝两者。然而，两者都通过了检查（也就是说，上面的测试失败了）。 The first string-concatenates two numbers, the second adds two strings. Therefore, both should be rejected by the type-checker. Yet both of them pass (i.e., the tests above fail).

这里的核心问题是什么？对于一个表达式，我们只知道它的子表达式是否通过了类型检查，却不知道它们的类型是什么。这不足以判断当前表达式是否类型正确。例如，++ 运算符不仅需要检查两个子表达式是否类型良好，还需要检查它们是否产生字符串；如果不是，这个拼接就是错误的。 What is the core problem here? It’s that, given an expression, we only know whether  its sub-expressions typed correctly, but not what  their types are.  That is insufficient to determine whether the current expression is type-correct. For instance, the ++  operator needs to check not only whether its two sub-expressions are well-typed, but also whether they produced strings; if they did not, then the concatenation is erroneous.

这说明，我们需要让类型检查器具有更丰富的类型：它必须改为 What this shows is that we need the type-checker to have a richer type: it must instead be

(tc : (Exp -> Type ))

也就是说，类型“检查器”实际上必须是一个类型计算器，即它与求值器更加相似，只不过运作于抽象值（类型）的世界，而不是具体值的世界。不过，按照惯例，我们仍然叫它检查器，因为它在计算类型的过程中也进行检查。 That is, the type “checker” must actually be a type calculator , i.e., it even more closely parallels the evaluator, just over the universe of abstracted values (types) rather than concrete ones. Following convention, however, we’ll continue to call it a checker, because it also  checks in the process of calculating types.

在上面的类型声明中，Type 是一个新的（plait 类型）定义，记录了可能的类型： In the type declaration above, Type  is a new ( plait  type) definition that records the possible types:

(define-type Type [numT] [strT])

有了它，就能重写我们的类型“检查器”： With this, we can rewrite our type-“checker”:

(define (tc e)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(binE o l r)

     (type-case BinOp o

       [(plus) (if (and (numT? (tc l)) (numT? (tc r)))

                   (numT)

                   (error 'tc "not both numbers"))]

       [(++)   (if (and (strT? (tc l)) (strT? (tc r)))

                   (strT)

                   (error 'tc "not both strings"))])]

    [(numE v) (numT)]

    [(strE v) (strT)]))

(test (tc (binE (plus) (numE 5) (numE 6))) (numT))

(test (tc (binE (++) (strE "hello") (strE "world"))) (strT))

(test/exn (tc (binE (++) (numE 5) (numE 6))) "strings")

(test/exn (tc (binE (plus) (strE "hello") (strE "world"))) "numbers")

这里有三个要点： There are three take-aways from this:

  1. 类型检查器遵循与解释器相同的实现模式：用代数数据类型表示 AST，用结构递归处理它。这就是我们称为 SImPl 的模式。 The type-checker follows the same implementation schema as the interpreter: an algebraic datatype to represent the AST, and structural recursion to process it. This is the schema we’re calling SImPl.
  2. 与解释器不同，类型检查器操作的是“弱化”的值：例如，注意 numE 分支如何忽略实际的数字值。传统类型检查的优点和缺点，都源自这种忽略。 A type-checker, unlike an interpreter, operates with “weak” values: note, for instance, how the numE  case ignores the actual numeric values. Both the strengths and weaknesses of traditional type-checking arise from this ignorance.
  3. 用数学术语说，从类型检查器到类型计算器的升级，是一个加强归纳假设的过程：我们不能只返回 Boolean，而必须返回每个表达式的实际类型。这看起来未必是字面意义上的加强；但从原来的 #true 被替换为 Type、#false 被替换为错误这个意义上来说，确实如此。 In mathematical terms, the upgrade we performed in going from a type-checker to a type-calculator was a process of strengthening the inductive hypothesis: instead of returning only a Boolean , we had to return the actual type of each expression. This may not seem like a literal strengthening; but it is inasmuch as the former #true  has been replaced by a Type  and the #false  by an error.

练习：为语言添加除法，并对其进行类型检查。 Exercise:  Add division to the language and type-check it.

一种简洁的记法 A Concise Notation

随着类型系统的扩展，把一切都写成代码会越来越笨重。我们将改用类型领域中常用的一种记法（不过它也可以用于解释器和其他 SImPl 程序）。我们会写出如下形式的项 As we extend our type system, it is increasingly unwieldy to write everything out as code. Instead, we will adopt a notation commonly used in the world of types (though it can also be used for interpreters and other SImPl programs). We will write terms of the form

|- e : T

其中，e 是表达式，T 是类型，: 读作“具有类型”：即上面的记法表示“e 具有类型 T”。暂时我们不读出 |-；之后会看到，它应该读作“证明”。 where the e  are expressions, T  are types, and :  is pronounced as “has type”: i.e., the notation above says “ e  has type T ”. For now we won’t pronounce |-  as anything at all; later, we will see that it should be read as “proves”.

首先，我们可以非常简洁地说明：所有数字表达式都具有数字类型，所有字符串表达式都具有字符串类型： First, we can very concisely say that all numeric expressions have numeric type and all string expressions have string type:

|- n : Num

|- s : Str

其中，n 代表所有具有数字语法的语法项，s 同样代表字符串。（可以将它看作无穷多条规则，每个数字和每个字符串各有一条。我们身处数学的世界，朋友之间，多出无穷多条规则又算什么呢？）前者完全等价于写出 where n  stands for all the syntactic terms with the syntax of numbers, and s  likewise for strings. (We can think of this as an infinite number of rules, one for each number and each string. We’re in the realm of mathematics, so what’s an infinite number of rules between friends?) The former is exactly equivalent to writing

    [(numC n) (numT)]

但简洁得多。 but much more concisely.

到了布尔值这里，我们有一个选择：可以写 When we get to Booleans, we have a choice: we can either write

|- b : Bool

其中 b 代表所有具有布尔值语法的语法项；或者，因为它们只有两个，也可以直接逐一列出来： where b  stands for all the syntactic terms with the syntax of Booleans, or—because there are only two of them—just enumerate them explicitly:

|- true : Bool

|- false : Bool

好，这些对应类型检查器的基本情况，称为公理。现在来看有条件的情况，它们称为（定型）规则。还记得用于确定加法类型的代码： Okay, so these correspond to the base cases of the type-checker. These are called axioms . Now let’s get to the conditional  cases, which are called (typing) rules . Remember our code for typing addition:

       [(plus) (if (and (numT? (tc l)) (numT? (tc r)))

                   (numT)

                   (error 'tc "not both numbers"))]

用这种记法，我们可以将它非常简洁地写成： We can write it in this notation very concisely as follows:

|- e1 : Num    |- e2 : Num

--------------------------

|- (+ e1 e2) : Num

横线读作“如果（上面的内容），那么（下面的内容）”，空白读作“并且”。因此，这条规则说：“如果 e1 具有类型 Num，并且 e2 具有类型 Num，那么 (+ e1 e2) 具有类型 Num。”当然，这与代码说的完全一样，但杂音少得多。 We read the line as “if (what’s above) then (what’s below)”, and the space as “and”. So this says: “if e1  has type Num  and e2  has type Num , then (+ e1 e2)  has type Num ”. This is of course the exact same thing the code says, but with rather less noise.

术语：上面的部分叫作前提（先出现的内容），下面的部分叫作结论（后出现的内容）。不要把它们叫作分子和分母！ Terminology:  The part above is called the antecedent  (that which goes before) and the part below is called the consequent  (that which comes after). Don’t call these the numerator and denominator!

扩展类型：除法与条件构造 Growing Types: Division, Conditionals

处理除法 Handling Division

加法、乘法和减法都是数字上的全函数：接收两个数字，产生一个数字。相比之下，除法是偏函数：当分母为零时，它没有定义。因此，我们需要一种处理它的策略。有几种可用的策略： Addition, multiplication, and subtraction are total  functions over numbers: they consume two numbers and produce one. In contrast, division is a partial  function: it isn’t defined when the denominator is zero. Therefore, we need a strategy for handling it. There are several available strategies:

  1. 我们可以规定，除法不返回数字，而是返回某种能够体现其偏函数性质的东西，例如 (Optionof Number)。这样完全可行。不过，这意味着每一次使用除法，都得检查是否得到了一个真正的数字。这可能变得相当繁琐。 We can declare that division doesn’t return  a number but instead something else that captures its partiality, such as (Optionof Number) . This can work just fine. However, it means every single use of division will need to check whether it obtained a proper number or not. This can get quite onerous.
  2. 我们可以规定，除法的第二个实参只接受非零数字。这会大幅改变类型系统，因为到目前为止，我们一直将所有数字归在同一个数字类型中。现在，这就会影响所有除法调用者：它们必须证明自己调用除法时没有把零作为第二个实参。这是另一种形式的繁琐。注意，类型检查器无法自动而无误地证明某个值非零，因为这不可判定（参见莱斯定理）。 We can declare that division only consumes  non-zero numbers in its second argument. This is a major change to our type system, because until now we had lumped all numbers together into a single numeric type. This now affects all callers of division, who must now prove that they are not calling it on zero as the second argument. This is onerous in a different way. Observe that the type checker cannot automatically prove that a value is non-zero without error, because this is not decidable (see Rice’s Theorem ).
  3. 我们给它与其他二元数字操作相同的类型，并规定异常情况由异常或错误处理。这就隐式地将负担放在程序的其他部分上，它们必须意识到这种可能性并加以处理。 We give it the same type as other binary numeric operations, and declare that the exceptional case will be handled by an exception or error. This implicitly puts the burden on the rest of the program, which must be aware of this possibility and handle it.

关于处理偏函数的一般策略，更多内容见 For more about general strategies for handling partial functions, see

https://dcic-world.org/2025-02-09/partial-domains.html

大多数编程语言采用了上面的第三种方案，它看起来最为务实。不过，越来越多的语言正在探索前两种方案。对于第二种情况，它们绕过莱斯定理的方法是：尝试证明值非零，而在无法证明时，将负担交给程序员。这虽然增加了程序员的工作，却也提高了程序的健壮性。 Most programming languages have taken the third option above, which seems the most pragmatic. However, a growing number of languages are exploring the first two options. They get around Rice’s Theorem in the second case by trying to prove non-zero-ness and, when they cannot, putting the burden on the programmer. While this creates more effort for the programmer, it increases the program’s robustness.

看待类型的另一种角度 Another Perspective on Types

我们已经看到，可以将类型看作值的抽象，将类型检查看作在这些抽象值上运行程序。我们很快就会看到，这种类比会在一定程度上失效。 We have already seen how we can think of types as abstractions of values, and type-checking as running a program over these abstract values. As we’ll soon see, the analogy will break down a bit.

另一种角度是将类型视为一种静态约束机制：静态判断程序的一种方式。从某种意义上说，我们已经在做这件事了：它叫作解析。解析器会静态地（也就是在程序运行之前）作出判断（即判定某些程序合格，另一些不合格）。可以将类型看作这一思想的扩展。 Another perspective is to think of types as a static discipline : a way of statically making judgments about programs. In a way, we have already been doing just this: it’s called parsing . A parser statically (i.e., before the program runs) passes judgment (i.e., decides that some programs are good and others are bad). Types can be viewed as an extension of this idea.

旁注：用可计算性理论的术语说，解析器通常是上下文无关的，而类型通常反映的是上下文相关约束。可计算性理论由此帮助我们理解，为什么可以把这些检查分成两个阶段，尤其是为什么可以先做其中一种，再做另一种。本质上，类型检查器只需要处理已经通过解析、也就是上下文无关检查的程序，所以比起包办一切，它的复杂度低得多。我们已经见过这一点：先前的检查器只接收 Expr，而 Expr 是解析器产生的。 Aside:  In computability theory terms, parsers are usually context-free , whereas types usually reflect context-sensitive  constraints. Computability theory then helps us understand why we might separate these checks into two separate phases, and in particular why we might do one before the other. Essentially, the type-checker only needs to deal with programs that have already passed the parsing, i.e., context-free check, so it has much less complexity than if it had to do everything. We already saw this: our previous checker only consumed Expr s, which are produced by the parser.

从公理和规则到判断 From Axioms and Rules to Judgments

需要将类型规则应用于某个程序时，我们会递归地组合它们，就像类型检查器运行时那样。考虑这个程序： When we need to apply type rules to a program, we compose them recursively, just as the type-checker runs. Consider this program:

(+ 5 (+ 6 7))

为了确定它的类型，我们将使用当前已有的规则［👉］。注意，它不符合任何公理，因为这个程序不匹配单个数字或字符串的语法。因此，必须使用一条有条件的规则。目前我们只见过一条，幸运的是，这个项确实匹配其结论：它要求两个项，而我们有两个项，因此 e1 是 5，e2 是 (+ 6 7)。所以，应用这条有条件的规则后，得到： To decide its type, we will use our current rules [ 👉 ]. Observe that it does not fit any axiom, because the program does not match the syntax of a single number or string. Therefore, we have to use a conditional rule. We have seen only one so far, and fortunately this term does match the consequent: it requires two terms, and we have two terms, so e1  is 5  and e2  is (+ 6 7) . Therefore, applying this conditional rule, we get:

|- 5 : Num    |- (+ 6 7) : Num

----------------------

|- (+ 5 (+ 6 7)) : Num

到目前为止，一切顺利。现在来看前提中的两个项。第一个现在确实匹配某条公理；因此，我们将它标为绿色，到这里就可以停了： So far, so good. Now let’s look at the two terms in the antecedent. The first one now actually matches to an axiom; therefore, we’ll mark that in green and can stop with that:

|- 5 : Num     |- (+ 6 7) : Num

----------------------

|- (+ 5 (+ 6 7)) : Num

对于另一个，我们必须再次应用同一条有条件的规则：  For the other, we have to apply the same conditional rule again:

              |- 6 : Num    |- 7 : Num

              ------------------------

|- 5 : Num     |- (+ 6 7) : Num

----------------------

|- (+ 5 (+ 6 7)) : Num

这些新项也匹配数字公理，所以也可以将它们标为绿色： These new terms also match the axiom for numbers, so we can mark them also in green:

              |- 6 : Num     |- 7 : Num

              ------------------------

|- 5 : Num     |- (+ 6 7) : Num

----------------------

|- (+ 5 (+ 6 7)) : Num

现在，树的每一部分都以公理结束。因此，我们认为这个程序已成功通过类型检查。这棵树称为一个判断，因为它对最初的项作出了判断：在这里，判断它通过了类型检查，并且会产生一个类型为 Num 的值。 Every part of the tree now terminates in an axiom. We therefore consider this program to have successfully type-checked. This tree is called a judgment , because it passes judgment on the initial term: in this case, judging it to have type-checked and to produce a value of type Num .

仔细观察，这与类型检查器的执行模式完全相同！不同的是，我们可以略过传入和返回各种东西的繁琐细节，直接使用模式匹配。这会在接下来的内容中为我们省下不少工作。 Observe closely that this is the same pattern of execution we had with the type-checker! The difference is that we were able to skip the tedious details of passing and returning things, and instead simply used pattern-matching. This will save us a fair bit of work as we go forward.

判断与错误 Judgments and Errors

再看一个例子，它会说明一条重要原则： Let’s see another example, which will illustrate an important principle:

(+ 5 (+ 6 "hi"))

过程与上一个例子类似。我们得到下面这个尚在尝试构造的判断： This proceeds analogously to the previous example. This leaves us with the following attempted judgment:

              |- 6 : Num     |- "hi" : Num

              ---------------------------

|- 5 : Num     |- (+ 6 "hi") : Num

-------------------------

|- (+ 5 (+ 6 "hi")) : Num

但现在有一个问题：我们需要对下面的表达式进行类型检查 But now we have a problem: we need to type-check

|- "hi" : Num

却没有匹配的规则。因此，我们无法构造一棵成功的树： but we don’t have a rule that matches . Therefore, we cannot  construct a successful tree:

              |- 6 : Num     |- "hi" : Num

              ---------------------------

|- 5 : Num     |- (+ 6 "hi") :

-------------------------

|- (+ 5 (+ 6 "hi")) :

还记得“如果……并且……那么……”这种解读吗？由于无法满足全部前提，我们就无法证明任何关于结论的内容，因此这棵树不完整。 Remember the “if … and … then” interpretation. Because we cannot satisfy all the antecedents, we cannot prove anything about the consequents, leaving the tree incomplete.

类型错误不过是无法构造出判断。作为用户反馈，这未必最令人满意，但我们在这里关心的是一种简洁表达思想的方式；从这里走向实现并不太难，用户界面的细节可以在实现中补上。 A type error is simply a failure to construct a judgment.  It may not be the most satisfying user feedback, but our concern here is with a concise way of expressing ideas; going from this to an implementation is not too hard, and the user interface details can be added to the latter.

这里需要澄清一下。只有当整棵树都完全“核对通过”时，我们才称它为判断：也就是说，每个前提都使用给定规则生成，所有叶节点都是真正的公理。在这个例子中，我们无法将整棵树核对通过：没有任何可用的规则或公理，能让我们得出 "hi" 是 Num 的结论。因此，我们无法“判断”最初的表达式。这是“判断”一词的技术含义，不要将它与这个词可能具有的日常含义混淆。 This requires some clarification. We only call it a judgment if the tree is “checked off” completely: i.e., every antecedent is generated using given rules, and all the leaves are actual axioms. In this example, we are unable to check off the tree: there is no available rule or  axiom that lets us conclude that "hi"  is a Num . Therefore, we cannot “judge” the initial expression. This is a technical meaning of the word judgment , not to be confused with potentially colloquial interpretations of the term.

同样，设想我们从这个程序开始： Similarly, imagine that we started with this program:

(+ 5 (- 6 7))

我们会进行到这里： We would get this far:

|- 5 : Num     |- (- 6 7) : Num

----------------------

|- (+ 5 (- 6 7)) : Num

然后又会失败，这一次是因为我们还没有为 (- e1 e2) 提供一条（有条件的）规则。显然，定义一条并不难；只是我们还没做，所以模式匹配器会失败。 Again we would fail, this time because we haven’t provided a (conditional) rule for (- e1 e2) . Obviously it’s not difficult to define one; we just haven’t done so yet, so our pattern-matcher would fail.

练习：构造 ++（字符串拼接）的有条件规则。将它与类型检查器中的代码进行比较。 Exercise:  Construct the conditional rule for ++  (string concatenation). Compare it to the code in the type-checker.

为条件构造确定类型 Typing Conditionals

现在，我们已经准备好为 if 添加规则。正如前面看到的，对于条件子句中允许出现什么，不同语言有不同规则。由于类型检查器的目标是捕捉类型错误，有类型检查器的语言通常会要求条件是 Boolean（而不是使用一套真性值／假性值作为布尔值）。我们这里的目标不是作价值判断，而是展示如何为它添加类型规则。 Now we’re ready to add a rule for if . As we have seen, different languages have different rules for what can go in the conditional clause. Since the goal of a type-checker is to catch type errors, it is common for languages with type-checkers to demand that the conditional be a Boolean (without a truthy/falsy set of Boolean values). Our goal here is not to make a value judgment but rather to illustrate how we would add a type rule for it.

到现在，我们可以看出，需要一条有条件的规则（因为我们要检查的不只是常量的类型）；按照 SImPl，我们还需要在前提中说明子表达式的情况。显然，我们至少需要： By now, we can see that we will need a conditional rule (because we want to type-check more than just constants); following SImPl, and we will need the antecedent to say something about the sub-expressions. Clearly, we need at least:

|- C : Bool    …

------------------

|- (if C T E) : …

好，接下来呢？整个条件表达式的类型是什么？严格来说，它应该是实际执行的那个分支返回的类型。不过，类型检查器无法知道哪个分支会被执行；随着时间推移，两个分支都可能执行。所以，必须以某种方式刻画这种情形中的不确定性。有两种常见解决方案： Okay, what now? What is the type of the entire conditional expression? Technically, it should be whatever type is returned by the branch that was executed. However, a type-checker can’t know which branch will be executed; over time, both might. So we have to somehow capture the uncertainty  in this situation. There are two common solutions:

  1. 引入一种新的类型，代表“这个类型或者那个类型”（联合类型）。引入它很容易，但会给每一段接收这种值的代码都带来负担。 Introduce a new kind of type that stands for “this type or  that type” (a union ). This is easy to introduce but creates a burden for every piece of code that will consume such a value.
  2. 直接规定两个分支应具有相同类型。 Just rule that both branches should have the same type.

后一种解决方案非常优雅，因为它彻底消除了不确定性。 The latter is a very elegant solution, because it eliminates the uncertainty entirely.

好，那么我们需要做以下几件事： Okay, so we need to do the following things:

  • 计算 T 的类型。 Compute the type of T.
  • 计算 E 的类型。 Compute the type of E.
  • 确保 T 和 E 具有相同类型。 Make sure T and E have the same type.
  • 让这个（相同的）类型成为条件表达式的结果类型。 Make this (same) type the result of the conditional.

这似乎有很多事要做：该如何表达这一切？实际上，非常简单： That seems like a lot: how will we express all that? Very easily, actually:

|- C : Bool    |- T : U    |- E : U

-----------------------------------

|- (if C T E) : U

这里，U 是一个占位符：它不是某个具体类型，而是代表任何可能出现在该位置的类型。重复使用 U，就达成了上面的所有目标。可以这样读：“如果 C 具有类型 Bool，并且 T 具有类型 U，并且 E 具有［同一个］类型 U，那么 (if C T E) 具有［同一个］类型 U。” Here, U  is a placeholder: it isn’t a concrete type but rather stands for  whatever type might go in that place. The repeated use of U  accomplishes all of our goals above. Read this as: “if C has type Bool  and T  has type U  and E  has [ the same ] type U , then (if C T E)  has [the same] type U ”.

来看看它如何应用于下面的程序： Let’s see this in action on the following program:

(if true 1 2)

我们得到： We get:

|- true : Bool     |- 1 : U    |- 2 : U

--------------------------------------

|- (if true 1 2) : U

另外两个前提中，任意一个所对应的公理都能告诉我们 U 必须是什么，从而让我们在所有位置填入 U 的结果： Either of the axioms for the other two antecedents tells us what U must be, which lets us fill in the result of U everywhere:

|- true : Bool     |- 1 : Num    |- 2 : Num

------------------------------------------

|- (if true 1 2) : Num

幸运的是，另外两个前提也都是公理： Fortunately, the other two antecedents are also axioms:

|- true : Bool     |- 1 : Num      |- 2 : Num

------------------------------------------

|- (if true 1 2) : Num

由此可以得出结论：整个项类型良好，而且具有类型 Num。 This lets us conclude that the overall term is well-typed, and that it has type Num .

现在来看： Now let’s look at:

(if 4 1 2)

应用这条有条件的规则，得到： Applying the conditional rule gives us:

|- 4 : Bool    |- 1 : U    |- 2 : U

-----------------------------------

|- (if 4 1 2) : U

不过，我们没有任何公理或有条件的规则，能让我们得出 4 具有类型 Bool 的结论（因为实际上它并不具有）。因此，无法完成这个判断： However, we do not have any axiom or conditional rule that lets us conclude that 4  has type Bool  (because, in fact, it does not). Therefore, we cannot complete the judgment:

|- 4 : Bool    |- 1 : U    |- 2 : U

-----------------------------------

|- (if 4 1 2) : U

这个程序因而被（正确地）判定为有类型错误。 and the program is (rightly) judged to have a type error.

最后一个例子： One last example:

(if true 1 "hi")

同样，应用这条有条件的规则，并核对通过第一个前提： Again, applying the conditional rule and checking off the first antecedent:

|- true : Bool     |- 1 : U    |- "hi" : U

-----------------------------------------

|- (if true 1 "hi") : U

但现在有一个问题。如果应用数字公理，就会把所有 U 都替换为 Num，得到： But now we have a problem. If we apply the axiom for numbers, we replace all instances of U  with Num  to get:

|- true : Bool     |- 1 : Num     |- "hi" : Num

---------------------------------------------

|- (if true 1 "hi") : Num

也许只是我们试错了公理？确实还有另一种选择！不过，它最终带来的整体效果相同： Maybe we just tried the wrong axiom? We do have one more option! However, it ends up with the same net effect:

|- true : Bool     |- 1 : Str     |- "hi" : Str

---------------------------------------------

|- (if true 1 "hi") : Str

由于无法为这个程序构造判断，它也有类型错误。 Because there is no  way to construct a judgment for this program, it too has a type error.

练习：现在加入函数。我们需要两种新构造：一种用于引入函数（lambda），另一种用于使用函数（函数应用）。分别写出它们的判断。提示：你可能还需要重新考虑类型集合。 Exercise:  Let’s now add functions. We need two new constructs: one to introduce them ( lambda ) and one to use them (function application). Write down judgments for each. Hint:  You may need to revisit the set of types, too.

注意，由于 let 会脱糖为 lambda，一旦有了这些，原则上我们也就有了 let 的有条件规则。（对于更复杂的语言构造，事情没这么直接；这篇论文推导了一些细节。） Observe that because let  desugars into lambda , once we have this, in principle we also have a conditional rule for let . (For more sophisticated language constructs this is not so straightforward; this paper  works out some of the details.)

练习：为类型检查器添加脱糖。 Exercise:  Add desugaring to the type-checker.

类型与求值从何处分道扬镳 Where Types Diverge from Evaluation

上面发生了一件非常重要而微妙的事。将条件构造的类型规则与求值过程比较一下。如果规则太抽象，就看看上面那些判断（或失败的判断）的例子。求值器只会对 T 和 E 中的一个分支求值；事实上，这正是条件构造的全部意义。相比之下，类型检查器会遍历两个分支！换句话说，它会查看可能被求值的代码，而不只是肯定会被求值的代码。 Something very important, and subtle, happened above. Compare the type rule  for a conditional with the evaluation  process. If the rule is too abstract, just look at the example judgments (or failed judgments) above. The evaluator evaluates only one  branch out of T  and E ; indeed, that is the entire point  of a conditional. The type-checker, in contrast, traverses both  branches! In other words, it looks at code that might  evaluate, not only code that absolutely does  evaluate.

换句话说，把类型检查器看作“在简单值上运行的求值器”，是一种方便的入门类比，但实际上并不正确。求值器和类型检查器采用不同的遍历策略。因此，像 (if true 1 "hi") 这样的程序可能运行起来毫无困难，却会被类型检查器拒绝。这个具体例子可能会让类型检查器显得过于迂腐，但如果同一个程序变成 In other words, the idea that a type-checker is like an “evaluator that runs over simple values” is a convenient starting analogy, but it is in fact false. An evaluator and type-checker follow different traversal strategies. That is why a program like (if true 1 "hi")  might run without any difficulty but is rejected by a type-checker. While this particular example may make the type-checker look overly pedantic, what if the same program were

(if (is-full-moon) 1 "hi")

现在怎么办？类型检查器应该每个月都放行这个程序吗？它应该考虑类型检查时的月相，还是执行时的月相？不幸的是，类型检查器不知道程序何时会运行；事实上，程序只做一次类型检查，却可能运行任意多次。因此，类型检查器必然必须采取保守策略。 What now? Should the type-checker pass the program every month? Should it consider the moon’s phase at the time of type-checking or at execution? Unfortunately, the type-checker doesn’t know when the program will run; indeed, the program is type-checked once but may run an arbitrary number of times. Therefore, a type-checker must necessarily be conservative .

这也让我们能够将类型检查与测试联系起来。在软件测试中，确保所有分支都被访问，叫作分支覆盖；让所有分支都得到覆盖，既重要又非常困难（因为每个分支内部可能还有分支，而这些分支又可能有更多分支，而这些分支又……）。相比之下，类型检查器可以毫不费力地覆盖两个分支。代价在于，它只在类型层面这样做（而且，正是将值抽象为类型，才使它能够做到这一点）。 This also lets us relate type-checking to testing . In software testing, making sure that all branches are visited is called branch coverage , and making sure all branches have coverage is both important and very difficult (because each branch may have additional branches which in turn may have even more branches which…). In contrast, a type-checker effortlessly covers both branches. The trade-off is that it does so only at the type  level (and indeed, the abstraction of values to types is precisely what enables it to do this).

因此，测试与类型检查是互补的。类型检查在轻量层面提供代码覆盖；测试通常只提供部分覆盖，却深入到具体值的层面。近年来，人们发明了“混合执行测试”（concolic，即“concrete”［具体］加“symbolic”［符号］）这一概念，试图兼得两者之长。 Thus, testing and type-checking are complementary. Type-checking provides code coverage at a lightweight level; testing typically provides only partial coverage but at the deep level of specific values. In recent years, people have invented a notion of concolic —i.e., “concrete” + “symbolic”—testing to try to create the best of both worlds.

扩展类型：为函数确定类型 Growing Types: Typing Functions

现在我们可以进一步扩展语言，把函数加入其中。正如前面指出的，函数这样的概念总是成对出现：一种引入它们的方式，以及一种使用（“消去”）它们的方式。和解释器中一样，我们用 lambda 形式表示前者，用应用表示后者。我们已经看到，有了 lambda，就能借助语法糖得到 let 等其他形式，因此这些足以构成我们的核心语言。（基本上如此，后面我们会看到……） Now we’re ready to grow our language further, to include functions. As we’ve noted before, concepts like functions come in pairs: a way to introduce them and a way to use (“eliminate”) them. As in our interpreter, we’ll use a lambda  form to represent the former and application for the latter. We’ve already seen that once we have lambda , we use syntactic sugar to obtain other forms like let , so this suffices for our core language. (Mostly, as we’ll see…)

因此，我们必须为应用和 lambda 制定类型规则。就按这个顺序来吧。 So we have to come up with typing rules for application and lambda . Let’s do them in that order.

为函数应用确定类型 Typing Function Applications

函数应用表达式有两个部分：函数和实参。为简单起见，我们假定处理的都是单实参函数。 A function application expression has two parts: the function and the arguments. For simplicity, we’re going to assume that we’re working with single-argument functions.

练习：扩展下面的规则，使其能处理具有任意数量形参的函数（这个数量的正式名称是元数，arity）。 Exercise:  Extend the rules below to deal with functions of arbitrary number of parameters (formally called arity ).

因为函数是一等值，所以函数位置本身也是一个表达式。要为整个表达式确定类型，必须先检查每个子表达式。因此，函数应用的规则是前提中含有两个项的条件规则： Because functions are first-class values, the function position is itself an expression. We have to check each sub-expression before we can type the whole expression. Therefore, function applications are conditional rules with two terms in the antecedent:

|- F : ???    |- A : ???

------------------------

|- (F A) : ???

首先注意，函数与其他值属于不同种类：函数本身不是数字、字符串或布尔值——它可能产生其中某一种值，但它本身并不是那种值（这是一个重要区别）。因此，我们需要一种不同的类型来表示函数，它要反映函数接受什么、产生什么。一个自然的想法是假设函数具有某种“函数”类型，这里称作 Fun： First, let’s notice that functions are different kinds of values than other values: a function is not itself a number, or string, or Boolean—it may produce  one of those, but it is not itself  one of those (an important distinction). Therefore, we need a different type for functions, which reflects what functions consume and what they produce. A natural idea is to assume functions have some “function” type, here called Fun :

|- F : Fun    |- A : ???

------------------------

|- (F A) : ???

对于实参表达式（实际参数），我们知道些什么？它的类型必须与形式参数要求的类型匹配。但在这里怎样检查呢？我们把世界上所有函数都归入了同一种类型 Fun。这实在太粗糙了。 What do we know about the argument expression (the actual parameter)? It had better match the type demanded by the formal parameter. But how do we check that here? We’ve collapsed all  functions in the world into a single type, Fun . That’s far too coarse.

因此，我们遵循惯例，用“箭头”语法表示函数： Instead, following convention, we’ll use the “arrow” syntax for functions:

|- F : (??? -> ???)    |- A : ???

---------------------------------

|- (F A) : ???

（严格来说，箭头是函数类型的构造器。它是一个二元构造器，原因下面就会看到。） (Technically, the arrow is a constructor  of function types. It’s a two-place constructor, for reasons we will see below.)

这样一来，我们现在就能说，函数形参的类型必须与实际实参的类型匹配。究竟是什么类型呢？函数可能接受数字、字符串，甚至其他函数……我们只知道两者应该一致。注意，这与我们对条件表达式各分支所要求的一致性非常相似。我们同样可以在两个位置使用相同的占位符来表达这一点： With this, we can now say that the function’s formal parameter’s type had better match up with the type of the actual argument. Which type, exactly? Functions could consume numbers, strings, even other functions…all we know is that these should be consistent . Notice that this is very similar to the consistency we expected of the branches of a conditional. We can again encode this by using the same placeholder in both places:

|- F : (T -> ???)    |- A : T

-----------------------------

|- (F A) : ???

那么，函数返回的东西呢？同样，它可能返回任何类型的值。无论是什么类型，那就是整个应用产生的类型。我们再次使用共同的占位符来反映这一点： Now, what about what the function returns? Again, it could return values of any type. Whatever that type is, that is what the entire application produces. Again, we use a common placeholder to reflect this:

|- F : (T -> U)    |- A : T

---------------------------

|- (F A) : U

因此，我们这样解读它： So here’s how we read this:

  • 对 F 位置进行类型检查。确保它具有函数类型（->）。假如是这样，就把形参的类型称为 T，把返回类型称为 U。 Type-check the F  position. Make sure it’s a function type ( -> ). Assuming it is, call the formal parameter’s type T  and the return type U .
  • 对实际参数（实参）进行类型检查。确保它的类型与函数形参所期望的类型相同。 Type-check the actual parameter (the argument). Make sure it has the same type as what the function is expecting in its formal parameter.
  • 如果这两点都成立，那么函数的返回类型就是整个应用的类型。 If both of those hold, then the function’s return type is the type of the entire application.

传统的类型检查器会实现这一系列步骤。注意，类型错误再次体现为无法构造出一个判断。例如，如果实参的类型与形参的类型不匹配，上面的条件规则就不适用（只有当我们能为占位符 T 写下同一类型时，它才适用）；我们就是这样得知程序存在类型错误的。 This list of steps is what a conventional type-checker would implement. Observe that again, a type error is the result of a failure to construct a judgment. If, for instance, the actual argument’s type doesn’t match that of the formal parameter, then the conditional rule above doesn’t apply  (it applies only when we can write the same type for the T  placeholder), which is how we learn that the program has a type error.

练习：构造一个例子，说明上述类型错误的情况。 Exercise:  Construct an example to illustrate the above type-error case.

旁注：我们故意没有使用编号列表，因为从形式上说，判断的语义并未规定这些步骤必须按这个顺序进行！例如，可以先对实参进行类型检查，再检查函数；这样就由实参确定占位符 T 代表什么，而检查 F 则是确认 F 的类型与之匹配。 Aside:  We intentionally don’t use a numbered  list because formally, the semantics of judgments doesn’t say that these steps have to occur in this order! For instance, the argument can be type-checked before the function; if so, that determines what the placeholder T  stands for, and the checking of F  confirms that F ’s type matches that.

甚至还可以更反其道而行之：设想先检查应用，根据上下文确定它需要具有什么类型（例如，如果它处在加法中，就必须产生数字），再以此驱动对 F 的检查。事实上，如果我们实现的不是检查器，而是类型推断，这些事情全都可能发生——我们很快就会看到。 Even more perversely, you can imagine checking the application, determining—from the context—what its type needs  to be (e.g., if it’s in an addition, it had better produce a number), and using that to drive the checking of F . In fact, all of these things can happen if instead of a checker , we implement type- inference —as we will soon see.

为函数定义确定类型 Typing Function Definitions

现在可以为 lambda 确定类型了。这里必须小心数清子表达式有几个。对于 (lambda V B)，我们很容易认为有两个：V（形参）和 B（函数体）。这是错的！形参是字面上的名称，不是表达式：我们不能用一个更大的表达式替换这个名称，而若它真是表达式，就应当可以这样替换。此外，我们也不能对它求值：这样做（很可能）会产生未绑定变量错误，因为它的全部职责就是绑定这个变量，所以不能假定它已经被绑定。因此，只有一个子表达式，即函数体。 Now we’re ready to type lambda . Here, we have to be careful about how many sub-expressions there are. Given (lambda V B) , it is tempting to think that there are two: V  (the formal parameter) and B  (the body). This is wrong! The formal parameter is a literal name, not  an expression: we can’t replace that name with some larger expression, which is what it would mean for it to be an expression. Furthermore, we can’t evaluate it: it would (most likely) produce an unbound variable error, because its whole job is to bind  that variable, so it can’t assume it has already been bound. Therefore, there is only one  sub-expression, the body.

因此，我们预期最终得到一个如下形式的条件规则： Therefore, we expect to end up with a conditional rule that looks like this:

|- B : ???

---------------------

|- (lambda V B) : ???

稍加思考就能看出，这里会出现一个问题。我们刚说过，lambda 会为 V 位置上的变量引入绑定。这恰恰是为了让函数体 B 能够使用这个变量。因此，设想最简单的函数： If we think about this for a moment, we can see that there’s going to be a problem.  We just said that the lambda  introduces a binding for the variable in the V  position. This is precisely so that the body, B , can make use of that variable. So let’s imagine the simplest function:

|- x : ???

---------------------

|- (lambda x x) : ???

但我们没有任何涵盖变量的类型规则！此外，我们也无法知道任意一个变量的类型会是什么。所以遇到了问题。 But we don’t have any typing rule that covers variables! Furthermore, we have no way of knowing what the type of any old variable will be. So we have a problem.
