为变量确定类型 Typing Variables

还记得我们在解释器中怎样处理这个问题吗：用环境记录每个变量绑定的值。我们将再次采用同样的思路：用类型环境记录每个变量的类型。也就是说，正如解释器具有这个类型 Remember how we addressed this problem in our interpreter: we had an environment  for recording the value bound to each variable. We will use this same idea again: we’ll have a type environment  for recording the type  of each variable. That is, just as our interpreter had the type

(interp : (Exp Env -> Value))

我们的类型检查器也将具有这个类型 our type-checker will have the type

(tc : (Exp TEnv -> Type))

在类型检查器的记法中，我们会采用略有不同的写法，终于让 |- 不再沉默，而是读出它本来的读音“证明”：所有类型规则都将具有如下形式 In our type-checker notation, we will use a slightly different way of writing it, which will finally make make |-  stop being silent and take its proper pronunciation, “proves”: all type rules will have the form

Γ |- e : T

其中，按照惯例，用大写希腊字母 gamma，即 Γ，表示环境。我们将它读作“环境 Γ 证明 e 具有类型 T”。因此，事实上，我们所有的判断中一直都隐藏着一个环境，只是在还没有变量时，无须操心它；但现在有了变量，所以从现在起必须把它明确写出来。幸运的是，在大多数情况下，环境都保持不变，只是递归地传给各个子项，这与你编写解释器时的预期一致。 where Γ , the capital Greek letter gamma, is conventionally used for the environment. We read this as “the environment Γ  proves that e  has type T ”. So in fact there’s been an environment hiding in all our judgments, but we didn’t have to worry about it when we didn’t have variables; but now we do, so from now on we have to make it explicit. Fortunately, in most cases the environment is unchanged, and just passes recursively to the sub-terms, as you would expect from writing the interpreter.

有了这些，我们就能写出变量的类型了。变量的类型是什么？环境说是什么就是什么！我们把环境视为函数，因此可以直接写下如下公理（其中 v 代表所有语法上合法的变量名）： With this, we can write a type for variables. What is the type of a variable? It’s whatever the environment says it is! We’ll treat the environment as a function, so we can just write the following axiom (where v  stands for all the syntactically valid variable names):

Γ |- v : Γ (v)

回到函数定义的类型 Back to Typing Function Definitions

现在可以填补空缺了。检查函数体时，应该在扩展后的环境中进行： Now we’re in a position to fill in the holes. When we check the body of the function, we should do it in an extended  environment:

Γ [V <- ???]   |- B : ???

-----------------------

Γ |- (lambda V B) : ???

其中，Γ[V <- _] 是我们表示“扩展 Γ，使 V 绑定到 _”的写法：这与之前写过的环境扩展函数相同，只不过操作的是类型环境而非值环境，操作方式则完全一样。 where Γ[V <- _] is how we write “ Γ  is extended with V  bound to _”: this is the same environment-extension function that we’ve written before, for type environments instead of value environments, but operationally the same.

好，不过有两个问题：扩展哪个环境，又用什么来扩展它？ Okay, but two questions: extend which  environment, and extend it with what ?

哪个环境很容易回答：就是函数定义所在的环境（静态作用域！）。在结论和前提中重复出现的 Γ 就实现了这一点。 Which is easy: it’s the environment of the function definition (static scope!). The repetition of Γ  in both the consequent and antecedent accomplishes that.

至于用什么来扩展：我们需要为变量提供一个类型，这样当尝试查找它的类型时，环境才能返回某个结果。但我们不知道该用什么来扩展！类型检查器需要程序员告诉它，函数期望什么类型。这就是编程语言要求在函数和方法定义中提供注解的原因之一。（另一个同样充分的理由是，这能为必须使用和维护函数的人更好地说明函数。） In terms of what:  We need to provide a type for the variable so that, when we try to look up its type, the environment can return something. But we don’t know what to extend it with! The type-checker needs the programmer to tell it  what type the function is expecting. This is one of the reasons why programming languages expect annotations in function and method definitions. (Another—equally good—reason is because it better documents the function for people who have to use it and maintain it.)

因此，我们必须扩展函数的语法，使其包含类型注解： Therefore, we have to extend the syntax of functions to include a type annotation:

(lambda V : T B)

这表示，在函数体 B 中，V 预期绑定到一个类型为 T 的值。接受了这个修改后，我们就能继续完善条件规则： which says that V  is expecting to be bound to a value of type T  in body B . Once we accept this modification, we can make progress on the conditional rule:

Γ[V <- T ] |- B : ???

---------------------------

Γ |- (lambda V : T  B) : ???

我们期望函数定义具有什么类型？显然，它必须是函数类型： What type are we expecting for the function definition? Clearly it must be a function type:

Γ[V <- T] |- B : ???

------------------------------------

Γ |- (lambda V : T B) : (??? -> ???)

此外，我们知道函数期望的类型必须是 T： Furthermore, we know that the type expected by the function must be T :

Γ[V <- T] |- B : ???

----------------------------------

Γ |- (lambda V : T B) : ( T  -> ???)

给定一个类型为 T 的值，函数就会返回函数体所产生的结果： Given a value of type T , the function will return whatever the body produces:

Γ[V <- T] |- B : U

--------------------------------

Γ |- (lambda V : T B) : (T -> U )

这样，我们就得到了函数定义的最终规则。 And that gives us our final rule for function definitions.

类型与求值之间的更多分歧 More Divergence Between Types and Evaluation

把上述这对类型规则与相应的求值规则对比一下，很有意思。在求值器中，每次应用时都会访问函数体——在一个程序中，这可能多达无穷次。相比之下，我们在定义时访问函数体，而这只发生一次。因此，即使程序永远运行下去，类型检查器也保证会终止！ It is interesting to contrast the above pair of typing rules with the corresponding evaluation rules. In the evaluator, we visit the body of the function on every application —which could be as many as an infinite number of times in a program. In contrast, we visit the body of the function on definition , which happens only once. Therefore, even if the program runs forever, the type-checker is guaranteed to terminate!

为什么我们可以这样做？求值器必须用给定的具体值运行函数体。而类型检查器已经把具体值抽象掉了。因此，它只需要用这个“抽象值”，也就是类型，遍历函数体一次。 Why can we get away with this? The evaluator has to run the body with the specific  value it was given. The type-checker, however, has abstracted the concrete values away. Therefore, it only needs to make one pass through the body with the “abstract value”, the type.

旁注：前面提出 Fun 类型时，我们说它把世界上所有函数都归入同一个类型。这太粗糙了，所以必须细化函数的类型。不过，我们仍然把无穷多个函数归入每一种函数类型——正如把无穷多个字符串归入 Str，等等。类型检查的优点与缺点都在于这种归并。 Aside: Earlier, when we proposed the type Fun , we said that it collapsed all functions in the world into one type. This was too coarse, and we had to refine the type of a function. However, we are still  collapsing an infinite number of functions into each of those function types—just as we collapse an infinite number of strings into Str , and so on. Both the strength and weakness of type-checking lies in this collapsing.

出于同样的原因，请注意，函数应用规则只关心函数的类型，而不关心具体应用的是哪个函数。因此，任何具有该类型的函数都可以使用。同样由于这个原因，类型检查器不能在应用时遍历函数体——它甚至不知道可能使用的是哪个函数！函数体和应用之间的所有交流，都必须完全通过类型边界进行。 For the same reason, observe that a function application rule only cares about the type  of the function, not which  specific function is being applied. Therefore, any function that has that type can be used. For that same reason, the type-checker cannot  traverse the function’s body at application time—it doesn’t even know which function might be used! All communication between the function body and application must happen entirely through the type boundary.

假设—保证推理 Assume-Guarantee Reasoning

应用与定义的这些类型规则之间存在一种微妙的配合（现在已更新为包含环境）。我们用颜色来突出这种联系： There is a delicate dance going on between these typing rules for application and definition (now updated to have the environment). We’ll use colors to highlight this:

Γ |- F : (T -> U)     Γ |- A : T

-------------------------------

Γ |- (F A) : U

Γ[V <- T ] |- B : U

--------------------------------

Γ |- (lambda V : T B) : (T -> U)

lambda 的规则假设形参会得到一个类型为 T 的值；应用规则则保证实参确实具有期望的类型。应用规则假设，给定一个 T，函数就会产生一个 U（因为类型是 (T -> U)）；lambda 规则则保证函数确实会如此表现。（仅从这对规则中，确实还可以找出更多联系；希望这些已经说明了基本思路。） The rule for lambda   assumes  the parameter will be given a value of type T ; the application rule guarantees  that that the actual parameter will indeed have the expected type. The application rule assumes  that the function, if given a T , will produce a U  (because the type is (T -> U) ); the lambda  rule guarantees  that the function will indeed perform that way. (There are indeed more connections to draw just from this pair of rules; hopefully this illustrates the general idea.)

旁注：(T -> U) 这个记法并非随意选取。-> 可能让你想起数学中表示蕴含的记法。这是有意为之。我们可以把这个类型读作“给函数一个 T，就意味着它会产生一个 U”（不给它 T，则不能据此推断它会做什么……）。应用规则假设的正是这个蕴含关系，而 lambda 的规则保证的也是它。 Aside:  The notation (T -> U)  is not chosen at random. The ->  may remind you of the notation for implication in mathematics. That’s intentional. We can read the type as “giving the function a T  implies that it will produce a U ” (not giving it a T  implies nothing about what it will do…). It is that implication  that is assumed in the application rule, and that is guaranteed by the rule for lambda.

这种假设—保证推理会出现在许多地方，因此，也要留意其他地方是否存在这种模式。 This assume-guarantee reasoning shows up in many places, so look out for this pattern in other places as well.

递归与无限循环 Recursion and Infinite Loops

前面我们提到过，可以把更有意思的特性脱糖为函数和应用。来看一个非常具体的特性：无限循环。先确认一下，我们能够写出无限循环。下面这个程序就能做到： We alluded, earlier, to how we can desugar more interesting features into functions and application. Let’s take a look at a very specific feature: an infinite loop. Let’s first confirm that we can write an infinite loop. Here’s a program that does it:

fun f():

  f()

f()

但这假定我们已经有了递归。不用递归能写出来吗？其实可以！我们采用历史上使用的名称（ω 是小写希腊字母 omega）： But this assumes we already have recursion. Can we write it without recursion? Actually we can! We’ll use historical names ( ω  is the lower-case Greek omega):

(let ([ ω  (lambda (x) (x x))])

  ( ω   ω ))

在 Racket 中运行它，确认它会永远运行下去！ Run this in Racket and confirm that it runs forever!

现在动手：为 let 写一条条件类型规则。 Do Now:  Write a conditional type rule for let .

现在看看尝试为它确定类型时会发生什么。我们必须提供一个类型注解： Now let’s see what happens when we try to type this. We have to provide a type annotation:

(let ([ ω  (lambda (x : ???) (x x))])

  ( ω   ω ))

历史上，整个项被称为 Ω（大写希腊字母 omega）。 Historically, the overall term is called Ω  (the capital Greek omega).

好，那么注解是什么呢？要确定 x 的类型，必须看它的用法。它用了两次。一次出现在函数应用的函数位置，因此我们知道类型必须具有 (T -> U) 的形式；现在必须确定 T 和 U 分别是什么。先看参数类型 T。但传入的是什么？传入的是 x，而它的类型是 (T -> U)。因此，我们需要求解这个方程 Okay, so what is the annotation? To determine a type for x , we have to see how it’s used. It’s used twice. One use is in a function application position, so we know that the type must be of the form (T -> U) ; now we have to determine what T  and U  are. Let’s focus on the parameter type, T . But what are we passing in? We’re passing in x , whose type is (T -> U) . So we need a solution to the equation

T  = (T -> U)

其中一边来自应用的函数位置，另一边来自实参位置。当然，不存在能满足这个方程的有限类型！因此，看起来这个程序无法被赋予类型！ with one coming from the application position and the other from the argument position. Of course, there is no finite type that can fit this equation! Therefore, it appears that this program cannot be typed!

当然，这不是证明。不过，这门编程语言有一个形式化性质；这门语言称为简单类型 lambda 演算（Simply Typed Lambda Calculus，STLC），这个性质称为强规范化，意思是这门语言中的所有程序都会终止。 Of course, this is not a proof. However, there is a formal property associated with this programming language, which is called the Simply Typed Lambda Calculus (STLC): the property is called strong normalization , and it means that all programs in this language terminate .

旁注：如果你听说过停机问题，它与你刚读到的内容如何相容？ Aside:  If you have heard about the Halting Problem, how does that square with what you just read?

一门所有程序都会终止的语言，似乎没什么用——你不能用它写操作系统、Web 服务器或许多其他程序。不过，这种看法忽略了两件事。 It may seem rather useless to have a language in which all programs terminate—you can’t write an operating system, or Web server, or many other programs in such a language. However, that misses two things.

第一，在许多情况下，我们希望程序总能终止。你不会希望网络数据包过滤器、设备驱动程序、编译器、类型检查器或……永远运行下去。当然，我们也希望它们运行得快，但如果能保证无论我们怎么做，都无法制造出无限循环，那将非常好。在某些这样的场景下，STLC 十分有用。另一个希望保证终止的场合是程序链接，因此 Standard ML 的模块语言建立在 STLC 之上：它甚至允许你编写高阶程序，但类型语言保证所有模块组合（链接）都会终止。 First, there are many cases where we want  programs to always terminate. You don’t want a network packet filter or a device driver or a compiler or a type-checker or … to run forever. Of course we also want them to run quickly, but it would be nice if we had a guarantee that no matter what we did, we cannot  create an infinite loop. The STLC is very useful in some of these settings. Another example of a place where we want guaranteed termination is in program linking, and the module language of Standard ML is therefore built atop the STLC: it lets you even write higher-order programs, but the type language guarantees that all module compositions (linkages) will terminate.

第二，许多长期运行的程序，实际上是无限循环与短时运行程序的组合。想想操作系统及其设备驱动程序、Web 服务器及其 Web 应用、GUI 及其回调，等等。每种情况都有一条无限循环构成的“脊柱”，只负责让程序持续响应；还有一些短小计算构成的“肋骨”，完成一点具体工作后就终止。事实上，在 Web 上，这些程序必须迅速终止，否则 Web 浏览器就会认为服务器挂起了，并提出关闭窗口！因此，这类响应式系统是由一个非常通用的无限循环调用具体程序组合而成的，而对于这些具体程序，终止保证往往非常有用。 Second, many long-running programs are actually a composition of an infinite loop and a short-running program. Think about an operating system with device drivers, a Web server with a Web application, a GUI with callbacks, etc. In each case, there is a “spine” of an infinite loop that simply keeps the program reactive, and “ribs” of short computations that do a little specific work and terminate. In fact, on the Web these programs must  terminate quickly, otherwise the Web browser thinks the server has hung and offers to kill the window! These kinds of reactive systems  are therefore a composition of a very generic infinite loop calling out to specific programs for which a termination guarantee will often be very useful.

最后，请注意，我们学到了一个深刻的道理。到目前为止，我们可能一直以为类型只是提供便利，或是消除基本错误的手段。但刚才我们看到，加入类型系统能够改变语言的表达能力。也就是说，这些类型具有“语义”意义。 Finally, observe that we’ve learned something profound. Until now, we have probably thought of types as just a convenience or as a way of eliminating basic errors. However, we have just now seen that adding a type system can change the expressive power of a language . That is, these types are “semantic”.

为递归确定类型 Typing Recursion

上面出了什么问题？问题在于，每次应用都会“消耗掉”函数类型中的一个箭头；因为程序文本必须有限，它最多只能包含有限个“箭头”，所以程序最终必须终止。要绕过这一点，我们需要某种方式，实际上拥有一个“无限箭袋”。 What went wrong above? The problem is that each application “uses up an arrow” in a function type; because a program text must be finite, it can contain at most a finite number of “arrows”, so eventually the program must terminate. To get around this, we need a way to effectively have an “infinite quiver”.

通常，我们会向语言加入递归函数构造，并为它专门制定类型规则。先从与之类似但更简单的 let 的类型规则开始： We typically do this by adding a recursive function construct to the language, and create a custom type for it. Let’s start with a type rule for the analogous, but simpler, let :

Γ |- E : T     Γ[V <- T] |- B : U

--------------------------------

Γ |- (let V : T E B) : U

注意，出于与函数定义相同的原因，我们将要求 let 中带有注解。因此，这条规则说，我们会检查 E 确实具有声明中承诺的类型 T；用类型为 T 的 V 扩展类型环境后，如果主体 B 产生类型 U，那么 U 就是整个表达式的类型。 Note that we’re going to expect an annotation in let  for the same reason we do for function definitions. So this says that we’ll check that E  actually does have the type promised in the declaration, T ; when we extend the type environment with the V  having type T , if the body B  produces type U , then that’s the type of the whole expression.

旁注：注意，前提中有一对假设—保证关系：第一项保证注解成立，而第二项则假设它成立。 Aside:  Notice that there’s an assume-guarantee pair in the antecedent: the first term is guaranteeing the annotation, which the second term is assuming.

旁注：严格来说，E 的类型是可以计算出来的。因此，T 注解并非绝对必要。 Aside:  Technically, the type of E  could be calculated . Therefore, the T  annotation is not strictly necessary.

注意，这基本上就是展开 let 的语法糖所得到的类型规则。因此，它仍不能让我们编写递归定义。我们还需要别的东西。为递归定义引入一个新构造 rec。在无类型的情形中，rec 的一个例子可能是 Observe that this is basically the type rule we would get from expanding the syntactic sugar for let . Therefore, this still doesn’t let us write a recursive definition. We need something more. Let’s introduce a new construct, rec , for recursive definitions. An example of a rec  (in an untyped setting) might be

(rec ([inf-loop (lambda (n) (inf-loop n))])

  (inf-loop 0))

(rec ([fact (lambda (n) (if (zero? n) 1 (* n (fact (- n 1)))))])

  (fact 10))

在有类型的世界里，我们希望 rec 具有如下形式 In the typed world, we’ll want rec to have the form

(rec V : T E B)

因此，我们就必须改写为 so we’d instead have to write

(rec inf-loop : (Number -> Number)

     (lambda (n) (inf-loop n))

  (inf-loop 0))

(rec fact : (Number -> Number)

     (lambda (n) (if (zero? n) 1 (* n (fact (- n 1)))))

  (fact 10))

其中 V 是 fact，T 是 (Number -> Number)，E 是那个很大的 lambda 项，而 B 是 (fact 10)。 where V  is fact , T  is (Number -> Number) , E  is the big lambda  term, and B  is (fact 10) .

因此，它引入一个递归定义，然后使用它。我们可以怎样为它确定类型？ So this introduces a recursive definition, and then uses it. How might we type this?

???

------------------------

Γ |- (rec V : T E B) : U

显然，其中一部分必须相同：必须在扩展后的环境中为主体确定类型，并且必须用注解中的类型来扩展环境： Well, clearly one part of it must be the same: we have to type the body in the extended environment, and the environment must be extended with the annotated type:

???    Γ[V <- T] |- B : U

-------------------------

Γ |- (rec V : T E B) : U

我们也知道，必须确认注解正确： We also know that we need to confirm that the annotation is correct:

??? |- E : T     Γ[V <- T] |- B : U

----------------------------------

Γ |- (rec V : T E B) : U

但显然，必须有某个地方不同，否则就只是重新造了一个 let。看看 rec 的使用示例：E 项中也需要有 V 的绑定！换句话说，E 和 B 都在同一个环境中确定类型： But clearly, something  needs to be different, otherwise we’ve just reproduced let . Look at the example use of rec : the E  term also needs to have V  bound in it! In other words, both E  and B  are typed in the same environment:

Γ[V <- T] |- E : T     Γ[V <- T] |- B : U

----------------------------------------

Γ |- (rec V : T E B) : U

从类型中，我们可以看出递归如何发生：B 的扩展环境启动递归，而 E 的扩展环境维持递归。从本质上说，E 的环境允许任意递归深度。 From the type, we can read off how the recursion happens: the extended environment for B   initiates  the recursion, while that for E   sustains  it. Essentially, the environment of E  enables arbitrary recursive depth.

简言之，要获得任意递归——从而获得无限循环——必须在语言及其类型检查器中加入特殊构造；仅靠脱糖无法得到它。不过，一旦把 rec 加入 STLC，我们就又得到了一门常规编程语言。 In short, to obtain arbitrary recursion—and hence infinite loops—we have to add a special construct to the language and its type-checker; we cannot obtain it just through desugaring. Once we add rec  to the STLC, however, we obtain a conventional programming language again.

安全性与健全性 Safety and Soundness

SMoL 的一个关键组成部分是安全性这个概念：某些操作对于所有值构成的集合而言是部分定义的，而 SMoL 语言会通过报告违规来强制遵守这一限制。部分定义的典型例子可能包括 + 只适用于某些类型的值。不过，我有意写的是“操作”，而非比如“函数”，因为它们也可能是应用这样的原始操作（要求第一个位置上的是函数或方法）。事实上，在 JavaScript 等某些语言中，违规情况非常少，Wat 演讲就展示了这一点。 A critical component of SMoL is the concept of safety : that some operations are partial  over the set of all values, and that a SMoL language enforces this by reporting violations. Typical examples of partiality may include +  applying only to certain types of values. However, I intentionally write “operations” rather than, say, “functions”, because these could be primitive operations like application (expecting the first position to be a function or method) as well. In fact, in some languages like JavaScript, there are very few violations, as the Wat talk  shows.

必须怎样实施这些约束？既可以静态实施，也可以动态实施。例如，在 Python 和 JavaScript 中，所有安全性违规都在动态时报告。在 Java 或 OCaml 中，大多数则在静态时报告。无论哪种方式，安全性都意味着数据具有完整性：对于“它们是什么”存在某种界定，而操作会尊重这种身份。换句话说，数据不会被误解。 How must these be enforced? It can be either statically or dynamically. In Python and JavaScript, for instance, all safety violations are reported dynamically. In Java or OCaml, most of them are reported statically. Either way, safety means that data have integrity : there is some notion of “what they are”, and that identity is respected by operations. Put differently, data are not misinterpreted .

这些说法都很抽象，我们很快就会把它们具体化。 These are all very abstract statements, which we will soon concretize.

重访基本计算器 Revisiting the Basic Calculator

我们从一个非常基本的计算器开始，它有两种类型：数字和字符串，并分别为它们提供一种操作（加法和拼接）。注意，要讨论安全性，拥有不止一种类型会很有帮助。我们会跳过大部分样板代码，重点看计算器的核心： We will start with a very basic calculator that has two types, numbers and strings, and an operation (addition and concatenation, respectively) on them. Note that it helps to have more than one type if we want to talk about safety. We will skip most of the boilerplate code and focus on the core of the calculator:

(define-type Exp

  [num (n : Number)]

  [str (s : String)]

  [plus (l : Exp) (r : Exp)]

  [cat (l : Exp) (r : Exp)])

(define-type Value

  (numV (n : Number))

  (strV (s : String)))

(calc : (Exp -> Value))

(define (calc e)

  (type-case Exp e

    [(num n) (numV n)]

    [(str s) (strV s)]

    [(plus l r) (num+ (calc l) (calc r))]

    [(cat l r) (str++ (calc l) (calc r))]))

(define (num+ lv rv)

  (type-case Value lv

    ((numV ln)

     (type-case Value rv

       ((numV rn) (numV (+ ln rn)))

       (else (error '+ "right not a number"))))

    (else (error '+ "left not a number"))))

(define (str++ lv rv)

  (type-case Value lv

    ((strV ls)

     (type-case Value rv

       ((strV rs) (strV (string-append ls rs)))

       (else (error '++ "right not a string"))))

    (else (error '++ "left not a string"))))

你可能以为后两个函数只是方便使用的辅助函数，因此会奇怪它们为什么属于“核心”。你很快就会明白！ You might have imagined the latter two functions to be merely convenient helpers, and hence wonder why they are part of the “core”. You will soon see why!

有了合适的解析器，我们就能运行如下测试： With a suitable parser, we can run tests such as the following:

(test (calc (plus (num 1) (num 2))) (numV 3))

(test (calc (plus (num 1) (plus (num 2) (num 3)))) (numV 6))

(test (calc (cat (str "hel") (str "lo"))) (strV "hello"))

(test (calc (cat (cat (str "hel") (str "l")) (str "o"))) (strV "hello"))

(test/exn (calc (cat (num 1) (str "hello"))) "left")

(test/exn (calc (plus (num 1) (str "hello"))) "right")

尤其是最后两个测试，说明这门语言是安全的。原语内部的检查——例如 num+ 中的检查——称为安全检查。 The last two, in particular, show that the language is safe. The checks inside the primitives—in num+ , for instance—are called safety checks .

（不安全地）将内存显式化 Making Memory Explicit (Unsafely)

现在来做一件有趣的事：把值的内存分配显式化。在这个过程中，请记住我们之前说过的话：SMoL 中的值就是一个内存地址。 Now we’re going to do something fun: we’re going to make the memory allocation of values explicit. As we go through this, remember what we’ve said before: a value in SMoL is just a memory address.

分阶段进行吧。首先，用一个向量表示内存： Let’s do this in stages. First, we’ll use a vector to represent memory:

(define MEMORY (make-vector 100 -1))

值 -1 有助于识别尚未触及的内存部分（当然，前提是我们不编写会产生 -1 的程序——在这个示例中，我们很容易避免这一点）。 The value -1  is useful for identifying parts of memory that have not yet been touched (assuming, of course, we don’t write a program that produces -1 —which we can avoid doing easily enough in this illustration).

旁注：要运行下面的代码，需要向 plait 导入一些 Racket 原语： Aside:  To run the code below, you will need to import some Racket primitives into plait:

(require (typed-in racket/base

                   [char->integer : (Char -> Number)]

                   [integer->char : (Number -> Char)]

                   [number->string : (Number -> String)]))

有一个辅助函数来使用下一块可用内存，会很有帮助： It will be useful to have a helper to use the next available bit of memory:

(define next-addr 0)

(define (write-and-bump v)

  (let ([n next-addr])

    (begin

      (vector-set! MEMORY n v)

      (set! next-addr (add1 next-addr))

      n)))

现在假设要在内存中存一个数字。我们把它放到下一个可用的内存位置，并返回存放这个数字的位置的地址。这里要小心：返回的数字是一个内存地址（这里用数组索引表示），它完全不一定等于所存储的数值。 Now let’s say we want to store a number in memory. We put it in the next available memory place, and return the address  of the place where the number was stored. Be careful here: the number we return is a memory address (which, here, is represented as an array index), which is not at all necessarily the same as the numeric value  being stored.

(define (store-num n)

  (write-and-bump n))

相应地，要读取一个数字时，我们只需返回该数字所对应地址处的内容。 Correspondingly, when we want to read a number, we simply return what is at the address corresponding to the number.

(define (read-num a)

  (vector-ref MEMORY a))

我们希望满足这样的性质：用 read-num 读取通过 store-num 存入一个数字的地址时，取回的就是原来的数字；对所有 N， We want the property that when we read-num  from the address where we store-num  a number, we get back that same number: for all N ,

(read-num (store-num N)) 就是 N (read-num (store-num N))  is N

旁注：这与大多数语言实际存储数字的方式并不完全相同。正如下面更新计算器时会看到的，这意味着每当产生某个数字——比如 1730——都要在内存中重新存储它。这会极其浪费。语言实现实际上会使用一些表示技巧，确保数字只有一个副本，而且完全不需要占用堆空间，下面会说明 [ 👉 ]。不过，我们将继续采用这个简单模型，因为这种优化并非本章重点。此外，有些数字——无法装进少量空间的那些——确实需要存储在堆上。 Aside:  This is not quite exactly how numbers are stored in most languages. As we will see when we update the calculator below, this means every time we produce a particular number— 1730 , say—we store it afresh in memory. That would be extremely wasteful. Rather, language implementations use representation tricks to make sure there is only one copy of numbers and that they don’t need to take up space on the heap at all, as we describe below [ 👉 ]. However, we will continue to work with this simple model because this optimization is not the focus of this chapter. In addition, some  numbers—that don’t fit in a small amount of space— do  need to be stored on the heap.

现在来看字符串。我们要把字符串转换为字符编码序列，并显式存储这些编码： Now let’s look at strings. We are going to convert the string into a sequence of character codes, and store those codes explicitly:

(define (store-str s)

  (let ([a0 (write-and-bump (string-length s))])

    (begin

      (map write-and-bump

           (map char->integer (string->list s)))

      a0)))

具体而言，代表字符串的地址处存储的是字符串长度，后面跟着各个字符。（字符串是否应在开头存储长度，还是只用特殊值分隔，或两者兼有，人们已经为此争得头破血流。这里这个问题并不重要。）因此，假设在全新的内存上运行 In particular, the value stored at the address representing the string is the length  of the string, followed by the individual characters. (Endless blood has been spent over whether strings should store their lengths at the front, or whether they should only be delimited by a special value, or both. The question is uninteresting here.) Thus, suppose with a fresh memory we run

(store-str "hello")

它会返回地址 0。此时 MEMORY 的值是 this would return the address 0 . The resulting value of MEMORY  would be

'#(5

   104

   101

   108

   108

   111

   -1

   -1

   -1

   …)

也就是说，地址 0 处是字符串长度，后面跟着五个字符编码；这六个内存条目共同构成了五字符的字符串 "hello"。其余内存保持未触及的状态。要读取字符串，必须将它重新组装起来： That is, at address 0  we have the length of the string, followed by five character codes; these six memory entries together constitute the five-character string "hello" . The rest of the memory remains untouched. To read a string we have to reassemble it:

(define (read-str a)

  (letrec ([loop

            (lambda (count a)

              (if (zero? count)

                  empty

                  (cons (vector-ref MEMORY a)

                        (loop (sub1 count) (add1 a)))))])

    (list->string

     (map integer->char

          (loop (vector-ref MEMORY a) (add1 a))))))

同样，我们希望读取已写入的字符串时，得到的结果就是原来那个字符串。 Once again, we want the result of reading a written string to give us the same string.

现在来更新计算器。首先，有个意外：我们不再需要（也不想要）复杂的 Racket 数据类型来跟踪值，因为值就是地址（即数组索引）！因此： Now let’s update the calculator. First, we’re in for a surprise: we no longer need (or want ) a fancy Racket datatype to track values, because values are just addresses (i.e., array indices)! So:

(define-type-alias Value Number)

计算器的类型并未改变；它仍然产生值。只是值的表示发生了……剧变。（再次提醒，这些 Number 是地址，而不是被解释语言中的数值。） The type  of the calculator doesn’t change; it still produces values. It’s just that the representation of values has changed…dramatically. (Recall, again, that these Number s are addresses, not numeric values in  the interpreted language.)

计算器保持不变。变化发生在辅助函数中。在基本值的情况下，我们必须显式分配它们——调用先前定义的 numV 和 strV（它们会把数据存到堆上）时，我们实际上也是这样做的，只不过当时可能没那么明显。我们将如下把它明确写出来： The calculator remains the same. What has changed is in the helper functions. In the primitive value cases, we have to explicitly allocate them—which is what we were doing when we called the previous definitions of numV  and strV  (which store data on the heap), except it may not have been so evident. We will make it explicit as follows:

(define numV store-num)

(define strV store-str)

好，现在更新辅助函数。重点看 num+。目前核心逻辑是 Okay, now to update the helper functions. Let’s focus on num+ . The core logic is currently

       [(numV rn) (numV (+ ln rn))]

注意，我们现在把调用 calc 的结果，也就是 Value，传给它。这意味着 num+ 会收到两个地址作为实参，需要在内存中查找对应的数字，然后产生作为结果的数字： Observe that now we’re calling it on the result of calling calc , i.e., on Value s. That means num+  is going to get two addresses as arguments, and it needs to look up the corresponding numbers in memory, and then produce the resulting number:

(define (num+ la ra)

  (numV (+ (read-num la) (read-num ra))))

旁注：如果你心存疑问：是的，我们稍微取了点巧。我们使用 Racket 的数字，而没有处理更底层的表示。因为那不是我们想说明的重点，就给自己这点余地吧。 Aside: In case you’re wondering: yes, we’re cheating a tiny bit. We’re using Racket numbers rather than dealing with even lower-level representations. We’ll give ourselves this little bit of leeway since this is not the point we’re trying to illustrate.

类似地，我们也能定义拼接： Analogously, we can define concatenation as well:

(define (str++ la ra)

  (strV (string-append (read-str la) (read-str ra))))

旁注：没错，我们又取巧了，而且取巧不少。如果没这么懒，我们就会编写一个遍历 MEMORY 的大循环，把第一个和第二个字符串中的所有值显式复制到新的第三个字符串中。但我们就是懒。 Aside: Yes, we’re cheating again, and quite a bit. If we were less lazy, we’d write a big loop over MEMORY  that copies all the values from the first and second strings into a new, third string, explicitly. But we’re lazy.

最后，还必须更新测试。因为 calc 现在返回地址，所以所有答案看起来都不正确。我们必须改为取得这些地址处对应的数字或字符串。这样做之后，calc 就通过测试了： Finally, we have to update our tests as well. Because calc  now returns addresses , all our answers appear to be incorrect. Instead, we have to obtain the corresponding numbers or strings at those addresses. Once we do so, calc  passes the tests:

(test (read-num (calc (plus (num 1) (num 2)))) 3)

(test (read-num (calc (plus (num 1) (plus (num 2) (num 3))))) 6)

(test (read-str (calc (cat (str "hel") (str "lo")))) "hello")

(test (read-str (calc (cat (cat (str "hel") (str "l")) (str "o")))) "hello")

不过……真的如此吗？这两个测试并未通过： Except…does it? These two tests do not pass:

(test/exn (calc (cat (num 1) (str "hello"))) "left")

(test/exn (calc (plus (num 1) (str "hello"))) "right")

事实上，它们怎么可能通过呢？上面所有代码中，已经没有任何报错了！相反，当运行 In fact, how can  they? In all the above code, there are no errors left! Rather, when we run

(calc (cat (num 1) (str "hello")))

我们会得到一个地址（可能是 69；取决于之前运行过什么，从而取决于 MEMORY 里有什么）。事实上，我们可以自行决定如何看待它：当作数字？还是字符串？ we get an address back (maybe 69 ; it depends on what you ran earlier and hence what is in MEMORY ). In fact, we can decide how we want to treat this: As a number? As a string?

> (read-num 69)

- Number

6

> (read-str 69)

- String

"\u0005hello"

但一个东西怎么能既是数字又是字符串？其实，情况比这还要混乱一点：上面的 69 只是一个内存地址，我们可以按照任何想要的方式，从那里读取任何想要的东西（也就是说，该地址的内容由读取它的函数来解释），结果可能是垃圾。事情还可能更糟： But how can something be both a number and a string? Well, actually, the situation is a bit more confusing than that: 69  above is just an address in memory from which we can read off whatever we want however we want it  (i.e., the content of that address is interpreted  by the function that reads from it), which can result in garbage. It can get even worse:

> (read-num (calc (plus (num 1) (str "hello"))))

- Number

6

> (read-str (calc (plus (num 1) (str "hello"))))

- String

. . integer->char: contract violation

  expected: valid-unicode-scalar-value?

  given: -1

也就是说，我们试图读取“内存末尾之外”的位置。初始值碰巧是 -1，纯粹是运气；当我们试图把 -1 转为字符时，它触发了错误，因为 Racket 的原语是安全的，从而使程序停止。如果 integer->char 没有安全检查，我们得到的就会是某个乱码字符串。 That is, we’ve tried to read “off the end of memory”. It was dumb luck that we had a -1  as the initial value; the -1  triggered an error when we tried to convert it to a character because Racket’s primitives are safe , which halted the program. If integer->char  did not have a safety check, we would have gotten some garbled string instead.

简言之，我们创建了一门不安全的语言。数据没有完整性。任何值都可以被当作任何种类的数据。简言之，这就是 C 的内存模型，而它在现代编程中大体上已被证明是一场灾难，这也是 SMoL 语言演化出来的原因。 In short, what we have created is an unsafe  language. Data have no integrity. Any value can be treated as any kind of datum. This, in short, is the memory model of C, and it’s largely proven to be a disaster for modern programming, which is why SMoL languages evolved.

恢复安全性 Recovering Safety

幸运的是，让语言重新变得安全并不需要太多工作。我们刚写下的内容就包含了关键：每个值都需要记录自己是哪一种值。使用该值时，都需要检查它是不是正确种类的值。这种信息叫作标签；它占用固定大小的空间，表示关于后续 p 的元数据。所有后续值都按照标签来解释。 Fortunately, it does not take too much work to make the language safe again. What we’ve just written holds the key: every value needs to record what kind of value it is. And any use of that value needs to check that it’s the right kind of value. This information is called a tag ; it takes a fixed amount of space, and represents metadata  about the subsequent p. All subsequent values are interpreted in accordance with the tag.

对于这两种值，我们需要两个标签。就用 We need two tags for the two kinds of values. Let’s use

(define NUMBER-TAG 1337)

(define STRING-TAG 5712)

重要的是，两个标签必须不同，这样才没有歧义。不过，无须担心标签本身会与其他数据（例如数字）混淆，因为标签永远不会被直接当作程序数据来处理（当然，除非实现中有缺陷，意外这么做了……所以语言实现需要充分测试）。 It’s important that the two tags be different, so they are unambiguous. However, we don’t need to worry about the tags themselves being confused with other data (e.g., numbers), because the tags will never be processed directly as program data (unless, of course, there is a bug in our implementation that accidentally does so…which is why language implementations need to be tested extensively).

现在，分配数字时，我们先在第一个地址写入标签，后面再放实际数值： Now, when we allocate a number, we write its tag  into the first address, followed by the actual numeric value:

(define (store-num n)

  (let ([a0 (write-and-bump NUMBER-TAG)])

    (begin

      (write-and-bump n)

      a0)) )

而尝试读取数字时，我们先检查它确实是数字，然后才取得实际数值： And when we try to read a number, we first  check that it really is  a number, and only then obtain the actual numeric value:

(define (safe-read-num a)

  (if (= (vector-ref MEMORY a) NUMBER-TAG)

      (vector-ref MEMORY (add1 a ) )

      (error 'number (number->string a))) )

字符串与此类似： Strings are analogous:

(define (store-str s)

  (let ([a0 (write-and-bump STRING-TAG )])

    (begin

      (write-and-bump (string-length s))

      (map write-and-bump

           (map char->integer (string->list s)))

      a0)))

(define (safe-read-str a)

  (if (= (vector-ref MEMORY a) STRING-TAG)

      (letrec ([loop

                (lambda (count a)

                  (if (zero? count)

                      empty

                      (cons (vector-ref MEMORY a)

                            (loop (sub1 count) (add1 a)))))])

        (list->string

         (map integer->char

              (loop (vector-ref MEMORY (add1 a ) ) (+ a 2 )))))

      (error 'string (number->string a))) )

因此，现在从全新的内存开始，运行 So now, starting from a fresh memory, running

(store-str "hello")

仍会产生 0，但 MEMORY 的内容有些不同： still produces 0 , but the content of MEMORY  looks a bit different:

'#( 5712

   5

   104

   101

   108

   108

   111

   -1

   -1

   -1

   …)

也就是说，在地址 0 处，我们首先遇到字符串的标签。然后才是字符串长度，后面跟着其内容。注意，现在把长度存到前面更有道理了：前两个位置包含标签和长度，两者都是帮助我们解释后续内容的元数据，第二个（长度）进一步细化了第一个（标签）。 That is, at address 0  we first encounter the tag for strings. Only then do we get the string’s length, followed by its contents. Observe that now, storing the length up front makes even more sense: the first two locations contain the tag and the length, both of which are metadata  that help us interpret what comes later, with the second (the length) refining  the first (the tag).

经过这个修改，解释器保持不变，辅助函数实际上也一样，只是改用我们选定的新名称： With this change, the interpreter stays unchanged, and effectively so do the helpers, other than using the new names we’ve chosen:

(define (num+ la ra)

  (store-num (+ ( safe- read-num la) ( safe- read-num ra))))

(define (str++ la ra)

  (store-str (string-append ( safe- read-str la) ( safe- read-str ra))))

所有“好”测试依然通过，但重要的是，“坏”测试现在会按预期失败： All our “good” tests still pass, but importantly, our “bad” tests now fail as desired:

(test/exn (calc (cat (num 1) (str "hello"))) "string")

(test/exn (calc (plus (num 1) (str "hello"))) "number")

练习：你可能注意到，上面错误消息的字符串略有变化。为什么？ Exercise: You may notice the error message strings above have changed slightly. Why?

安全性的代价是什么？ What Price Safety?

不过，与不安全的求值器相比，安全求值器是有代价的。在运行时间方面，现在显然要支付安全检查的开销。在空间方面，要支付标签的开销。因此，我们不得不接受更差的空间和时间表现。 Our safe evaluator has, however, come at a price relative to the unsafe evaluator. In terms of running time , we are now clearly paying for the overhead of safety checks. In terms of space , we are paying for the tags. Thus, we have had to get worse space and  time.

尽管如此，不安全语言的代价如此高昂——例如安全漏洞——而安全性的成本往往如此低廉，以至于程序员乐于支付这个代价（或者付出了也并未特别注意到）。 Nevertheless, the price of unsafe languages is so high—e.g., in the form of security problems—and the cost of safety is often so low, that programmers gladly pay this price (or do so without even particularly noticing it).

不过，如果完全不用付出这个代价就好了。而确实有办法做到：类型。 Still, it would be nice if we didn’t have to pay the price at all. And there is a way to accomplish that: types .

看看那些“坏”程序。它们都是类型检查器可以静态拒绝的程序。如果能拒绝所有这类程序，那么——既然不会剩下任何“坏”程序——就可以在不安全的求值器上运行程序，而不必担心不良后果。实际上，这正是 Java 和 OCaml 等大多数有类型语言的做法。因此，我们发现类型的另一个用途：提高程序性能。不过，这需要谨慎。 Look at our “bad” programs. These are programs that can statically  be rejected by a type-checker. If we could reject all such programs, then—since no “bad” programs would be left—we can then run the program on the unsafe  evaluator without worrying about negative consequences. This, in effect, is what most typed languages, like Java and OCaml, do. Thus we find another use for types: to improve program performance. But this requires care.

练习：在计算机科学中，我们通常会谈论空间—时间权衡。然而，在这里，我们似乎同时改善了空间和时间（即减少了二者的使用）！这怎么可能？ Exercise:  Usually, in computer science, we talk about a space-time tradeoff . Yet here we seem to have a situation where we’ve improved (i.e., reduced the use of) both the space and  the time! How is that possible?

健全性 Soundness

顾名思义，在不安全的求值器上运行程序是危险的。因此，只有确信不会出任何问题时，才应该这么做。这意味着我们的类型系统必须附带一种保证。 Running on an unsafe evaluator is, as the name suggests, dangerous. Therefore, we should only do it if we can be sure that nothing can go wrong. That means that our type system needs to come with a guarantee .

这种保证通常表述如下。假设有 The way this guarantee is usually formulated is as follows. Suppose we have

e : t

并假设对它求值后发现 and suppose we evaluate it and find that

e -> v

后者——它的值——才是事实依据。类型检查器的职责是确保它的结论与求值器的产物匹配。也就是说，理想情况下，我们希望 The latter—its value—is the ground truth. The type checker’s job is to make sure it matches what the evaluator produces. That is, we would ideally like that

e : t 当且仅当 e -> v 且 v : t e : t  if and only if e -> v  and v : t

这表示类型检查器的职责是完美对应求值器：程序结果值的类型，与类型检查器所说的类型完全相同。 This says that the type checker's job is to perfectly mirror the evaluator: whatever type the program’s result value has is the same type the type-checker says it has.

不幸的是，对于图灵完备的语言，根据莱斯定理，不可能获得这种完整的保证。我们只能妥协，看看能否至少得到两个方向中的一个。思考后会发现，在有类型的语言中，我们真正关心的只是通过类型检查器的程序（即具有类型的程序）。因此，我们期望 Unfortunately, for a Turing-complete language, this full guarantee is impossible to obtain, because of Rice’s Theorem . Instead, we have to compromise and see if we can get at least one of the two directions. When we think about it, we realize that, in a typed language, we’re only really interested in programs that pass the type-checker (i.e., have a type). Therefore, we expect that

如果 e : t，那么 If e : t  then

如果 e -> v，那么 v : t         if e -> v , then v : t

这表示，类型检查器预测的类型，正是程序实际具有的类型。这意味着我们可以依赖类型检查器的预测。进而意味着可以确信不存在类型违规。于是可知，我们能在不安全的求值器上安全地运行程序！这个性质叫作类型健全性。 This says that whatever type the type-checker predicted is exactly the type that the program has. That means we can rely on the type-checker’s prediction. Which in turn means that we can be sure there are no type violations. Which tells us we can safely run the program atop an unsafe evaluator! This property is called type soundness .

注意，健全性并非理所当然：对于给定的类型检查器和求值器，这是一个必须通过形式化数学证明来确立的性质。证明可能相当复杂。因为程序求值与类型检查的“形状”可能非常不同，前面讨论条件表达式 [ 👉 ] 和函数 [ 👉 ] 时已经见过。而如果没能正确证明它——即宣称它成立，实际上却不成立——就意味着我们放过了一个漏洞。这可能表现为未捕获异常、崩溃、段错误等。此外，聪明的攻击者可能构造程序利用这个漏洞，使系统遭受安全攻击或其他攻击。因此，任何健全性违规都是紧急事件，会引起恐慌。 Note that soundness is not a given: it’s a property that must be formally, mathematically proven  of a given type-checker and evaluator. The proof can be quite complex. This is because the “shape” of program evaluation and that of type-checking can be very different, as we have seen before for conditionals [ 👉 ] and functions [ 👉 ]. And failure to prove it correctly—i.e., claiming it holds when in fact it doesn’t—means we’ve allowed a vulnerability to slip through. This can manifest as uncaught exceptions, crashes, segmentation faults, etc. In addition, a clever attacker can construct a program that exploits the vulnerability, and our system can be subjected to a security or other attack. Thus, any soundness violations are emergencies and result in panic.

通用打印 Generic Printing

带标签表示的一个结果是，从内存提取值时，无须预先知道该用 safe-read-num 还是 safe-read-str；地址处的标签会告诉我们该用哪个。也就是说，可以定义 One of the consequences of our tagged representation is that when extracting a value from memory, we don’t have  to know whether to use safe-read-num  or safe-read-str ; the tag at the address can tell us which to use. That is, we can define

(define (generic-read a)

  (let ([tag (vector-ref MEMORY a)])

    (cond

      [(= tag NUMBER-TAG) (safe-read-num a)]

      [(= tag STRING-TAG) (safe-read-str a)]

      [else (error 'generic-print "invalid tag")])))

遗憾的是，plait 无法为这段代码确定类型，因为两个分支返回不同类型。可以用几种方式解决： Unfortunately, this code can’t be typed by plait because the two branches return different types. We can solve this in a few ways:

  1. 可以用类似 Value 的数据类型来表示内存中的值。不过，这会使内存表示复杂得多，掩盖底层正在发生的事情。因此，我们不探索这条路。 We could use a datatype, similar to Value , to represent the memory values.  However, this creates a much more complicated representation for memory, which masks what is happening at a lower level. Therefore, we don’t explore that avenue.
  2. 可以采用一个变通办法：使用 #lang plait #:untyped，它提供相同的语法语言、特性和运行时行为，但会关闭类型检查器。（有趣的是，我们一直在借助类型检查器约束自己：这样，能存入 MEMORY 的值就只能是数字！因此，最好不要经常使用无类型版本。） We can use a hack: use #lang plait #:untyped , which provides the same syntactic language, features, and run-time behavior, but turns off the type-checker. (Curiously, we were using the type-checker to keep us disciplined: so that the only values we could store in MEMORY  would be numbers! Therefore, it’s good to not use the untyped version often.)
  3. 注意，归根结底，打印器所做的事本质上是打印一个字符串。因此，我们只需在所有情况下都返回字符串：(define (generic-read a) Notice that in the end, what printers do is essentially print a string. Therefore, we just need to return a string in all cases:



    (define (generic-read a)

  (let ([tag (vector-ref MEMORY a)])

    (cond

      [(= tag NUMBER-TAG) (number->string (safe-read-num a))]

      [(= tag STRING-TAG) (safe-read-str a)]

      [else (error 'generic-print "invalid tag")])))

有了这个函数，就可以把测试改写得更妥当： A consequence of having this function is that we can rewrite our tests to be more proper:

(test (generic-read (calc (plus (num 1) (num 2)))) "3")

(test (generic-read (calc (plus (num 1) (plus (num 2) (num 3))))) "6")

(test (generic-read (calc (cat (str "hel") (str "lo")))) "hello")

(test (generic-read (calc (cat (cat (str "hel") (str "l")) (str "o")))) "hello")

这更接近在原始解释器中编写测试的方式；唯一的区别是，这里的求值器产生一个地址作为值，而我们希望以人类可读、可写的形式查看该值，所以使用 generic-read。 This is much closer to how we would write the test in the original interpreter; the only difference here is that the evaluator produces an address as the value, but we would like to inspect the value in a human-readable and -writable form, so we use generic-read .

提醒：如果在之前那些测试之外还要运行这些测试，可能需要增大 MEMORY。 Alert:  If you run these tests in addition to the preceding ones, you may need to enlarge MEMORY .

数字的表示 The Representation of Numbers

在我们的实现中，计算出的每一个数字都会存入 MEMORY；如果某个数字（比如 3）计算了两次，每个实例都会分别存储，从而各自占据空间。不过，这并不是真实实现的空间消耗模型。 In our implementation, every single number we compute is stored in MEMORY  and, if we compute a certain number (say 3 ) twice, each instance will be stored distinctly and hence take up separate space. However, this is not the space consumption model of real implementations.

在大多数现代架构上，值都存放在“字”边界上：根据机器不同，起始地址是 4 或 8 的倍数。（原因涉及计算机体系结构的细节，超出了本书范围。）为便于说明，假设使用一台 32 位机器，按 4 字节对齐。这意味着每个合法内存地址，用二进制表示时，都以 …00 结尾。不过，这两位共有四种合法取值，现在只使用了一种。这就带来了机会。 On most modern architectures, values are stored at “word” boundaries : depending on the machine, starting at addresses that are multiples of 4 or 8. (The reasons for this are due to details of computer architecture that are outside the scope of this book.) For the purposes of illustration, let’s say we have a 32-bit machine, with 4-byte alignment. That means every legal memory address, when viewed in binary, ends in …00. However, there are four legal values for those two bits, only one of which is being used. This creates an opportunity.

因此，一种常见技巧是用 …01 这样的模式作为数字的标签。实际数值本身存放在“地址”剩余的位中（比如 30 位）。这意味着，以 01 结尾的“地址”并不是真正的地址，绝不能拿去查内存；它们实际上只是数字。 A common technique is to therefore use a pattern like …01 to be the tag for numbers. The actual number itself is stored in the remaining (say 30) bits of the “address”. That means, “addresses” that end in 01 are not true addresses, and must not be looked up; they are actually just numbers.

因此，原则上，对一个值（即地址）首先要做的是检查它的第 0 位。如果这一位是 1，就把该值右移 2 位。这样就去掉了 01 标签，留下原来的数字。同样，构造数字时，只要它能放进 30 位，就将它左移两位，再把最后一位置为 1（形成 01 标签）。 Thus, in principle, the first thing to do with a value (that is, an address) is to test its 0’th bit. If this is 1, then shift the value right by 2 places. This drops the 01 tag, leaving the number in place . Similarly, when a number is constructed, provided it fits in 30 bits, it is shifted left by two places, and the last bit is made 1 (resulting in the 01 tag).

这样，每个数字都有标签；但每个数字也都存放在寄存器和栈上，而不是堆上。所有数值相同的数字都有相同的位模式表示（30 位数值后跟 01）。因此，它们在堆上的实例数为零，而且可以在常量时间内准确比较是否相等。 As a consequence, every number has a tag; but every number is also stored in registers and on the stack, not on the heap. All numbers with the same value have the same bit-pattern representation (the 30-bit numeric value followed by 01). Thus, there will be zero  instances of them on the heap, and they can be accurately compared for equality in constant time.

旁注：注意，上述技巧只适用于能放进 30 位的数字（在 64 位机器上则约为 60 位）。更大的数字仍然必须存放在堆上。 Aside:  Notice that the above technique only works for numbers that can fit in 30 bits (or about 60 bits in a 64-bit machine). Larger numbers have to still be stored on the heap.

你或许已经想到，我们还有发挥空间：还剩下 …10 和 …11 两种模式。另一个适合完全放入地址的值是布尔值，所以可以用 …10 模式来表示它。非常短的字符串也可能放进一个字里。诸如此类。在底层设计这些标签时，需要考虑许多架构、指令集和程序方面的因素。 As you might imagine, we have further room to play: we still have the patterns …10 and …11. Another good candidate for fitting entirely in the address is a Boolean, so the pattern …10 could be used for that. Very short strings might fit in a word. And so on. There are many architectural, instruction-set, and program considerations in designing these tags at the low level.

类型推断 Type Inference

无注解的程序与类型 Unannotated Programs and Types

考虑下面这个 plait 程序： Consider the following plait program:

(lambda (x y)

  (if x

      (+ y 1)

      (+ y 2)))

如果把这个程序输入 plait，例如如下所示，就会发生一件非凡的事： If we enter this program into plait, e.g., as follows, something remarkable happens:

> (lambda (x y)

    (if x

        (+ y 1)

        (+ y 2)))

- (Boolean Number -> Number)

#<procedure>

 

作为响应，plait 会确定这个函数的类型，无须我们提供任何注解。相比之下，我们刚编写的类型检查器 [ 👉 ] 要求扩展语法，只为了提供（必需的）类型注解。这告诉我们，plait 底层一定发生了不同的、而且更多的事情。再对比看看另一个例子： In response, plait figures out  the type of this function without  our having to provide any annotations. This is in contrast to the type-checker we just wrote [ 👉 ], which required us to extend the syntax just to provide (required) type annotations. That tells us that something different—and more—must be happening under plait. In contrast, consider another example:

(lambda (x)

    (if x

        (+ x 1)

        (+ x 2)))

它会产生一个错误，指出 x 既出现在要求它是布尔值的位置（if 中），又出现在要求它是数字的位置（两处加法中）。同样，plait 在我们完全没写任何注解的情况下就发现了这一点！ This produces an error, observing that we are using x  both in a position that requires it to be a Boolean (in if ) and a number (in the two additions). Again, plait has figured this out without our having to write any annotations at all!

plait 底层的算法，本质上与 OCaml、Haskell 和另外几门编程语言底层的算法相同。这些语言提供类型推断：自动从程序源代码中确定（推断）类型。现在我们就来看看它如何工作。 The algorithm that sits underneath plait is essentially the same algorithm under OCaml, Haskell, and several other programming languages. These languages provide type inference : figuring out (inferring) types automatically from the program source. Now we’re going to see how this works.

关键思路是，把这个看似非常复杂的问题分成两个相当简单的部分。第一部分，我们（遵循 SImPl）递归访问程序的每个子表达式，生成一组约束，把上面非形式化的做法形式化。第二阶段求解这组约束，所用的过程是你在学校解“联立方程组”的过程的一种推广。解就是每个变量的类型。有了它，就能填上程序员留空的注解。 The key idea is to break this seemingly very complex problem into two rather simple parts. In the first, we recursively visit each sub-expression of the program (following SImPl) and generate a set of constraints  that formally do what we’ve been doing informally above. The second phase solves  this set of constraints, using a process that is a generalization of the process you used for solving “systems of simultaneous equations” in school. The solution is a type  for each variable. That lets us fill in the annotations that the programmer left blank.

生成过程也已经施加了类型约束，因此不再需要对程序进行类型检查；不过，我们仍可以使用这些注解，例如在 IDE 中提供工具提示，在编译器中进行优化，等等。也就是说，有了推断，我们编程时可以像使用没有注解的“脚本式”语言一样，却仍获得类型的大多数好处。（说“大多数”，是因为其中一个好处是文档说明；省略所有注解会使程序更难阅读和理解。因此，推断应该节制使用。） The process of generation will also have applied the type constraints, so there will be no further need to type-check the program; but we can use the annotations, for instance, in an IDE for tool-tips, in a compiler for optimization, etc. That is, with inference, we can program as if we’re in a “scripty” language without annotations, yet achieve most of the benefits of types. (I say “most” because one of the benefits is documentation; leaving off all annotations makes programs harder to read and understand. For that reason, inference should be used sparingly.)

设想解决办法 Imagining a Solution

到目前为止，类型检查器都要求我们为每个函数的参数加注解。但设想有人交给我们一段没有注解的代码；我们还能确定类型吗？例如，考虑： Until now, our type checker has required us to annotate the parameter of every function. But let’s imagine someone handed us a piece of code without annotations; can we figure out the type anyway? For instance, consider:

(+ 1 2)

显然，我们知道它的类型；甚至类型检查器也能在没有任何注解的情况下替我们算出来。但这当然不奇怪：这里根本没有需要注解的变量。现在考虑这个表达式： We clearly know the type of this; even our type-checker can calculate it for us without any annotations. But of course that’s not surprising: there are no variables to annotate. So now consider this expression:

(lambda (x : ___) (+ x 1))

稍加查看，就能知道这个函数的类型是 (Num -> Num)。但我们的类型检查器无法算出这一点，因为它会被空缺的注解绊住。那我们是怎么确定的呢？ With a moment’s inspection, we can tell that the function has type (Num -> Num) . But our type-checker couldn’t have calculated that, because it would have tripped on the empty annotation. So how can we  figure it out?

来看看。首先，必须确定 x 的类型。为此，应该寻找 x 的用法。它只用了一次，用在加法中。而加法规则 Well, let’s see. First we have to figure out the type of x . To determine its type, we should look for uses  of x . There is only one, and it’s used in an addition. But the rule for addition

Γ |- e1 : Num     Γ |- e2 : Num

------------------------------

Γ |- (+ e1 e2) : Num

告诉我们，那个位置上的项必须具有类型 Num。我们没有关于 x 的其他信息（这句话稍后就会更清楚）。因此，可以确定它的类型必须是 Num。此外，我们知道加法的结果也是 Num。由此可以得出，这个函数的类型是 (Num -> Num)。 tells us that the term in that position must have type Num . There is no additional information we have about x  (this remark will become clearer in a moment). Therefore, we can determine that its type must be Num . Furthermore, we know that the result of an addition is also a Num . From that, we can conclude that the function has type (Num -> Num) .

唯一的变量名 Unique Variable Names

接下来，我们假设程序中所有变量名都唯一。也就是说，给定的变量名在一个程序中最多只在一个地方被绑定。这极大地简化了下面的叙述，因为我们可以谈论某个变量的类型，并明确知道指的是哪个变量，而不必不断限定所说的是具有那个名字的哪一个变量。 In what follows, we will assume that all variable names in the program are unique. That is, a given variable name is bound in at most one place in a program. This greatly simplifies the presentation below, because we can speak of the type of a variable and know which  variable it refers to, instead of having to constantly qualify which variable of that name we mean.

在具有静态作用域的语言中，这个限制实际上并不会排除任何程序。考虑下面这个产生 7 的程序： This restriction does not actually preclude any programs in a language with static scope. Consider this program, which produces 7 :

(let ([x 3])

  (+ (let ([x 4])

       x)

     x))

完全可以把其中一个 x 一致地重命名为别的名称（嗨，甚至可以使用 DrRacket 界面，让 Racket 替我们重命名），而程序的含义丝毫不变： We can just as well consistently rename  one of the x s to something else (heck, we can even use the DrRacket interface to have Racket do the renaming for us), and leave the program meaning exactly the same:

(let ([x 3])

  (+ (let ([y 4])

       y)

     x))

这个重命名过程叫作 alpha 转换或 alpha 重命名。 This renaming process is called alpha conversion  or alpha renaming .

更多非形式化示例 More Informal Examples

处理好这个重要细节后，回到根据变量在程序中的使用方式来推断或重建其类型的过程。下面是另一个例子，使用一个双参数函数： With that important detail out of the way, let’s return to our process of inferring  or reconstructing  the types of variables from the way they’re used in a program. Here’s another example with a two-parameter function:

(lambda ((x : ___) (y : ___))

  (if x

      (+ y 1)

      (+ y 2)))

同样，不能直接用类型检查器算出它的类型；必须根据函数体重建类型。来试试看。能看出什么？再次参照条件表达式的规则： Once again, we can’t just calculate its type with our type-checker; instead, we must reconstruct the type from the function body. Let’s do that. What can we tell? Let’s again refer to the conditional rule:

Γ |- C : Bool     Γ |- T : U     Γ |- E : U

-----------------------------------------

Γ |- (if C T E) : U

它告诉我们，C 位置上的东西——这里是 x——必须是 Bool。此外，两个分支 (+ y 1) 和 (+ y 2) 必须具有相同类型。这就是从 if 规则中能得知的全部信息！但现在可以（也必须）递归进入子表达式。它们都是加法，而加法规则告诉我们，两个实参都必须是 Num。两处都表明 y 的类型必须是 Num。此外，两处都表明整个加法返回 Num。由此可知，整个表达式必须具有这个类型 This tells us that what’s in the C  position—here, x —must be a Bool . Furthermore, both branches (+ y 1)  and (+ y 2)  must have the same type. That’s all we can learn from the rule for if ! But now we can (and must) recur into the sub-expressions. Each one is an addition, and the addition rule tells us that both arguments must be Num s. Both of these indicate that the type of y  must be Num . Furthermore, both indicate that the overall addition returns a Num . From that we can tell that the entire expression must have the type

(Bool Num -> Num)

通过这个过程，我们可以确定缺失的注解中应该填入什么类型。更微妙的是，注意，执行这个过程实际上已经应用了所有类型规则；因此，如果成功重建了类型注解，就不必再费心用这些注解对程序进行类型检查：它必然能够通过。 By this process, we can figure out what types to put in the missing annotations. More subtly, notice that by running through this process, we have effectively applied all the typing rules; therefore, if we have successfully reconstructed the type annotations, we need not bother type-checking the program with those annotations: it will have to type-check.

现在考虑上述程序的一个小变化： Now let’s consider a slight variation on the above program:

(lambda (x : ___)

  (if x

      (+ x 1)

      (+ x 2)))

来确定从函数体中能得知关于 x 的哪些信息： Now let’s figure out everything we can learn about x  from the function’s body:

  • x 用在 if 的条件位置。因此，它必须具有类型 Bool。 x  is used in the conditional position of an if . Therefore, it must have type Bool .
  • x 用作 + 的参数。因此，它必须具有类型 Num。 x  is used as a parameter to + . Therefore, it must have type Num .
  • x 又一次用作 + 的参数。因此，它必须具有类型 Num。 x  is again used as a parameter to + . Therefore, it must have type Num .

注意，每个结论单独来看都完全没问题。但把它们放到一起（这就是上面“其他信息”的意思），就出现了问题：x 不可能两者都是。也就是说，无法为 x 找到一个统一的类型。无法为 x 找到类型，就意味着程序有类型错误。事实上，也确实不存在一个能让这个程序安全执行的类型可供我们指定。 Notice that each of these conclusions is perfectly fine on its own. However, when we put them together  (which is what we meant by “additional information” above), there’s a problem: x  cannot be both of those. That is, we are unable to find a single type for x . This inability to find a type for x  means that the program has a type error . And indeed, there is  no type we could have given that would have enabled this program to execute safely.

注意一个微妙之处。虽然可以报告程序显然有类型错误，但错误消息必然要模糊得多。以前，x 有类型注解时，我们可以准确指出错误发生的位置。现在只能说程序的类型不一致，却不能归咎于某个位置，否则就可能误导程序员。相反，必须报告所有这些位置，让程序员根据自己未明示的意图（未以类型注解的形式表达）来决定错误在哪里。 Observe something subtle. While we can report that the program clearly has a type error, our error message must necessarily be much more ambiguous. Previously, when we had a type annotation on x , we could pinpoint where the error occurred. Now, all we can say is that the program is not type- consistent , but cannot blame one spot or the other without potentially misleading the programmer. Instead, we must report all these locations and let the programmer decide where the error is based on their unstated intent  (in the form of a type annotation).

算法细节 Algorithmic Details

这个算法称为 Hindley-Milner 推断，其细节非常迷人，本书 PLAI 的第一版和第二版都作了详细介绍（第一版第 30 章，第二版第 15.3.2 节）。约束生成和约束求解的若干完整示例，请参阅第一版。第一版的介绍更侧重算法，第二版则提供代码（比较两者可能有所帮助）。第二版的文字与第一版不同，因此不同读者可能各有所好。 The details of this algorithm—called Hindley-Milner inference —are fascinating, and worked out in detail in both the first and second editions of this book, PLAI  (Chapter 30 in the first edition and Chapter 15.3.2 in the second edition). For several worked examples of both constraint generation and constraint solving, refer to the first edition. The first edition has a more algorithmic presentation, while the second provides code (it may be useful to compare the two). The prose in the second is different from that in the first, so different readers may prefer one over the other.

代数数据类型 Algebraic Datatypes

到目前为止，我们已经写了许多 define-type 定义，例如表达式的定义。如今，越来越多新编程语言中都有这种机制，现在我们将更详细地研究它。 We have written numerous define-type  definitions so far, e.g., for expressions. Now we will study this mechanism, which is increasingly found in many new programming languages, in more detail.

为简单起见，考虑下面这个 plait 数据定义，表示由数字组成的二叉树： To simplify things, consider a simple plait data definition of a binary tree of numbers:

(define-type BT

  [mt]

  [node (v : Number) (l : BT) (r : BT)])

这里的 define-type 构造做了三件不同的事，值得把它们拆开来看： The define-type  construct here is doing three different things, and it’s worth teasing them apart:

  1. 为一个新类型命名为 BT。 Giving a name  to a new type, BT .
  2. 允许通过多个情况或变体（mt 和 node）定义该类型。 Allowing the type to be defined by multiple cases or variants  ( mt  and node ).
  3. 允许递归定义（BT 引用 BT）。 Permitting a recursive  definition ( BT  references BT ).

值得问一问，这些功能真的必须捆绑在一起吗，还是可以分别处理？虽然确实能拆开，但它们往往最终要协同工作，尤其是在相当常见的递归定义中。递归定义需要一个名称来建立递归；因此，第三项特性需要第一项。此外，递归定义通常需要一个非递归情况来“触底”；这就需要不止一个变体，用到第二项特性。因此，将这三者结合起来很有道理。 It’s worth asking whether all these pieces of functionality really have to be bundled together, or whether they can be handled separately. While they can indeed be separated, they often end up working in concert, especially when it comes to recursive definitions, which are quite common. A recursive definition needs a name for creating the recursion; therefore, the third feature requires the first. Furthermore, a recursive definition often needs a non-recursive case to “bottom out”; this requires there to be more than one variant, using the second feature. Putting the three together, therefore, makes a lot of sense.

这种构造叫作代数数据类型，有时也称“积之和”。这是因为各个变体被解读为“或”：BT 是 mt 或 node。每个变体又是其字段的“且”：node 有 v 且有 l 且有 r。在布尔代数中，“或”类似于和，“且”类似于积。 This construct is called an algebraic datatype , sometimes also known as a “sum of products”. That is because the variants are read as an “or”: a BT  is an mt   or  a node . Each variant is an “and” of its fields: a node has a v   and  an l   and  an r . In Boolean algebra, “or” is analogous to a sum and “and” is analogous to a product.

有时也会看到它被称为带标签联合。“联合”一词是因为，从概念上，可以把 BT 看作 mt 与 node 的联合。标签就是构造器。等我们将它与“不带标签”的联合类型 [ 👉 ] 比较后，这个术语就更容易理解了。 Sometimes, you will also see this referred to as a tagged union . The word “union” is because we can conceptually think of a BT  as a union of mt s and node s. The tag is the constructor. This term makes more sense once we compare it against “untagged” union types [ 👉 ].

生成的绑定 Generated Bindings

现在的问题是，如何为使用这种定义的代码确定类型？首先，盘点一下它可能创建的所有定义。它至少创建两个构造器： Now the question is, how do we type code that uses such a definition? First, let’s take an inventory of all the definitions that this might create. It at least creates two constructors :

(mt : ( -> BT))

(node : (Number BT BT -> BT))

我们一直从空环境开始解释和类型检查，但没有理由必须这样，实践中也并非如此：初始环境可以包含各种预定义值及其类型。因此，可以把上面的 define-type 想成将上述两个定义加入初始类型环境，从而使 mt 和 node 的使用能够接受类型检查。 We have been starting our interpretation and type-checking with the empty environment, but there is no reason we need to, nor do we do so in practice: the primordial environment can contain all kinds of pre-defined values and their types. Thus, we can imagine the define-type  above adding the above two definitions to the initial type environment, enabling uses of mt  and node  to be type-checked.

这部分在各种语言中都很常见。但较少见的是，在 plait 中还能得到另外两组函数：用于区分变体的谓词： This much is standard across various languages. But less commonly, in plait you get two more families of functions: predicates  for distinguishing between the variants:

(mt? : (BT -> Boolean))

(node? : (BT -> Boolean))

以及用于从字段中取出值的访问器： and accessors  for getting the values out of fields:

(node-v : (BT -> Number))

(node-l : (BT -> BT))

(node-r : (BT -> BT))

静态类型安全 Static Type Safety

这些访问器的类型应该让我们感到不安。它们似乎不加区分地尝试取出字段值，不管那个变体是否具有这些字段。例如，可以编写下面这个程序，并通过类型检查，这很不错： We should be troubled by the types of these accessors. They seem to indiscriminately try to pull out field values, whether the variant has them or not . For instance, we can write and type-check this program, which is appealing:

(size-correct : (BT -> Number))

(define (size-correct (t : BT))

  (if (mt? t)

      0

      (+ 1 (+ (size-correct (node-l t)) (size-correct (node-r t))))))

(test (size-correct (mt)) 0)

不过，下面这个程序也同样能通过类型检查： However, we can just as well type-check this  program:

(define (size-wrong (t : BT))

  (+ 1 (+ (size-wrong (node-l t)) (size-wrong (node-r t)))))

它本不该通过类型检查，因为其中有明显的类型错误。size-wrong 的类型是 This should not type-check because it has a clear type-error. The type of size-wrong  is

(size-wrong : (BT -> Number))

因此，写下面这样的代码在类型上完全正确： so it is perfectly type-correct to write:

(size-wrong (mt))

但运行它当然会产生运行时错误，而这正是我们原本希望类型检查器能够捕获的那类错误。 But running this, of course, results in a run-time error, the very kind of error we might have hoped the type-checker would catch.

模式匹配与类型检查 Pattern-Matching and Type-Checking

在 OCaml 和 Haskell 等语言中，这种错误不会自然出现。它们不会暴露所有这些谓词和访问器，而是使用模式匹配来解构代数数据类型的实例。因此，计算大小的代码会写成（-pm 表示“pattern matching”，即模式匹配）： This kind of error cannot occur naturally in languages like OCaml and Haskell. Instead of exposing all these predicates and accessors, instances of an algebraic datatype are deconstructed using pattern-matching. Thus, the size computation would be written as ( -pm  stands for “pattern matching”):

(size-pm : (BT -> Number))

(define (size-pm t)

  (type-case BT t

    [(mt) 0]

    [(node v l r) (+ 1 (+ (size-pm l) (size-pm r)))]))

这可能看起来只是一种便利——它确实让代码紧凑得多，或许也更易读——但它还做了更多事情。模式匹配器实际上被融入了程序的类型检查方式中。也就是说，上面的代数数据类型定义实际上向类型检查器加入了如下类型规则： This might seem like a convenience—it certainly makes the code much more compact and perhaps also much more readable—but it’s also doing something more. The pattern-matcher is effectively baked into the way programs are type-checked. That is, the above algebraic datatype definition effectively adds the following typing rule to the type checker:

Γ |- e : BT

Γ   |- e1 : T

Γ [V <- Number, L <- BT, R <- BT]   |- e2 : T

-----------------------------------------

Γ   |- (type-case BT e

       [(mt) e1]

       [(node V L R) e2]) : T

第一个前提很清楚：用 BT 的模式对表达式 e 进行模式匹配之前，必须确认它求值为 BT。第二个前提在与结论相同的环境中对 e1 进行类型检查，因为 mt 变体不会增加任何局部绑定。按照我们处理条件表达式的方式，这个表达式的类型必须与另一个分支的类型相同。最后，要对 e2 进行类型检查，必须用绑定的变量扩展结论中的类型环境；这些变量的类型可以直接从数据定义中读出来。简言之，上述类型规则可以通过脱糖自动定义。 The first antecedent is clear: we have to confirm that the expression e  evaluates to a BT  before we pattern-match BT  patterns against it. The second type-checks e1  in the same  environment as in the consequent because the mt  variant does not add any local bindings. The type of this expression needs to be the same  as the type from the other branch, due to how we’re handling conditionals. Finally, to type-check e2 , we have to extend  the consequent’s type environment with the bound variables; their types we can read off directly from the data definition . In short, the above typing rule can be defined automatically by desugaring.

旁注：注意，这里也存在假设—保证关系：我们在假设注解类型成立的环境中对 e2 进行类型检查；node 构造器保证了这一点。 Aside:  Notice that there is also an assume-guarantee here: we type-check e2  in an environment that assumes  the annotated types; this is guaranteed  by the node  constructor.

尤其要注意，我们做不了什么！这里没有 node-v 之类棘手的选择器，也就不必为它们想出某种类型。说它们接受 BT，就不得不允许它们在静态时接受任何种类的 BT，从而导致运行时问题。这里没有选择器：模式匹配意味着，只能在代数数据类型定义允许的变体中写模式变量，而变量会自动获得正确类型。因此，模式匹配在静态安全地处理类型方面起着关键作用。 In particular, observe what we couldn’t  do! We didn’t have awkward selectors, like node-v , for which we had to come up with some type. By saying they consumed a BT , we had to let them statically consume any kind of BT , which caused a problem at run-time. Here, there is no selector : pattern-matching means we can only write pattern-variables in variants where the algebraic datatype definition permits it, and the variables automatically gets the right type. Thus, pattern-matching plays a crucial role in the statically safe  handling of types.

代数数据类型与空间 Algebraic Datatypes and Space

之前我们看到，类型能够同时节省时间和空间。对于代数数据类型，需要更细致地区分情况。 Earlier, we’ve seen that types can save us both time and space. We have to be a little more nuanced when it comes to algebraic datatypes.

代数数据类型引入的新类型仍然享有空间节省。因为类型检查器能区分 BT 与所有其他类型，运行时就无须记录一个值是 BT：它不需要类型标签。不过，仍然需要区分不同变体：函数 size-pm 实际上脱糖为（-ds 表示“desugared”，即已脱糖）： The new type introduced by an algebraic datatype still enjoys the space saving. Because the type checker can tell a BT  apart from every other type, at run-time we don’t need to record that a value is a BT : it doesn’t need a type-tag. However, we still need to tell apart the different variants : the function size-pm  effectively desugars into ( -ds  stands for “desugared”):

(define (size-pm-ds (t : BT))

  (cond

    [(mt? t) 0]

    [(node? t)

     (let ([v (node-v t)]

           [l (node-l t)]

           [r (node-r t)])

       (+ 1 (+ (size-pm-ds l) (size-pm-ds r))))]))

（我们引入 let 来绑定模式引入的名称。）这说明，运行时有一些条件检查，需要知道本次迭代中绑定到 t 的是哪种 BT。因此，只需要足以区分各变体的标签即可。实践中，这意味着所需位数为变体数量的对数；由于这个数量通常很小，这些信息往往能挤进数据表示的其他部分。 (We’ve introduced the let  to bind the names introduced by the pattern.) What this shows is that at run-time, there are conditional checks that need to know what kind of BT  is bound to t  on this iteration. Therefore, we need just enough tagging to tell the variants apart. In practice, this means we need as many bits as the logarithm of the number of variants; since this number is usually small, this information can often be squeezed into other parts of the data representation.

联合类型与后加的类型 Union Types and Retrofitted Types

Typed Racket 是后加类型系统的一个实例：为原本没有类型的语言加入类型系统。没有静态类型系统的原始语言通常称为动态语言。现在已有许多后加类型系统，例如 JavaScript 的 TypeScript，以及 Python 的 Static Python。有些语言甚至有多个后加类型系统：例如 TypeScript 和 Flow 都为 JavaScript 加入类型。 Typed Racket is an instance of a retrofitted  type system: adding a type system to a language that did not previously have types. The original language, which does not have a static type system, is usually called dynamic . There are now numerous retrofitted type systems: e.g., TypeScript for JavaScript and Static Python for Python. There are even multiple retrofitted type systems for some languages: e.g., both TypeScript and Flow add types to JavaScript.

后加类型系统的目标，是把运行时错误转变为静态类型错误。由于停机问题，不可能精确地把每一个运行时错误都变成静态错误，因此类型系统设计者必须决定哪些错误更重要。此外，程序员已经用许多动态语言编写了大量代码，所以要求程序员大幅重写代码的改动不会被采纳。相反，类型系统设计者应尽可能兼容符合语言惯用写法的类型安全程序。 The goal of a retrofitted type system is to turn run-time errors into static type errors. Due to the Halting Problem, we cannot precisely turn every single run-time error into a static one, so the designer of the type system must make some decisions about which errors matter more than others. In addition, programmers have already written considerable code in many dynamic languages, so changes that require programmers to rewrite code significantly would not be adopted. Instead, as much as possible, type system designers need to accommodate idiomatic type-safe programs .

代数数据类型是一个好例子。通常，动态语言往往没有它们，而是提供某种结构定义机制（例如类，或它的轻量变体，如 Python 的 dataclasses）。因此，代数数据类型及其模式匹配所带来的优雅类型处理方式并不适用。强迫动态语言程序员全面转向这种（对于该动态语言而言的）“新”编程风格并不现实，所以类型系统设计者必须找出他们使用的（恰好类型安全的）惯用写法，并设法认可它们。我们将看几个这样的例子。 Algebraic datatypes present a good example. Typically, they have tended to not be found in dynamic languages. Instead, these languages have some kind of structure definition mechanism (such as classes, or lightweight variants thereof, like Python’s dataclasses ). Therefore, the elegant typing that goes with algebraic datatypes and their pattern-matching does not apply. Because it is not practical to force dynamic language programmers to wholesale change to this “new” (to that dynamic language) style of programming, type system designers must find the idioms they use (that happen to be type-safe) and try to bless them. We will look at some examples of this.

Typed Racket 是后加类型语言的一个很好的实际例子：它为 Racket 加入类型，同时尽量保留 Racket 程序的惯用写法。（这与 plait 不同；plait 也是 Racket 的一种有类型形式，但并不十分努力地保留 Racket 的惯用写法。前面看到的代数数据类型访问器 [ 👉 ] 对接受的内容比较宽容，代价是静态安全性。） A good working example of a retrofitted typed language is Typed Racket, which adds types to Racket while trying to preserve idiomatic Racket programs. (This is in contrast to plait, which is also a typed form of Racket but does not  try very hard to preserve Racket idioms. The accessors we saw earlier, for algebraic datatypes [ 👉 ], are forgiving in what they accept, at the cost of static safety.)

给你一个类型！也给你一个类型！再给你一个类型！ You Get a Type! And You Get a Type! And You Get a Type!

回到 [ 👉 ] plait 中那些不具备静态类型安全性的访问器：例如， Let’s return [ 👉 ] to our non-statically-type-safe accessors in plait: e.g.,

(node-v : (BT -> Number))

某种意义上，责怪访问器并不公平：真正的问题在构造器，因为 In a way, it’s not fair to blame the accessor: the fault is really with the constructor, because

(node : (Number BT BT -> BT))

一旦 node 构造器创建出一个 BT，关于它是 node 的信息就丢失了，访问器也无能为力。所以，另一种办法或许是不创建 BT，而是创建一个 node 类型的值。 Once the node  constructor creates a BT , the information about node -ness is lost, and there’s not much that the accessors can do. So perhaps the alternative is to not  create a BT , but instead create a value of the node  type.

那就重新开始。这次使用另一门有类型语言 Typed Racket： So let’s start over. This time, we’ll use a different typed language, Typed Racket:

#lang typed/racket

在 Typed Racket 中，可以创建称为结构的积，它会定义一种新类型： In Typed Racket, we can create products, called structures, which define a new type:

(struct mt ())

这会创建一个构造器，其类型正如我们所期望： This creates a constructor with the type we’d expect:

> mt

- : (-> mt)

#<procedure:mt>

它还会创建一个谓词，不过其类型有些不同；之前的函数只能接受 BT，因为把 mt? 应用于其他类型并没有意义。但现在甚至（还）没有 BT 这个概念，所以 mt? 会接受任何类型的值： It also creates a predicate, whose type is a bit different; previously we had a function that could only take a BT , because it didn’t make sense to apply mt?  to any other type. Now, however, there isn’t even a concept of a BT  (yet), so mt?  will take values of any type:

> mt?

- : (-> Any Boolean : mt)

#<procedure:mt?>

（额外的文字 : mt 告诉我们，什么时候这个布尔值为真；暂时忽略它。） (The additional text, : mt , is telling us when the Boolean is true; ignore this for now.)

现在尝试定义节点。这里遇到了一个问题： Now let’s try to define nodes. Here we run into a problem:

(struct node ([v : Number] [l :

联合类型 Union Types

哎呀——这里该写什么？！还必须引入二叉树这个概念。但已经有两个现成类型：mt 和（正在定义中的）node。因此，需要一种定义二叉树的方式，用一个和把这两个现有类型结合起来。这启发我们提供一种方式，把新类型描述为现有类型的联合： Oops—what do we write here?!? We have to also introduce a notion of a binary tree. But we already have two existing types, mt  and (in progress) node . Therefore, we need a way to define a binary tree that has a sum that combines these two existing types. This suggests that we have a way of describing a new type as a union  of existing types:

(define-type-alias BT (U mt node))

注意，在这种情况下，没有专门的构造器来区分两种 BT。因此，与带标签联合 [ 👉 ] 相比，这叫作无标签联合。 Observe that in this case, there are no special constructors to distinguish between the two kinds of BT. Therefore, this is called an untagged union , in contrast to tagged unions [ 👉 ].

现在可以回过头来完成 node 的定义： Now we can go back and complete our definition of node :

(struct node ([v : Number] [l : BT] [r : BT]))

现在看看 Typed Racket 告诉我们，node 的构造器、谓词和选择器分别具有什么类型： Now let’s look at what Typed Racket tells us are the types of node ’s constructor, predicate, and selectors:

> node

- : (-> Number BT BT node)

> node-v

- : (-> node Number)

> node-l

- : (-> node BT)

> node-r

- : (-> node BT)

利用这些定义，可以创建树：例如， Using these definitions we can create trees: e.g.,

(define t1

  (node 5

        (node 3

              (node 1 (mt) (mt))

              (mt))

        (node 7

              (mt)

              (node 9 (mt) (mt)))))

但现在来尝试编写一个计算其大小的程序： But now let’s try to write a program to compute its size:

(define (size-tr [t : BT]) : Number

  (cond

    [(mt? t) 0]

    [(node? t) (+ 1 (size-tr (node-l t)) (size-tr (node-r t)))]))

这个程序是否应该通过类型检查，完全不明显。考虑表达式 (node-l t)。node-l 的类型要求实参具有 node 类型。但我们只知道 t 的类型是 BT。然而，这个程序却通过了类型检查！ It is not clear at all that this program should type-check. Consider the expression (node-l t) . The type of node-l  expects its argument to be of type node . However, all we know is that t  is of type BT . Yet this program type-checks!

不过，它确实通过类型检查这件事，不应该让我们高兴得太早。我们已经看到 size-wrong 虽然通过类型检查，最终却因一个不希望出现的运行时错误而停止。那么，如果改写出与它对应的这个版本呢？ The fact that this does type-check, however, should not fill us with too much joy. We saw how size-wrong  type-checked, only to halt with an undesired run-time error. So what if we instead write its analog, which is this?

(define (size-tr-wrong [t : BT]) : Number

  (+ 1 (size (node-l t)) (size (node-r t))))

这个程序不能通过类型检查！相反，它给出的类型错误恰好就是我们预期的那种：node-l 和 node-r 都抱怨，期望的是 node，得到的却是 BT。所以，令人惊奇的不是 size-tr-wrong 有类型错误，而是 size-tr 没有！ This program does not  type-check! Instead, it gives us a type error of exactly the sort we would have expected: node-l  and node-r  both complain that they were expecting an node  and were given a BT . So the wonder is not that size-tr-wrong  has a type-error, but rather that size-tr  does not!

要理解它为什么通过类型检查，必须回头看谓词的类型： To understand why it type-checks, we have to go back to the types of the predicates:

> mt?

- : (-> Any Boolean : mt)

> node?

- : (-> Any Boolean : node)

关键在于，: mt 和 : node 是 Typed Racket 的表示方式，说明只有输入分别是 mt 或 node 时，布尔值才会为真。类型检查器会获取这一关键的细化信息。在 cond 子句的右侧，它会将 t 的类型分别收窄为 mt 和 node。因此，对 (node-l t) 进行类型检查时，所在类型环境中 t 的类型是 node，而非 BT。 Critically, the : mt  and : node  are Typed Racket’s way of saying that the Boolean will be true only when the input is an mt  or node , respectively. This crucial refinement  information is picked up by the type-checker. In the right-hand-side of the cond  clauses, it narrows  the type of t  to be mt  and node , respectively. Thus, (node-l t)  is type-checked in a type environment where the type of t  is node  and not BT .

为检验这个推测，可以尝试另一个错误程序： To test this theory, we can try another wrong program:

(define (size-tr-w2 [t : BT]) : Number

  (cond

    [(node? t) 0]

    [(mt? t) (+ 1 (size-tr-w2 (node-l t)) (size-tr-w2 (node-r t)))]))

这里交换了两个谓词。重要的不只是这个版本会产生类型错误；读一读类型错误、理解其原因，也很有启发。它明确指出，程序期望 node（例如在 node-l 中），得到的却是 mt（根据 mt?）。这证实了 Typed Racket 会根据谓词细化各分支中的类型。 Here, we have swapped the predicates. It is not only important that this version produces a type error, it is also instructive to understand why, by reading the type error. This explicitly says that the program expected an node  (for instance, in node-l ) and was given an mt  (based on the mt? ). This confirms that Typed Racket is refining the types in branches based on predicates.

if 拆分 If-Splitting

总之，size-tr 之所以能通过类型检查，是因为类型检查器看到下面这个模式时，会做特殊处理 To summarize, size-tr  type-checks is because the type-checker is doing something special when it sees the pattern

(define (size-tr [t : BT]) : Number

  (cond

    [(mt? t) …]

    [(node? t) …]))

它知道，每个 BT 都通过这个联合与 mt 和 node 相关联。看到谓词时，就会把类型从完整的联合收窄为该谓词所检查的联合分支。因此，在 mt? 分支中，它把 t 的类型从 BT 收窄为 mt；类似地，在 node? 分支中，把 t 的类型收窄为只有 node。这样，例如 node-l 就能确认自己确实在处理 node 值，程序也就具备静态类型安全性。size-tr-wrong 中没有这些谓词，t 的类型得不到收窄，从而出错。在 size-tr-w2 中，交换谓词也会导致错误。再看一个版本： It knows that every BT  is related to mt  and node  through the union. When it sees the predicate, it narrows  the type from the full union to the branch of the union that the predicate has checked. Thus, in the mt?  branch, it narrows the type of t  from BT  to mt ; in the node?  branch, similarly, it narrows the type of t  to just node . Now, node-l , say, gets confirmation that it is indeed processing a node  value, and the program is statically type-safe. In the absence of those predicates, in size-tr-wrong , the type of t  does not get narrowed, resulting in the error. In size-tr-w2 , swapping the predicates also gives an error. Here is one more version:

(define (size-tr-else [t : BT]) : Number

  (cond

    [(mt? t) 0]

    [else (+ 1 (size-tr (node-l t)) (size-tr (node-r t)))]))

这个程序通过与否，两种情况都有可能！碰巧它确实能在 typed/racket 中通过类型检查，因为 typed/racket 足够“聪明”，能确定 BT 只有两种，其中一种已经排除，因此在 else 情况下必然是另一种。但也完全可以设想一个不那么聪明的检查器，必须看到显式的 node? 检查，才能认可第二个子句。 This program could go either way! It just so happens that it does type-check in typed/racket, because typed/racket is “smart” enough to determine that there are only two kinds of BT  and one has been excluded, so in the else  case, it must be the other kind. But one could also imagine a less clever checker that expects to see an explicit test of node?  to be able to bless the second clause.

简言之，无论代数数据类型还是联合类型的方式，都需要类型检查器对语法作某种特殊处理，才能处理变体。前者通过模式匹配来实现。上面的收窄技巧有时称为 if 拆分，因为 if（cond 和其他条件构造都会脱糖为它）“拆分”了联合。有时你还会看到出现位置类型分析（occurrence typing）和流类型分析（flow typing）等术语，用来描述本章思路的变体。 In short, both the algebraic datatype and union type approaches need some special treatment of syntax by the type-checker to handle variants. In the former case it’s through pattern-matching. The narrowing technique above is sometimes called if-splitting , because an if  (which cond  and other conditional constructs desugar to) “splits” the union. You will sometimes also see the terms occurrence typing  and flow typing  to describe variants of the ideas in this chapter.

旁注：这个思路是 Typed Racket 通过研究程序员如何编写 Scheme 和 Racket 程序而发明的。后来证明，它也适用于许多真实世界的后加类型系统。 Aside:  This idea was invented by Typed Racket  by studying how programmers write code in Scheme and Racket programs. It has later proved to be relevant to many real-world retrofitted type systems.

引入联合类型 Introducing Union Types

正如讨论条件表达式求值 [ 👉 ] 时提到的，联合类型可用于表示部分函数。处理它们有几种方式： As we discussed when evaluating conditionals [ 👉 ], union types can be useful to represent partial functions. There are several ways of handling them:

https://dcic-world.org/2025-02-09/partial-domains.html

使用选项类型可以避免临时拼凑类型联合。不过，如果本来就有联合，那么就能为部分函数指定类型：例如，在 Racket 中是 (V U Boolean)，在 Python 中则是 (V U None)，其中 V 是正常的返回类型。因此，可以把 Racket 的 string->number 的类型设为 (Number U Boolean)。 Using an option type avoids the need for ad-hoc type unions. If we have unions anyway, however, then we can give types to partial functions: e.g., (V U Boolean)  in Racket or (V U None)  in Python, respectively, where V  is the normal return type. Thus, Racket’s string->number  can be given the type (Number U Boolean) .

刚才我们看到，利用 if 拆分可以消去联合类型。于是就有了另一种可能：我们也可以引入联合类型！当然，一种方式是像上面那样，为内置函数指定联合类型。但用户程序呢？之前我们拒绝了这样的方案：如果引入联合，就没有办法处理它。现在，只要语言提供了解构联合的办法，就可以安全地引入它们。 What we’ve just seen is that with if-splitting, we can eliminate union types. That then raises the possibility that we can also introduce union types! One way is of course by giving union types to built-in functions, as above. But what about in user programs? Previously we had rejected such a solution: if we introduced a union, we had no way to deal with it. Now we can safely introduce them in languages that have solutions for deconstructing them.

怎样引入联合类型？有趣的是，用的正是消去它们的同一个构造！注意，现在不再需要条件表达式的两个分支返回相同类型： How do we introduce union types? Curiously, using the same construct that eliminates them! Observe that we no longer need both branches of a conditional to return the same type:

Γ |- C : Bool     Γ |- T : V     Γ |- E : W

-----------------------------------------

Γ |- (if C T E) : (U V W)

其中，我们的记法表示“V 和 W 所代表类型的联合”。 where our notation means “the union of the types represented by V  and W ”.

可以有多少个联合？ How Many Unions?
